HMRC also cautioned that figures should be used as a “guide” – as individual level Isa data is provided to it annually by Isa managers, however each year a proportion will enter records incorrectly, or fail to submit.

Isas enable savers to turbo-boost their funds as accounts that are ringfenced from tax.

Will Bryant, director of wealth strategy at Plum, said: “A jump of more than 50% in a single year is really telling.”

He said the Isa millionaires are not people who “suddenly saved” their way to £1 million.

Highlightng the benefits of compound interest boosting pots over time, he added: “It’s the result of years of patient investing, where the growth on your growth starts doing the heavy lifting. That’s the bit people underestimate.

“These figures underline the value of investing and the importance of taking a long-term approach.

“Despite the geopolitical volatility of recent years, global markets powered by the US stock market have continued to climb.”

In April 2027, the annual cash Isa limit will be slashed from £20,000 to £12,000 for savers aged under 65, although the overall annual Isa allowance will remain at £20,000.

The cash Isa allowance for people aged 65 and over will remain at £20,000.

Mr Bryant said the changes “may lead people to use more of their stocks and shares Isa to make full use of their tax-free allowance,” but he added: “Many people simply won’t know what’s changing.”

Figures released by HMRC in September showed around £135.7 billion was subscribed to adult Isas in the tax year 2024-25 – a £32.7 billion annual increase.

The £32.7 billion increase was driven by a rise in cash Isa subscriptions, which grew by 37.5% or £26.1 billion.

Stocks and shares Isa subscriptions saw a 19.7% or £6.1 billion annual increase, and Lifetime Isa subscriptions had a 20.1% or £472 million rise.

Maike Currie, vice president of personal finance at PensionBee, said: “Isas are one of Britain’s great savings success stories.

“Their beauty lies in their simplicity: a straightforward, tax-efficient way for ordinary people to build wealth and take greater control of their financial futures.

“And you don’t need to become an Isa millionaire to benefit.”

Ms Currie said cutting the cash Isa allowance and introducing additional restrictions “risks making a simple product unnecessarily complicated, potentially undermining confidence at precisely the time we need more people saving and investing”.

News.title: Nasa’s Perseverance rover breaks off-world record on Mars
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nasa's Perseverance rover has broken a record on Mars.

The car-sized, six-wheeled rover has now driven farther than any other vehicle on the surface of another world, logging 28.1 miles (45.2 km) since arriving on Mars in 2021, the US space agency said on Tuesday.

Perseverance reached the milestone 5.5 years into its mission to explore whether conditions conducive to microbial life ever existed on Earth's neighbour. In doing so, it is visiting some of the most ancient terrain ever encountered in the solar system.

"Perseverance's engineering hardware and instruments are in excellent shape with all redundant systems still available," said Steven Lee of Nasa's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California and project manager for Nasa's two Mars rovers, Perseverance and Curiosity.

"A recent assessment of all systems concluded that they are capable of operating well into the 2030s, likely beyond.”

Perseverance surpassed the previous record of 28.06 miles (45 km) driven on the Martian surface by Nasa's Opportunity rover from 2004 to 2018. Both also exceeded the driving distances of any lunar rover.

open image in gallery Nasa's Perseverance Mars rover taking a selfie ( Nasa )

Traversing Jezero Crater

Perseverance, with its suite of scientific instruments, has focused on the Jezero Crater, a region in the northern hemisphere of Mars believed to have been flooded with water and home to a lake basin billions of years ago.

The rover set the milestone in a journey toward an area called Idubi, through the region off the crater's western rim nicknamed Lac de Charmes.

Its companion rover, Curiosity, rolls along in the Gale Crater near the Martian equator.

Perseverance is showing no signs of slowing down, Lee added.

open image in gallery Image from Nasa's Perseverance Rover reveals sandstone at the base of Jezero Crater ( Nasa/JPL-Caltech )

Its mobility system mechanisms are being tested to show it can drive 100 km (62 miles) or more, he said, with the hardware to be tested to the equivalent of 150 km to 300 km (93 miles to 186 miles) in the effort.

Nasa attributed a major role in Perseverance's success to its self-driving capability, an autonomous navigation system called AutoNav. Lee said 90 per cent of its drives are done autonomously, with no human intervention.

"Perseverance takes stereo images of the terrain ahead, generates a 3D software map, and selects the safest path towards a drive goal," he said.

Another key component is the Vision Compute Element, a fast co-processor computer that allows the rover to process images and run its self-driving software very quickly, almost continuously during drives, Lee added.

That contrasts with previous rovers, which needed to pause to "think" before each drive segment, he said.

"Perseverance builds on the 29-year legacy of our past Mars rovers — Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity — each incorporating prior lessons and improving our ability to drive on another world," Lee said.

Potential biosignature

Lee said the rover's biggest achievement was almost certainly its discovery, unveiled last year, of a potential biosignature, or possible sign of ancient microbial life.

This was found in reddish rock believed to have formed 3.2 billion to 3.8 billion years ago in a river channel feeding the lake that once filled Jezero Crater.

The Lac de Charmes terrain, Lee said, may yield clues to early planetary geological processes, such as the effects of large meteorite impacts. Jezero Crater was formed by such an impact early in Martian history.

Lee cited orbital evidence that some areas of the rim were once hydrothermal systems with warm or hot groundwater.

"These areas may once have provided a warm, watery subsurface environment conducive to life," he added. "Indeed, some palaeontologists hypothesise that life on Earth began in such environments."

The rover's original mission envisaged just 12.4 miles (20 km) of driving. Nasa recently approved an extension of its mission to explore the crater rim until roughly the end of 2028.

The rover's plutonium-based power system is performing as expected, Lee said, adding it has "many years of useful energy still available."

News.title: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle
News.content:
You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

News.title: AI cuts diagnosis for eye disease from 23 days to just 30 seconds
News.content:
Patients whose eye scans were read by an AI programme got results in 30 seconds, compared to facing an average waiting time of 23 days for results from a doctor, a study in Tanzania has shown.

Millions of people around the world have diabetic retinopathy, a condition where high blood sugar levels damage the tiny blood vessels in the retina.

It can lead to irreversible blindness if left untreated. Around a third of the 23 million people with diabetes in Africa have the complication.

In its early stages, diabetic retinopathy can have no symptoms, and the World Health Organization recommends that people living with diabetes undergo regular screening to check their eye health, so that they can be treated if necessary.

For the new study, published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers randomly assigned over 2,000 patients with diabetes visiting clinics in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions to either receive usual screening care, or to have a new type of AI-assisted screening.

Two fifths of the participants had changes in their eyes that needed referral to specialist care. In the half screened using AI, 36 per cent attended the central ophthalmology clinic within eight weeks, compared to 18 per cent in the standard care group.

Most of the people working in the regions where the study was based are farmers, said Dr Jestus Rwiza of the Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, co-author on the paper. “They depend on vision.”

The economic effects of blindness are felt by the whole family, he said, recalling how the daughter of one patient “had to stop schooling to help the mother”.

News.title: WHO probes ‘unanswered questions’ over Russian plague worker
News.content:
The World Health Organization has said it still does not have enough information to rule out a lab accident after the death of a worker in a Russian plague lab.

Last week reports emerged that Darya Shipilova, a lab worker in Irkutsk, Siberia, had died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube containing samples of the pathogen Yersinia pestis, which causes the disease.

Some 200 people were quarantined and there were reports of a further case. Shipilova was working at the Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk.

Russian authorities have insisted that there was no lab accident and Shipilova’s mother, Svetlana, has also disputed that her daughter dropped a test tube.

“It’s impossible to break a test tube like that,” she said. “Even if you fling it at the wall. Only an amateur could say something like that,” she said.

News.title: El Nino, hunger and fuel threaten ‘perfect storm’, says UN
News.content:
A triple shock of rising energy prices, spiralling borrowing costs and a turbocharged El Niño could push “tens if not hundreds of millions of people” into poverty, the UN has warned.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) said the three “compounding crises” are hitting developing economies especially hard, with governments running out of resources to shield people from the fallout, in a new report.

“We are witnessing a perfect storm that could throw tens if not hundreds of millions of people back into poverty,” said Alexander De Croo, the UNDP administrator, warning that surging oil and food prices mean families across the world have “no safety margin”.

“Governments of developing countries are left with impossible choices: cut support to their poorest citizens or risk their entire development agenda,” he added.

The report was published ahead of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund’s annual meetings, which kicked off in Bangkok on Monday. Debt pressures, energy prices and geopolitical tensions are high on the agenda.

But UNDP stressed that the meetings were taking place as three shocks converge, and the crisis morphs from a regional to a global one that’s affecting roughly 100 countries.

Seven months ago, when the war in Iran broke out, the UN agency warned that the conflict had triggered the “most severe oil supply shock in history”. That continues today – after a brief respite, oil prices have been pushed back beyond $100 a barrel, as hostilities have resumed in the Middle East.

But two more threats now “challenge the capacity of developing countries to manage the energy shock”, meaning developing economies “will have trouble funding their policy responses in the months ahead”.

News.title: Max Verstappen is back and Mercedes are already worried
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli, third: “It was a very tough race out there but really happy with a podium at the end, I managed to take advantage of the fight between Lewis and Lando. To take P3 is a great result from the team, very happy with that.”

He is told that he can clinch the title at the next race:

“Can I, really? Let’s not worry about that. Let’s try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job.”

Charles Leclerc, second: “We were quite strong at the beginning of the race and then we started degrading at the end of the first stint. I pushed a lot at the beginning of the last stint and then degraded a bit more than the others. I gave it all and I don’t regret anything.

“I don’t think there’s anything more we could do but be a bit more aggressive at the start. It’s true that we brought some small new parts to the car which maybe helped us to do a little step forward but it’s enough. Today I think we had a good pace overall.”

Max Verstappen, winner: “It’s taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. Very happy to win here. You always try to do your best and luckily [the start] it was just good enough.

“I think the last few races have been really positive for us. It’s great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try to deliver even more results... hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”

News.title: The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool
News.content:
Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

News.title: Three tasks to get your home ready for autumn, according to a professional cleaner
News.content:
When I was sweating away this summer, I never thought the weather would turn, but it’s almost time to crank up our radiators and crack out the big duvet.

They’re the tasks no one likes doing, but luckily for you, I’ve worked as a cleaner for more than a decade. I’ve discovered some shortcuts to make the hated jobs that bit easier.

Tip one: Keep your summer duvet fresh in storage

If, like me, you want to get your winter duvet out, your summer one needs to be cleaned and packed away to keep it fresh come spring.

Start by spot cleaning any stains. You can just use a standard household fabric stain remover for this. If you want to wash your duvet, most domestic washing machines aren’t big enough to fit a double, let alone a king or a super king. Your best bet is to take them down to the laundrette and follow the care instructions on the label.

Sports.title: Championship Catch-up: Swans soaring, Burnley win and Eckert saga ends
Sports.content:
Welcome to The Championship Catch-up, a new Sky Sports column in which Andy Hinchcliffe rounds up some of the key stories from the second tier. This week:

Soaring Swansea City lead the way

Burnley finally get their first win

Saints draw line under Eckert saga

Swansea City are deserved Championship leaders

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Swansea and Norwich

Swansea have been stronger than we thought they'd be this season. It seems that less is more with them because last season Zan Vipotnik scored 23 goals and really carried the team.

This season, he's only scored a couple of goals and hasn't played that many games. They've shown now, again, that without a star striker they over-rely on for goals, they're more of a team, both defensively and importantly going forward as well.

You look at them from back to front, they've got one of the best goalkeepers in the division and one of the most stubborn, strongest defences in the division. If you're going to be successful, certainly in the Championship, that really does help.

They're not a defensive team, they're a team that defend well. They dominate the ball, they control games and they've got a variety of goalscorers now as well. They're not reliant on just that one centre-forward. Adam Idah's got four goals, so he's kind of the main threat, but it's still not just him and nobody else.

The way they play enables four, five or six players to get into goalscoring positions and score goals over the course of the season. You're better being that type of team than having that reliance on one central striker. If he gets injured or he's out of form, things can get really tricky.

They deserve to be where they are right now, and we're going to learn a lot more this week about whether they can stay the course. They head to Millwall on Tuesday night, then host West Ham on Saturday.

Coaches and clubs are looking at squad depth now. You can't just be reliant on a few players, even on six or seven players, and keep hoping game in and game out that those six or seven players produce and get the job done for you.

For Swansea, there are maybe five or six attacking players who can change the course of a game.

Every defence they play against isn't really sure how Swansea are going to line up. You probably know how they're going to play in terms of their set-up, energy, urgency, pressing game and passing game. But who's going to be in the team and who's going to impact the game? I'd much rather have one problem than four or five coming at me.

Vitor Matos has done a brilliant job. You listen to players playing under these coaches talk about them, and Ben Cabango was saying this team will run through brick walls for the gaffer.

I think that drives players on even more.

Burnley get off the mark with a thumping win at Watford

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Watford and Burnley

Looking at Burnley's overall performances, they weren't performing like a bottom-three team. They were probably around mid-table, but for the club Burnley are, what they're looking to achieve and the players they've got, mid-table performances in this league aren't really acceptable. They're much better than that.

They've had the big change since relegation. We thought Craig Bellamy was coming in, but that didn't happen, and Nicky Hayen came in. He and the players have got to get to an understanding, and that can take a little bit of time.

Playing Watford, you're never really sure what you're going to get. They're a struggling team at the moment, but they can suddenly produce. I never expected Burnley to win that game, so to win it so comfortably was impressive.

Looking at all the stats from the game, the expected goals, they thoroughly deserved to win. Their xG was three times higher than Watford's. It wasn't a case of scoring four goals from four shots and being lucky to win. It was a game they dominated.

You look at the personnel and the teamsheet and think that's a team that should win a lot of Championship games. Not necessarily 4-0, but they should be winning Championship games.

Now they've won a game, I guarantee the training ground will be a totally different place. Looking at the experience and quality they've got, I wouldn't be surprised if they started to put a bit of a run together.

Let's see how they back that up during midweek and in that big game against Wolves on Friday night.

Saints win derby against toothless Pompey - and draw line under Eckert saga

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Portsmouth

The situation rumbled on far too long with Tonda Eckert. I still have to say that I, and most people looking at the situation, were surprised there wasn't some kind of enforced lay-off when you consider the bans that are given out for other things.

I think the FA commission probably looked at it and thought they'd thrown Southampton out of the play-offs and imposed a points deduction. That is unprecedented and a massive punishment for the club and the coach. Maybe they thought piling more agony on Eckert's shoulders wasn't what was needed.

The decision drew a line under it, and then Southampton's performance against Portsmouth drew a second line under it completely.

Eckert showed in that game what a talented coach he is. How he managed it and how he coached his team through it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tonda Eckert reflects on Southampton's first win over Portsmouth in almost 22 years and backs young midfielder Cameron Bragg to learn from his sending off

We got back to talking about football and him as a coach, rather than someone who did something he has admitted was wrong and that shouldn't happen in the English game.

He showed why Southampton were so desperate to keep him. They know they've got a good guy and a good coach there. Why would you want to get rid of someone you know can do the job? His record and numbers are outstanding, as is the quality of football they play.

From a Portsmouth perspective, the goal they gave away was an absolute shocker. It was a dreadful goal to concede. Collectively and individually, it was so avoidable, yet they didn't defend properly.

They haven't conceded an awful lot of goals, with only 11 so far, but it's the kind of goals they're giving away. They're soft goals, and you can't afford to do that if you want to get anywhere in the Championship.

John Mousinho did his best, looking at how many attacking players he sent on to try to influence things and change the game for Portsmouth after the Southampton red card. Time and again, they got into promising positions, but absolutely nothing came from it.

The main criticism will be that they were toothless. How can they not have a shot on target when they have the extra man and all those attacking players on? It just didn't happen.

They also lost the game because of the goal they gave away, which should never have happened. Losing a big derby is horrendous anyway, but how they lost it will be so disappointing for Portsmouth when they sit down, watch the game and have a debrief.

Sports.title: Jaissle sorry for Coventry loss as Carra says Newcastle 'beaten up' again
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has apologised to the travelling fans following their 4-1 loss at Coventry, as Jamie Carragher said they were "beaten up" once again on the road.

The Magpies' previous away game a month ago also saw them defeated 4-1 on the Monday Night Football at Leeds.

A second loss in three games comes after Jaissle had enjoyed an unbeaten five-game start across all competitions, but recent results have seen his side fall to 11th in the Premier League table.

A wasteful Newcastle lost at Coventry despite having 19 shots, three big chances and more than double the number of touches in the opposition box than the home side.



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United

Jaissle told Sky Sports: "We're frustrated. It's a feeling you don't want to have on a Monday evening after a match where you should win.

"We can only apologise to the fans who came here; they deserve a different result.

"We need to analyse it, clearly. There were bits that were good but, in both boxes, to defend our own goal we need to improve and also score goals.

"The opportunities were there, but the desire and hunger to finish the attacks was missing."

"If you conceded eight goals in two away matches on Monday evenings, then it's not good enough for the Premier League."

Carra: Newcastle 'beaten up' again

It is the first time since December 2012 that Newcastle have conceded four or more goals in back-to-back Premier League away games.

Speaking on Monday Night Football, Sky Sports' Carragher said: "We've consistently said this season they've had a good start results-wise, but the underlying numbers haven't been great.

"He's going with two strikers up there; I know (Yoane) Wissa drops a little bit deeper, but when Eddie Howe was there it was more of a 4-3-3.

"Every manager has their own way, but when you think of the lack of physicality in that team, it might be a case where you leave one of the strikers out and go with an extra body in midfield.

"It's a young team, and it isn't as physically powerful as a lot of the teams in the Premier League.

"And in their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly."

"A chastening evening for Newcastle, with another 4-1 away defeat.

"Newcastle actually created plenty of chances and looked dangerous in attack, and it felt like they might get something after Sven Botman's goal.

"But it's wide open at the back again, and that's against a Coventry team that had only scored once in the Premier League in their previous five games until Monday night.

"With no proper No 10 in the squad, it feels like they need to get back to the 4-3-3 and get some solidity back into the midfield.

"Teams are running over the top of the midfield due to lack of numbers and physical presence.

"There was more evidence tonight that Yoane Wissa is not a No 10, Joe Willock is not a No 6, and Matias Fernandez-Pardo is not a No 9."

It was one they had learned the hard way too, with the worst shot conversion of any team in the league coming into Monday's game and just one of 51 shots finding the back of the net to date.

Three superb finishes, and an early penalty, saw them to their first Premier League home win in more than 9,000 days, but their finishing was still not Coventry's most impressive quality on the night.

That fortitude, digging in after taking an early lead and hanging on after Sven Botman's wonder strike had given Newcastle a glimmer of hope at 2-1, was what won them the day and, on fight at least, that was enough to crown them worthy winners.

They have already needed that mental strength to bounce back from four goalless and pointless games to start their Premier League return, and, in a league as punishing as this, that could be what decides whether they will stay there come May.

Sports.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Southwell, Hereford and Wolverhampton feature
Sports.content:
The Sky Sports Racing cameras head to Southwell, Hereford and Wolverhampton on Tuesday, with every race LIVE from 1.45pm.

6.00 Wolverhampton - Bella Angelina and Soft Landing clash

Unexposed duo Bella Angelina and Soft Landing clash in the Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Novice Stakes.

The Harry Charlton-trained Juddmonte filly Bella Angelina has run to a fair level on both of her starts thus far. She ran behind two promising three-year-olds to finish third at Doncaster on debut, before being edged out by the progressive Wootton Bassett filly Wid, after travelling strongly into the race without the hood. Related to promising two-year-old, Sierra Belle, she holds a great chance of progressing and breaking her maiden tag with the aid of a wind operation.

Her main danger could be in the form of Saeed bin Suroor trained Soft Landing, who is coming off the back of a very encouraging debut where she tired late to finish second after looking sure to have the race won. Bin Suroor tends to have his horses ready to go but at least a small bit of improvement can be expected given the way she shaped on her last start.

Missmisfortune reopposes Soft Landing here and has run to a fair standard in two starts but was well beaten with the advantage of experience at Wolverhampton.

Perhaps Mr Keble is the most intriguing of the rest, making his first start for Oli Rix having been transferred from the Gosden yard. He was hampered in the final furlong when fifth at Kempton in September and so was better than the bare result, with the subsequent St James's Palace fifth ahead of him. He can run respectably if fit after over a year off the track.

Blue Point Gold is the only runner making their debut and contains an interesting pedigree, being a half-brother to the once potentially-useful Movie Maker.

2.35 Southwell - Cheesy Icon makes chasing debut

Progressive hurdler Cheesy Icon makes his chasing debut in the HEB Group "The Power Behind Everyday" Novices' Handicap Chase.

Cheesy Icon could not quite get off the mark over hurdles, but was steadily progressive and an opening mark of 116 over fences does seem fair. However, he does not seem like the obvious type to take a massive step forward for going over a fence and is very much a free going type who has been hard to settle. As such, the forecasted weak pace could therefore put him at a disadvantage.

The Ben Pauling-trained Four Springs is the most unexposed in the field and began his career very promisingly, mixing with horses that have since featured in top-end handicaps and graded races - most notably Sinnatra. However, he ran as if something was amiss when pulled up in the EBF Handicap Hurdle at Sandown when last seen, and will need to put that performance behind him. This lad seems a chasing type and there could be a lot more to come over fences with his opening mark of 118 not beyond him.

Marche D'Aligre is prone to a mistake or two so it cannot be certain whether he will take to fences for the first time, whilst Jamada has been progressive over hurdles for Olly Murphy. Lady Kara should run well, given she is the only one in the field to have proven consistency over fences.

3.30 Hereford - Krak and Donnie Azoff head field

Krak and Donnie Azoff feature in a trappy Betting.Bet Free Bets Handicap Hurdle.

Krak gradually improved over fences over four starts since moving to Dan Skelton, while dropping down to a fairer handicap mark. He returns to hurdles here, where he has shown his best form and only career success to date. He can prove competitive off a mark of 120 with Charlie Todd taking the ride.

At the age of 10, Donnie Azoff has been in the form of his life, maintaining incredible consistency to only finish outside of the top three on three occasions in his last 11 starts. The two and a half miles should suit here, given he seemed outpaced in his last two starts. His last win in June came when running on late under a perfectly timed ride from Isabelle Ryder.

Sixty Plus is an interesting contender for the dual purpose trainer James Owen, as he is back to just a pound above his last winning mark. Moreover, he has fallen nine pounds in the handicap since his last win over obstacles. He can go well after a fruitful flat campaign, which included a quick-fire hat-trick.

Son Of Hypnos won well on his penultimate start when getting free on the front, before doing too much at the head of affairs last time. The forecasted strong pace may not see him to best effect, while Jaramillo got back to form last time out, although he is not the most reliable type.

3.10 Southwell - Competitive 0-115 handicap chase

Sports.title: 'I let the team down' - Norris accepts blame for Piastri collision
Sports.content:
Lando Norris says he let McLaren down and has taken responsibility for his collision with Oscar Piastri in the Sprint at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Norris and Piastri made contact on the last lap of Saturday's shortened race when battling for fourth, which the stewards did not penalise either driver for.

However, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella labelled the incident as "not acceptable" while Norris was not keen to talk about the collision on Saturday and told Sky Sports F1: "As a team we all spoke about it. I apologised but that's all you need to know."

However, following his fourth-place finish in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix, Norris changed his tune when speaking to the written media.

"It's pretty straightforward. I can't attempt what I did. I should never have attempted in the first place, even if the move was on. I've got to think of the team that I represent more than myself," he said.

"It was a mistake on my part, and I let down the team. I've also apologised to all of them, I owe them all an apology, and I will do better next time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok dissects who was at fault for the collision between the two McLaren's which saw Oscar Piastri crash out of the Singapore GP Sprint

Stella: Conversations with drivers not finished

During Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix, Norris asked several times if he could aid team-mate Piastri in any way during the closing stages of the race.

Piastri was attempting to catch and overtake Lewis Hamilton at the time of the radio calls, suggesting Norris was querying whether he should back up the Ferrari driver. In the end, Piastri overtook Hamilton without any help to finish fifth behind Norris.

Stella says he was "very encouraged" by Norris' willingness to aid his team-mate but more talks will be held before the United States Grand Prix in Austin next weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McLaren team principal Andrea Stella reacts to the Sprint collision between Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri at the Singapore Grand Prix

"We are aligned as to how we want to lead this team forward in a joint effort between the team and the drivers," he said.

"The conversations that we are having, they are not finished but it's not because we need to go back discussing if Lando was alongside Oscar, that's not the interesting bit.

"For me the interesting bit is a reflection that all the stakeholders, the team, the drivers will have to make around leading together the team, embracing constantly from inside the cockpit the interest of the team, as something that is superior to any particular singular individual interest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris was downbeat after his performance in Singapore and hopes for better upgrades on the car going forward

"While the conversations from this point of view, they are not concluded and there's more we can do to become a more united and even stronger team, I'm pleased that Lando at some stage in the race adopted this way of thinking.

"This is what I expect as a team principal, this is what the 1000 people that work at McLaren expect from our drivers so it's good that we read this example. I expect definitely more of that in the future, independently of the fact that they will be heard in the radio, or they will happen behind the closed door in every meeting or in the way we approach our race plan."

Sports.title: Coventry thump Newcastle for first home win to move out of drop zone
Sports.content:
Coventry made it back-to-back Premier League wins with a thumping 4-1 home victory over Newcastle to move Frank Lampard's side out of the relegation zone.

Goals from Jack Rudoni, teenager Sidiki Cherif and substitutes Ellis Simms and Stephen Mfuni gave the Sky Blues their first home win of the season.

A stunning Sven Botman strike had given Newcastle hope of a comeback in the 70th minute, but Simms restored the hosts' two-goal lead with his first touch 11 minutes later before Mfuni superbly added a fourth to become Coventry's youngest-ever Premier League goalscorer.

A night of firsts for Coventry… First home win of the season

First PL home win in 25 years

First PL home goals of the season

First career penalty goal for Jack Rudoni

First Coventry goal for Sidiki Cherif

Ellis Simms scored with his first touch

First senior goal for Stephen Mfuni

The visitors, who suffered a second consecutive 4-1 away defeat, made a nightmare start at the CBS Arena as goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek brought down summer signing Cherif to allow Rudoni to hit a sixth-minute penalty opener.

Newcastle responded well to falling behind but were wasteful as Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed two big chances, with his one-on-one opportunity cleared off the line by Bobby Thomas.

Coventry then punished their profligacy immediately after the restart as Cherif fantastically doubled the lead in the 48th minute with the 19-year-old's powerful low strike from just outside the box, his first goal for the club.

Botman's goal, however, was even better as he thundered home from long range, but Coventry hit back through Simm's deflected strike three minutes and 15 seconds after he came off the bench.

Eighteen-year-old summer signing Mfuni, who joined from Manchester City on loan, then hit his first senior goal in the 86th minute to cap off a fine evening for Lampard's side.

Coventry can make it three victories in a row when they visit winless Tottenham next Monday, live on Sky Sports, while Newcastle aim to bounce back against Aston Villa at home on Saturday, also live on Sky Sports.

Carra: Newcastle have been 'beaten up' in their last two away games

Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher speaking on Monday Night Football:

"Every manager has their own way, but when you think of the lack of physicality in that [Newcastle] team, it might be a case where you leave one of the strikers out and go with an extra body in midfield.

"It's a young team, and it isn't as physically powerful as a lot of the teams in the Premier League.

"And in their last two away games, they've been beaten up twice - and that's got to stop very quickly."

Jaissle apologises to fans

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matthias Jaissle apologises to the travelling Newcastle fans

Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle speaking to Sky Sports:

"We're frustrated. It's a feeling you don't want to have on a Monday evening after a match where you should win.

"We can only apologise to the fans who came here; they deserve a different result.

"We need to analyse it, clearly. There were bits that were good, but in both boxes, to defend our own goal, we need to improve and also score goals. The opportunities were there, but the desire and hunger to finish the attacks was missing.

"We need to improve on the things we can control, and that's a lot right now."

Lampard: We played like the team we want to be

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Frank Lampard says his Coventry side delivered a 'complete performance'

Coventry boss Frank Lampard speaking to Sky Sports:

"We played like the team we want to be here. There's so much spirit and energy. We know we're going to have to suffer at times in games; we have to understand what the level is.

"But the work ethic from the team, the belief, then you get what you deserve, which is great finishes. We haven't had that rub of the green, which might have helped us nick a few more points.

"As a complete performance, we've got to keep our feet on the ground because it's only one game and we need 30 more of those. But it's a great feeling for the players."

Sports.title: Renshaw stars as Australia close in on first Test victory in Durban
Sports.content:
Matt Renshaw continued to hog centre stage as Australia pushed closer to winning the first Test against South Africa in Durban.

Renshaw added a second-innings knock of 82 to his game-shaping 190 and was not finished there. After Australia declared with a lead of 420, the occasional off-spinner picked up his maiden Test wicket as the Proteas laboured to 102-4.

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma was his victim, caught off bat and pad by Nic Maddinson for just one. Josh Hazlewood had already got the ball rolling, dismissing Ryan Rickelton and David Bedingham, with Pat Cummins adding Tristan Stubbs before the close on day four.

Aiden Markram will resume on 45 not out alongside Wiaan Mulder but the odds are stacked against the hosts salvaging the game on day five. Australia were without Steve Smith's brilliance at slip after he was hit on the helmet by Anrich Nortje and was subsequently replaced in the field pending further assessments.

Renshaw's second innings bore almost no relation to his first. The 190 came at a strike-rate of 47. The 82 came at 82, with seven fours and two sixes in it.

Then it took a freak moment to end it. The ball went through Keshav Maharaj's hands more than once and off his own head before it stayed put, by which time the bowler was flat on the pitch.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Renshaw was caught and bowled by Keshav Maharaj in bizarre fashion after the decision was reviewed

Renshaw was on for twin centuries when it happened. Instead he finished with 272 runs for the match, which is close to the most any Australian has made against South Africa.

Three more runs would have put him level with Phillip Hughes, who made twin tons on this ground in 2009. Nine more and he would have passed David Warner's pair of centuries in Cape Town in 2014. Bradman's 299 not out was 28 away.

Nobody else in the Australian order got past 48. Maddinson stopped there, Marnus Labuschagne on 37, Smith on 27 and Alex Carey on 24.

Captain Cummins hurries things along for Australia

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia captain Pat Cummins smashed three sixes from four balls

Australia resumed on 33-0 and never looked like batting for time. They were 174-4 at lunch and 280 in front, with Maddinson's 48 from 38 balls setting the rate.

Labuschagne then produced the day's statistical curiosity. He made 37 from 58 balls, exactly what he managed in the first innings, which is only the 12th known instance of a batter matching his runs and his balls faced in both innings of a men's Test.

But Smith's 27 was the innings Nortje will remember. The bouncer that hit him on the helmet arrived on the fourth ball he faced and Smith answered by taking 14 off one Nortje over.

Cricket Australia said he was being assessed for concussion and he will be monitored for 24 hours.

Cummins made the rest a formality. His 32 not out took just a dozen balls, with Simon Harmer conceding three of his four sixes inside one over. The declaration came shortly before tea on 314-6.

Markram the last line of resistance for hosts

South Africa were left 421 to win, which no side in Test history has managed.

West Indies' 418 against Australia in Antigua in 2003 is still the mark and the best at this ground is 336, chased by Australia in 1950.

Batting out the day is the realistic hope and the record there is thin. Just two sides in the last 13 years have lasted 140 overs to save a Test.

Rickelton pulled at a short one in the fourth over and Carey took the catch, two runs made with Hazlewood again the bowler who had him.

Markram and Bedingham put on 66 in 19.4 overs before Hazlewood pinned Bedingham in front for 46. He was 49 first time round, so twice in the match he got into the forties and no further.

Image: South Africa's Aiden Markram was 45no at stumps

Three wickets went down for 13 runs from there and South Africa were 86-4, scoring across the innings at 2.48 an over.

Markram has needed 115 balls for his 45 not out and he was dropped on the way, on 15, when the chance hit Carey on the elbow and ran away past slip.

Among players still active, only Kusal Mendis of Sri Lanka averages more than Markram's 45.56 in a fourth innings. His 136 won the World Test Championship final against these same opponents at Lord's.

He has been in this position at this ground before, too. He made 143 here in 2018 chasing 417 against Australia, 340 minutes of work that still ended in defeat.

He will be hoping that something miraculous can happen on Tuesday with Australia needing six wickets to win and South Africa still requiring 319 runs.
