Sports.title: The 10 England bolters ready to shake up Steve Borthwick's squad this autumn: A 19-year-old Northampton flier, a Tongan-born wildcard in the centres, the hooker 'built like cement' and the 2003 World Cup winner's son
Sports.content:
The 10 England bolters ready to shake up Steve Borthwick's squad this autumn: A 19-year-old Northampton flier, a Tongan-born wildcard in the centres, the hooker 'built like cement' and the 2003 World Cup winner's son

After three rounds of try-filled PREM Rugby action, attention shifts to the start of the 2026-27 Champions Cup.

It is also now less than a month until England’s November Nations Championship campaign begins with matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, before the inaugural finals weekend at Twickenham.

Steve Borthwick will name his first autumn training squad later this month and after a rocky 2026 that saw him register England's worst Six Nations performance and a first-ever defeat by Italy, he may well be on the lookout for new blood, with less than a year to go until the World Cup.

Here, Daily Mail Sport’s Alex Bywater looks at 10 uncapped players who could make the cut to shake up England’s established order after impressing so far this season.

1. George Hendy

Age: 23, Position: Wing/full-back, Club: Northampton Saints

Hendy has been a regular PREM try scorer for a while now, crossing twice in last season's final as Northampton lifted the title, and has three more already to begin this campaign.

Fast and elusive, the flame-haired flier has earned England A selection before – winning two caps in 2025 – but looks ready to make the next step.

George Hendy is a constant threat for free-flowing Northampton, and has three tries already this season

Borthwick has flitted between full-backs in recent years, with a rotating cast of George Furbank, Freddie Steward, Elliot Daly and Marcus Smith, and he could do with a nailed-on solution.

In addition to his individual abilities, Hendy would link up well with the raft of Northampton players already in England's back line, such as Fin Smith, Alex Mitchell and Tommy Freeman.

Hendy missed his team’s hammering of Bath at the weekend with a hip injury but the problem isn’t thought to be serious and he should be back fit soon.

2. Nathan Jibulu

Age: 23, Position: Hooker, Club: Sale Sharks

England’s options at hooker look ripe for disruption.

Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie have been wonderful servants and are still leading the way, but are 35 and 33 respectively, while Theo Dan hasn’t quite come through as expected.

Jibulu was player of the match in Sale’s wins over Saracens and Harlequins this season, and could be the answer to what is threatening to become a problem position.

Nicknamed ‘cement’ by his club coaches (because he’s as hard as), the Croydon-born former Harlequin is very good around the park and his set-piece throwing has improved.

He signed a long-term contract this summer keeping him in the North West until 2030, and has already begun to repay Sale's faith.

Nicknamed ‘cement’ by his club coaches (because he’s as hard as), Nathan Jibulu is very good around the park and his set-piece throwing has improved

3. Jack Bracken

Age: 20, Position: Wing, Club: Saracens

Son of 2003 World Cup-winning scrum-half Kyran, Bracken's brother Charlie, another No9, has already been part of a senior England squad and Jack could soon follow suit.

He impressed as Saracens beat Bristol at the weekend and provides an elusive running threat.

Bracken, who came through Saracens' academy and has also represented development side Ampthill, is well-liked by his club coaches and looks one to watch, regardless of whether this autumn comes too soon.

He has represented England's Under 18s and Under 20s, and scored his first PREM try of the season on Saturday in a comprehensive 30-7 win over Bristol.

Jack Bracken scored his first PREM try of the season on Saturday in a comprehensive 30-7 win over Bristol

4. Max Hicks

Age: 27, Position: Flanker, Club: Newcastle Red Bulls

The New Zealand-born flanker arrived in English rugby this summer after signing for Newcastle from French side Perpignan.

While not a youngster by any stretch, he qualifies for Borthwick’s side through his mother Liane, who is from Cornwall.

He’s tall, rangy and very athletic – a good link player and a dark horse. He too got his first try of the season at the weekend, crossing in Newcastle's narrow defeat at Exeter.

England-qualified flanker Max Hicks (left) is tall, rangy and very athletic – a good link player and a dark horse

5. James Pater

Age: 19, Position: Full-back, Club: Northampton Saints

Pater was picked out by Daily Mail Sport as a young gun to watch at the start of the new PREM season and promptly scored a hat-trick in his team’s opener against Newcastle.

He has shown his talent for England Under 20s and has adjusted well to senior level for his club, even if playing in the league’s best team has aided that transition.

Pater is still growing into his body but his ball-playing talent is obvious. He only joined Saints three years ago after impressing at the Rosslyn Park Sevens, and is already one of their most exciting prospects on a seemingly endless production line.

Pater was picked out by Daily Mail Sport as a young gun to watch at the start of the new PREM season and he promptly scored a hat-trick in his team’s opener against Newcastle

6. Sione Va'enuku

Age: 23, Position: Centre, Club: Saracens

Like at hooker, England have question marks at centre. But Tongan Va’enuku, who started his career in the NRL with the Sydney Roosters, is a wildcard option to shake things up.

England-qualified through his mother Kate, Va'enuku has only played two PREM games after moving to Saracens from Championship Ampthill but has a nice blend of power, pace and handling ability.

He has gone well against Sale and Bristol, and Borthwick may look to get him involved to ensure he’s kept out of the hands of other countries.

Will Joseph has also been playing very well for Gloucester, but he does not make this list as he already has a cap to his name, against Australia back in 2022.

English-qualified Tongan Sione Va'enuku could be a wildcard option in the centres

7. Archie McParland

Age: 21, Position: Scrum-half, Club: Northampton Saints

Yes, another Northampton player – but perhaps the one most likely to make a big impact next month.

Alex Mitchell has been England’s first-choice scrum-half, but McParland has been rivalling him at club level for some time and may well now do so internationally.

His dynamic game is perfect for Saints. He has quick distribution and an eye for a gap.

McParland is yet to play a Test despite being in England squads, but that could all change very quickly after a fast start to this season.

Alex Mitchell has been England’s first-choice scrum-half, but Archie McParland (pictured) has been rivalling him at club level for some time and may well now do so internationally

8. Fitz Harding

Age: 27, Position: Flanker, Club: Bristol Bears

Harding has a problem in that England are stacked with back-row talent – the likes of Ben Earl, Tom Curry, Sam Underhill, Ollie Chessum, Henry Pollock and Guy Pepper are all top operators, while there are plenty more lurking on the sidelines.

But if PREM form is the barometer by which international selection is earned, Harding must be putting himself in the frame for a call-up. The Bristol captain is a consistent league performer and a good leader too.

He also did what many can’t and stopped Northampton’s free-flowing, go-forward possession in round two.

Bristol captain Fitz Harding (left) managed to do the impossible in round two and stymie Northampton's free-flowing attack

9. Ethan Burger

Age: 26, Position: Prop, Club: Exeter Chiefs

South African-born and raised, Burger rose from nowhere to be a regular for Exeter last season as they made the PREM final against the odds. He is eligible to represent England because his grandfather was born in Leicester.

Ross McMillan, Exeter’s forward coach, scouted Burger when he was playing for the University of Pretoria, where he was studying education, and the Chiefs have reaped the rewards.

He has a good combination of being a strong scrummager and also explosive around the park for a big man.

Exeter's Ethan Burger has a good combination of being a strong scrummager and also explosive around the park for a big man

Orlando Bailey, who can play fly-half and inside centre, has quietly impressed since moving to Leicester Tigers at the start of last season

10. Orlando Bailey

Age: 25, Position: Fly-half/centre, Club: Leicester Tigers

His talent was recognised by former England coach Eddie Jones when he was a surprise Six Nations squad inclusion in 2022 while still at Bath. A hamstring injury put paid to him featuring in that championship.

Bailey, who can play fly-half and inside centre, has quietly impressed since moving to Leicester Tigers at the start of last season, as an instrumental figure in their rise back into the play-offs.

The 25-year-old won his first England A cap in February against an Ireland XV and his versatility along the back line is another boost for his chances.

Sports.title: Britain's star cyclist - one half of GB's golden couple - is SENT HOME from World Championships in China over 'misconduct'
Sports.content:
Britain's star cyclist - one half of GB's golden couple - is SENT HOME from World Championships in China over 'misconduct'

Team GB cyclist Matthew Richardson has been sent home from the World Track Cycling Championships in Shanghai over allegations of misconduct.

Richardson, 27, switched allegiance from Australia to Britain after the last Olympics and had been expected to secure three medals in China this week after declaring himself the fastest cyclist in history.

Now instead he is in the process of leaving the country.

In a statement sent to Daily Mail Sport, a British Cycling spokesperson said: 'British Cycling can confirm that Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain Cycling Team squad for the upcoming 2026 Tissot UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, China.'

When approached by Daily Mail Sport about the misconduct allegations which are believed to have prompted Richardson's withdrawal, the organisation added that they would not be commenting further at this stage.

The Times reported Richardson is subject to an investigation into his behaviour, particularly towards teammates.

The investigation is said to have been prompted by a complaint from another rider.

Matthew Richardson has been withdrawn from the World Track Cycling Championships

Richardson's partner is fellow British cyclist Emma Finucane, who is also out in China

One rider who spoke to the Times said Richardson would not moderate his behaviour even when engaging with athletes from minority backgrounds.

British Cycling added to the Times: ‘British Cycling takes any allegations of harassment, bullying or discrimination extremely seriously.

'Where concerns are raised, they are investigated thoroughly through our established procedures.

'Out of fairness to anyone involved in an investigation, we would not comment on any ongoing process.’

Richardson is one half of Britain's cycling golden couple. He is in a long-term relationship with Emma Finucane, the star of Great Britain's women's team.

Richardson and Finucane live together in Manchester and have been dating since February 2024 after 'knowing each other for a long time'.

Richardson had been due to be one of four members of the men's sprint squad at the World Championships.

He had been due to join Harry Ledingham-Horn, Ed Lowe and Joe Truman in the squad.

Richardson had claimed three medals at the European Championships in Konya, Turkey, earlier this year.

Richardson and Finucane have joked about being 'the world's fastest household' on the track

The 27-year-old won gold in both the men's sprint and keirin events, as well as claiming silver in the team sprint with Truman and Hamish Turnbull.

Richardson had been due to make his comeback after he was injured during the Keirin World Series in July.

Last week, Richardson said he is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival in an incident, which ruled him out of the Commonwealth Games three months ago.

Richardson had been slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the event July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The sprinter said he has not received an apology from Suzuki over the incident.

Richardson poses in a Union Jack flag after switching allegiance from Australia

Richardson's hopes of competing at the Commonwealth Games were ended in Japan

Join the discussion Should sports teams act faster on misconduct allegations, or risk damaging trust among athletes and fans?

He was favourite to win gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash. He was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

Richardson had been hoping to defend the title he won when competing for Australia in 2022, before he switched nationality to represent Britain, which he claimed was like 'Hogwarts' compared to 'High School'.

The Australian defector, who was born in the English town of Maidstone but moved to Perth at nine and went on to carve out a brilliant track career for Australia, caused a sensation by switching allegiance straight after winning two silvers and a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

He received a life ban for competing for Australia, but despite early bitter criticism back in the country that honed his cycling talent, he's since carved out a strikingly impressive career in GB and England skinsuits.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba in limbo: How the World Cup winner is still mulling his next move after his shock Monaco exit - as the ex-Man United star calls for Man City to hand over TWO Premier League titles
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba in limbo: How the World Cup winner is still mulling his next move after his shock Monaco exit - as the ex-Man United star calls for Man City to hand over TWO Premier League titles

Paul Pogba is strolling down the pit wall at Marina Bay Street Circuit in Singapore. Journalists begin to circle, and soon enough, the subject of Manchester City’s guilty verdict arises.

The Frenchman smirks, raises his hand, and responds: ‘I have nothing to say, to be honest.’

But Pogba does have something to say. Four years may have passed since the 33-year-old was last competing with the Cityzens for their biggest rivals, Manchester United, but the midfielder still has a vested interest in the outcome of their appeal against the club's conviction on 114 Premier League charges.

‘I just hope it doesn't affect the Premier League,’ Pogba continues. ‘Hopefully we can get two titles back.’

Pogba was once the main man at United, a key cog in two teams that went toe-to-toe with City at their very peak. But he came out on the wrong side of the fight to the juggernaut on both occasions, with the Red Devils coming second to their rivals in both the 2017-18 and 2020-21 campaigns.

Only the first of those near-misses came during the period in which City were found to have used 'sham' contracts and agreements to cook their books by around £900million. So whatever punishment does come City’s way, if there is one, Pogba can most likely only dream of one Premier League crown.

Paul Pogba spoke on the Man City guilty verdict while at Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday

These days the one-time World Cup winner isn’t competing for titles, though. He is a free agent, and has been since his Monaco contract was terminated in the summer, following an injury-ravaged spell in the principality.

Instead of strutting his stuff on the pitch, he now lives the glamorous life of an attendee of Formula One Grands Prix – as he was in Singapore on Sunday when asked about City – and fashion shows in the most stylish city in the world.

Pogba’s appearance in the Asian city-state was courtesy of his long-term sponsor Adidas, who he has been partnered with for over a decade, and followed on from his presence with wife Zulay at The Business of Fashion 500 Gala in Paris last week.

The former France international has long loved the world of fashion, constantly showcasing bold clothing choices away from his sporting career – some cool, and some questionable – and he even has his own apparel brand.

POGBA MDXCIII – 1593 in Roman numerals, which could refer to his birthdate of March 15, 1993 – was launched in October last year and is designed in Miami, with 'the finest artisans and manufacturers', and aims to 'redefine the codes of luxury sport, blending excellence, authenticity, and emotion'.

BOF 500 was part of the famous Paris Fashion Week, the most prestigious cohort of shows in the world of fashion – part of the ‘Big Four’ alongside Milan, London and New York – and Pogba rocked up sporting a sleek tuxedo, arm in arm with Zulay. He looked a million dollars and the smile on his face suggested he felt the same way.

Pogba is living a truly lavish life of extravagance, and if he were to step away from football altogether, he wouldn’t be short of avenues to go down. That said, he has not let it be known that he has plans to hang up his boots.

The midfielder, who was once deemed one of the best in the world, was trying to revive his career when he signed for Monaco on an initial two-year deal. He broke down once the move was confirmed, with this his first step toward redemption after serving an 18-month doping ban.

Pogba (pictured scoring against Man City in 2018) was part of a Man United team who twice finished second to rivals City

Pogba is without a club after having his Monaco contract terminated during the summer

His first game for the club came a mammoth 808 days after he last laced up his boots for his previous club, Juventus. That was due to a four-year suspension he was initially handed while at the Italian club after testing positive for the prohibited substance DHEA – a ban which sent one of football's biggest names into the wilderness.

Pogba had admitted to Juventus that he took some nutritional supplements, supposedly supplied to him by a Miami-based doctor, but was totally unaware that they contained testosterone, which led to his ban.

In the year that followed, the former Man United and Juventus star kept a low profile. That was until October 2024, when his ban was slashed to 18 months. From the darkness, Pogba could then see the light.

The reduction meant Pogba was free to return to professional football, and he did so with Monaco. But after only featuring in six games during one season at the club, while earning £44,000 a week, his contract was cut short.

After everything he has been through, he is back to square one.

A career in Europe doesn’t seem to be on the cards for Pogba, nor does a venture to Saudi Arabia. However, the MLS appears to be the most likely destination at the time of writing. Daily Mail Sport understands Pogba was offered to clubs within the league back in August.

Interest from across the pond isn’t new; Pogba previously held talks with DC United, while David Beckham’s Inter Miami – home to Lionel Messi – have also been linked to the midfielder in the past.

There have also been rumours about a new life in the Big Apple, with Pogba linked with a move to New York City FC, where Frank Lampard went to retire following his 13-year trophy-laden stint at Chelsea. Nevertheless, Pogba has yet to have had any concrete talks with a new suitor.

The 33-year-old was last week spotted at aParis Fashion Week event with wife Zulay

Pogba has launched a new clothing brand last year and has long held an interest in the world of fashion

Meanwhile, as the rumour mill continues to spin, Pogba, who enjoyed two spells at United and made over 230 appearances for the club – scoring 39 times and providing 51 assists – is making sure to help those who trod the same steps he once took in Manchester.

Summer signing Carlos Baleba, who made his debut during the disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham at Old Trafford on Saturday night, recently revealed that Pogba was the first to congratulate him on his £70million switch from Brighton.

‘It was Paul Pogba,’ Baleba said when questioned on who first texted him after the move. ‘He said Manchester is a big club, a great city and he really enjoyed it here.’

If Baleba can produce similar moments of magic to what Pogba did in a Red Devils shirt, he will do more than just endear himself to the fans. The Frenchman will also want to rediscover that form when he eventually returns to the turf, to help rebuild a career that once threatened to flourish into one of the greatest we have seen but didn’t.

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle hits out at Newcastle's lack of 'desire and hunger to score' after humbling at Coventry
Sports.content:
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle has hit out at his side's lack of 'desire and hunger to score' after they suffered a demoralising 4-1 away defeat at Coventry.

The Magpies slipped to 11th in the Premier League table as they suffered their second defeat of the season, with Frank Lampard's side picking up their second win in as many games.

While the away side struggled defensively, they also came up short in attacking areas, with centre back Sven Botman the only away player on target with an impressive long-range effort.

Summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed a golden opportunity in the first-half at 1-0, and Jaissle has admitted he needs to address his forward players.

'We're frustrated definitely,' he said on Sky Sports after the game. 'The lads (are) as well in the dressing room, it's a feeling you don't want to have when you feel as though you should have won.

'We can only apologise to the fans that took the journey. We need to analyse it clearly, especially in the box, at both ends. The desire and hunger to score, to finish the attacks, that was missing.

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle has admitted his team lacked 'the desire to score' in their defeat by Coventry

Matias Fernandez-Pardo missed a golden opportunity to level the score when it was 1-0

'There's something we need to look at for sure. We need to win these games in the boxes. Defensively we need to improve. On the offensive we need to be more sharp.'

Coventry hadn't scored in the league until their last match, but managed four on Monday evening.

The deadlock was broken when Jack Rudoni netted from the penalty spot, after goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek had brought down Sidiki Cherif in the box.

Cherif himself then made it 2-0, and Coventry added two more late on.

'It's something that can happen in football, especially when you're managing a young squad, but there can still be a possibility to go on and win that match,' Jaissle added of the penalty. 'The second goal there was a foul on Joe Willock but it wasn't whistled, in my eyes, he was then missing in that spot where the ball dropped after the throw in.

On the timing of Cherif's goal, he said: 'It's never nice to concede a goal but we had the approach after half-time to come out and turn it around.

'The lads believed so we made the first goal and momentum was on our side. That's something also we need to learn that in a risk zone you cannot lose the ball. You cannot invite the opposition to score the third one, then it's going to be difficult.'

Manchester City have appealed after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules and await a decision over the sanctions they face

Sports.title: 'It was getting worse every day at Man Utd – but I enjoyed my football again at Atletico'
Sports.content:
'It was getting worse every day at Man Utd – but I enjoyed my football again at Atletico'

The forward needed to leave Old Trafford to get his career back on track and two of his former clubs meet this week

View 2 Images Memphis Depay didn't enjoy his time at Manchester United (Image: Clive Brunskill, Getty Images)

This week's Champions League meeting between Atletico Madrid and Manchester United pits two of Memphis Depay's former clubs against one another. The Dutch international left both with some regrets, but the Old Trafford stint had him in a particularly bad place.

‌



‌



Memphis moved to Old Trafford in the summer of 2015 in a move which reunited him with his former Netherlands boss Louis van Gaal. However, the former PSV Eindhoven forward was unable to reprise the magic he produced for the Oranje.

‌



He scored just twice in the Premier League, though five further goals arrived in Europe. Things got even worse in his second season, though, with new manager Jose Mourinho handing him just 134 minutes of competitive football.

‌



In his 2019 book Heart of a Lion, the Dutchman reflected on his time in Manchester. While he got back to his best after leaving England, he said it was an especially tough time.

"During that time I lost it," he said. "After training I went home and didn't want to see anybody. That was mentally a very bad period. And it got worse every day.

‌



"Looking from the outside I had a good life: being a part of one of the biggest clubs in the world, living in a beautiful home with a swimming pool, together with my best friend Gigi [Vitale], driving in a Rolls-Royce. But I was totally unhappy with my life.

"For the first time I lost the joy in playing football. The most beautiful thing in my whole life, football, gave me a very sad feeling. The frustration grew by the day and I didn't know how to change that."

The 32-year-old spent 18 months in the Spanish capital and scored four league goals in his first half-season - twice as many as he delivered in the Premier League. Sports.title: Man Utd without six players vs Atletico Madrid as injury crisis hits Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Man Utd without six players vs Atletico Madrid as injury crisis hits Michael Carrick

Manchester United will be without six players for their Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid tonight

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has new injury problems as he struggles to steer Manchester United to form this season (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw will miss Manchester United's Champions League showdown with Atletico Madrid through injury. The English duo are among six players who head coach Michael Carrick will be without for the crucial European outing.

‌



‌



United are facing a crucial run of fixtures as the pressure mounts on the Red Devils boss following a mediocre start to the season. Dominic Solanke's stoppage-time header earned a deserved point for Tottenham Hotspur on Sunday as United failed to capitalise on a man advantage once again, in an underwhelming showing.

‌



Tuesday's opponents appear to have a clean bill of health, while Carrick still has several squad members sidelined. Amad returned against Tottenham, Matthijs de Ligt has travelled to the Spanish capital, and Tom Heaton is training again - however, their returns have coincided with other injury issues.

‌



Shaw was substituted in the sixth minute of second half added-time against Spurs. Mainoo completed the match but has now joined his fellow England international on the sidelines after not training on Monday morning.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Carrick confirmed during his press conference in Madrid hours later: "They've not travelled, they both picked up issues in the game on Saturday, and we were working through that, to see what that looks like. At the moment, they are not ready for the game tomorrow."

Benjamin Sesko, Noussair Mazraoui and Patrick Dorgu also did not take part in the session. Neither did Manuel Ugarte, who continues to rehabilitate from knee surgery at Carrington.

Dorgu and Mazraoui sustained injuries while on international duty with Denmark and Morocco, respectively. Carrick confirmed before the Spurs match that they would be absent.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone's £34million property empire with Atletico boss owning over 180 Madrid homes
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone's £34million property empire with Atletico boss owning over 180 Madrid homes

The Atletico Madrid manager is also a property mogul with almost 200 homes and plans to build more

View 3 Images Diego Simeone has made millions from his side hustle (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Diego Simeone has topped up his staggering earnings with a property empire worth £34million. The Atletico Madrid boss, whose side host Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, is one of the best-paid managers in the game with an annual salary of around £14million per year.

‌



‌



And that's after recently taking a pay cut from his previous wage of £17m per annum. Away from football, the Argentine has diversified impressively by building a Madrid property portfolio of 180 homes, mostly flats in the heart of the Spanish capital.

‌



He hasn't just snapped up flats but seven entire buildings. The scale of Simeone's property has been revealed by the Equipo de Investigacion show presented by Gloria Serra.

‌



Property is a thorny issue in Spain, with complaints of high prices, a housing shortage and evictions, but the Simeones have made hay. The show says Simeone's wife, former model and presenter Carla Pereyra, fronts their main property company called Carpersim SL.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

According to the firm's financial statements filed with the Mercantile Registry, the assets held by this company are worth around €39.7, just under £34m.

‌

In the Equipo de Investigacion report, Cote Villar, of the lifestyle website Vanitatis, says: "They have opened an agency to handle rentals for these properties, and their most recent financial statements, covering the 2024 fiscal year, show assets valued at around €40m."

Villar adds that Pereyra, who has a family background in architecture, is the "driving force behind the business" and "knows the sector well."

Sports.title: Donald Trump appears in new Mike Tyson documentary to discuss rape case
Sports.content:
Donald Trump appears in new Mike Tyson documentary to discuss rape case

President Donald Trump features on Mike Tyson's new Netflix documentary and had some belated advice to the boxing legend

View 3 Images President Donald Trump has suggested Mike Tyson made a mistake by testifying in his own rape trial in 1992 (Image: Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Mike Tyson may have weakened his own case by testifying in the 1992 trial over his rape of Desiree Washington. That's according to the president of the United States, Donald Trump, who gives his account in a new Netflix documentary.

‌



‌



Tyson, 60, was convicted of raping then-18-year-old beauty pageant contestant Washington at the Canterbury Hotel in July 1991. The boxing icon was sentenced to six years in prison, though he ultimately served only three before his release in March 1995.

‌



President Trump was involved in Tyson's career at the time and helped promote several of his fights in the late 1980s and early '90s. The Convention Hall in Atlantic City, New Jersey, which was connected to Trump Plaza, hosted bouts against the likes of Michael Spinks, Carl Williams and Alex Stewart.

‌



Specifically, Trump has suggested Tyson may have harmed his own defence by giving testimony. 'The Baddest Man on the Planet' testified in an Indianapolis court for 78 minutes, insisting his encounter with Washington was consensual, which led to accusations of inconsistencies in his account from the prosecution.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I think Mike shouldn't have testified," said the sitting president during his cameo on the docuseries, TYSON, which premieres on Tuesday. Trump was himself found liable for the sexual abuse and defamation of writer E Jean Carroll in a federal civil jury in 2023.

‌



Mike Tyson did not stutter when offering Conor Benn vs Ryan Garcia prediction READ MORE :

"I'm not sure that he did a bad job in testifying. But one thing with Mike, he's very truthful. And I think the truth hurt him...in this case."

TYSON features accounts from those close to the famed boxer, as well as his personal bodyguard and others. One friend, Dawn Milhouse, suggests he "never stood a chance" of winning the trial in Indianapolis due to alleged racist roots in the state.

However, the third episode of the series also features an account from Dr. Thomas Richardson, an emergency room physician at Methodist Hospital in Indianapolis at the time. Richardson, who examined Washington when she went to the hospital the day after agreeing to visit Tyson, said she had abrasions consistent with sexual assault.

‌



Other beauty pageant witnesses who had also met Tyson around the time of the allegations noted his forthcoming nature regarding his intentions. One recalled how Tyson would go from girl to girl asking if they wanted to date, highlighting some intentionally steered clear of him as a result.

View 3 Images Tyson was sentenced to six years in prison over the rape charge but only ended up serving half that (Image: Getty)

Tyson's testimony in court appeared to back up those accounts as he admitted in court: “I explained to her that I wanted to f*** her."

‌



He maintains his innocence and belief the encounter was completely consensual in the documentary, saying: "She never said 'no'. I didn't cross a line."

An account from Tyson's chauffeur at the time, Virginia Foster, also worked against his defence. Foster testified under oath that Washington looked more dishevelled and appeared to be "in a state of shock" when she returned to the limousine in the early hours of the morning.

Foster also alleged Tyson had previously exposed himself to her in a hotel room and made advances on a separate occasion.

‌



View 3 Images Tyson appeared at a Trump rally this week endorsing the President ahead of the US mid-term elections (Image: Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Trump's relationship with Tyson appears to be alive and well today. Just this week, Tyson appeared at a Trump rally in Syracuse, New York, ahead of the US mid-term elections and called him "my president."

Addressing a crowd of Republican supporters, he added: "There's no way in the world I would ever be here if it wasn't for a president like Donald Trump."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick replacement 'targeted' as JJ Gabriel's 'next club' emerges

Manchester United round-up as Michael Carrick chases a much-needed win amid reports a potential replacement has been contacted

View 3 Images Michael Carrick may not have long left to turns things around (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

The pressure is cranking up on Michael Carrick ahead of Manchester United's Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid. Carrick's struggling side are winless in their four matches since opening the league phase with a 4-0 victory against minnows Sabah of Azerbaijan.

‌



‌



United's latest setback came in Saturday's 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham, who equalised in stoppage time, despite having lost Rodrigo Bentancur to a second-half red card. The Spurs midfielder was sent off for headbutting Shaw, who had reacted angrily to an ugly challenge by the Uruguay international.

‌



To make matters worse, Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are injury doubts for the Atletico game and missed training ahead of the flight to Spain. Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui are out of the match, joining long-term absentee Manuel Ugarte on the sidelines.

‌



Ahead of a big night for Carrick, here's a round-up of the latest United news…

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Conte 'tops replacement list'

Antonio Conte is at the top of United's managerial shortlist if the club loses patience with Carrick, according to reports in Italy. Conte is out of work after leaving Napoli at the end of last season and has said he would be interested in returning to work with a fallen giant.

‌



Michael Owen makes feelings clear on Michael Carrick as Man Utd sent sack verdict READ MORE :

Man Utd make late call on two stars struggling with injury ahead of Atletico Madrid clash READ MORE :

Per Calciomercato IT, United have made 'initial contact' with Conte's representatives and are assessing his interest in the role, should it become available. There is also reported interest from Juventus, where Conte managed between 2011 and 2014, but the United role is said to interest the 57-year-old more.

Speaking to The Athletic recently, Conte dropped an intriguing hint about his next move. He said: "If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself - a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories - you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back, if it isn't there today, to fight for those goals."

View 3 Images Antonio Conte is ready to return to work (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Real confidence

Real Madrid are increasingly confident of signing wantaway youngster JJ Gabriel. The 16-year-old, who had been close to making his senior debut, rocked United last month by asking the club to release him amid interest from the likes of Real, Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

While United can stop him from joining another Premier League club this season, as he holds an EU passport, there is a mechanism for him to join a European club. According to Madrid-based reporter Jose Felix Diaz, a final decision on Gabriel is looming, with Los Blancos believing they are leading the race to sign the teenager, who has made La Liga his first-choice destination.

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel is close to leaving United (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Article continues below

There seems to be growing acceptance at United that Gabriel will soon move on. Asked last week if there had been any change to the situation during the international break, Carrick said: "No, nothing's changed at all."

Sports.title: Horse ridden by Team GB two-time Olympic gold medal winner Laura Collett dies in crash
Sports.content:
Horse ridden by Team GB two-time Olympic gold medal winner Laura Collett dies in crash

Tinks Walker, 17, has had her hopes of competing in the Olympics thrown into doubt after her beloved prizewinning horse was killed in a horror crash in Wiltshire

View 3 Images Tinks Walker and her beloved horse Benny who tragically died (Image: JustGiving)

A prizewinning horse - previously ridden by a two-time Team GB gold medal winner - was killed in a horror crash that has thrown its teen equestrians Olympic dreams into doubt.

‌



‌



A car ploughed into Tinks Walker, 17, while on a country lane in the Cotswolds with her beloved elite showjumping horse Killossery Kaptain, known as Benny. The teen said her horse, thought to be worth hundreds of thousands of pounds, was fatally injured in the incident.

‌



The heartbreaking crash has shattered the 17-year-old girl's hopes for being selected for Great Britain in next year's Eventing European Championships for Young Riders.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Benny was a 10-year-old prizewinning horse (Image: Instagram/tinks_walker)

Tinks had taken her 10-year-old gelding out for a ride in the morning, on April 2, along with a two-year-old horse named Lily. The teenager told the police she allegedly saw a car "flying around the curve" in a country road around a mile from her home in Malmesbury, Wiltshire.

‌



The teen allegedly moved the horses onto a grass verge, according to the Daily Mail, and said: "I felt totally powerless and the next thing was I felt an impact. I woke up on the floor. It felt like I had been beaten up."

Tinks, in her account to Wiltshire Police, added: "I saw Benny lying on the floor. Benny did try and get up once - but struggled to do so and ultimately fell back down to the floor. He did not try and stand up again."

View 3 Images The horse died after a road incident in the Cotswolds (Image: Instagram/tinks_walker)

‌



Benny had been a four-star competition horse and was ridden by Laura Collett, a Team GB two-time Olympic gold medal winner. The A-Level student trained with the horse each day and said Benny was her "best friend".

In a fundraiser set up by the teen, Tinks said: "He was the most wonderful, kind horse that I was looking forward to learning from as we went up the levels eventing together."

Tinks's mother, Netia Walker, told the Mail that Benny was "the Brad Pitt of horses to us". She said: "My daughter could have been killed, we have lost her best horse and have another one that is so traumatised we can't ride her on the roads."

‌



Tink's furious family said they want justice after Wiltshire Police reportedly wrote to the teen five months after the incident. The force reportedly said "there is sufficient evidence to bring a prosecution against the alleged offending driver" but she had been offered a "safe and considerate driving course" to "re-educate" the driver.

The teenager's solicitor Cathryn Godfrey, of Irwin Mitchell, has started proceedings against the driver. Hannah Bradley, of Aria Grace Law, is suing on behalf of Benny's owners - one of which is Tink's grandmother - for the loss of a prizewinning horse said to be worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.

A spokesman for the driver and her company, which owned the car, said they were "deeply saddened by the death of Benny". The statement said: "The incident was a terrible accident, and our team are extremely distressed by what occurred."

Article continues below

The teenager will be racing at Newbury, on November 5, to raise money for the the British Horse Society’s (BHS) Dead Slow road safety campaign.

In a JustGiving page, the teen wrote: "I am hoping to raise awareness of road safety and stop what happened to us happening to someone else. It was devastating and should not have happened." The Mirror has contacted Wiltshire Police for comment.

You can donate to the fundraiser here.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies.
