Sports.title: Tim Tszyu vs Erislandy Lara WBA Title Fight Announced in Australia
Sports.content:
Tszyu secured the middleweight title shot by defeating Errol Spence Jr and will pursue a championship in a second division.

Tim Tszyu will challenge Erislandy Lara for the WBA middleweight title in Australia. Promoters have not announced the fight date, host city, venue or broadcaster.

The matchup sends Tszyu back into a championship fight after he outpointed Errol Spence Jr in Sydney in July. That victory extended his winning streak to three bouts and lifted his record to 28-3 with 18 knockouts.

Tszyu will remain at the 160-pound limit rather than return to super welterweight.

“At 160 I feel strong, I feel sharp and I feel dangerous. Middleweight is my division now. Spence was just the appetiser,” Tszyu said in the official announcement.

Tszyu Targets Championship in Second Division

Tszyu previously captured the WBO super welterweight title. Dethroning Lara would add a middleweight championship to his record and make him the first member of the Tszyu family to claim world titles in two weight classes.

His father, Kostya Tszyu, unified the junior welterweight division and captured every world championship of his career at 140 pounds.

“I’ve carried the Tszyu name my whole life. It’s a privilege and it’s pressure. This is my chance to write a chapter that belongs to me, and it’s the legacy defining moment of my career,” Tszyu said.

Jeff Fenech will command Tszyu’s corner for the title challenge. The former three-division champion joined Tszyu’s team in April 2026 and guided him through the Spence victory.

Lara Brings WBA Belt to Australia

Lara enters the matchup with a 32-3-3 record and 19 knockouts. The Cuban southpaw captured the WBA “Regular” middleweight belt in 2021 before the organization elevated him to full champion in 2023.

The 43-year-old has completed four successful title defenses and has never lost by stoppage as a professional. He also previously captured WBA championships at super welterweight.

Lara’s title reign and southpaw craft give Tszyu a seasoned champion to crack. Tszyu will bring pressure, body punching and home support into his bid to seize the belt.

Promoters expect to announce the date, location, ticket information and broadcast details in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II Preview & Prediction
Sports.content:
Coming up this Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, in a heavyweight championship showdown that will be streamed live worldwide exclusively on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois puts his title on the line in a highly anticipated immediate rematch against former champion Fabio Wardley.

BUY Dubois-Wardley 2 on DAZN

The heavyweight landscape is absolute chaos right now, turning into the Wild West ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts. With the rest of the division fighting over the pieces, the stakes could not be any higher. For Dubois, a victory confirms that his reign is the real deal and cements his standing as one of the premier heavyweights in the world. For Wardley, it is entirely about redemption – proving his storybook run was no fluke and reclaiming the world title he worked so hard to win.

Their first encounter just five months ago in Manchester was an absolute barnburner. Wardley stunned everyone early, scoring two dramatic knockdowns and pushing Dubois to the brink. But Dubois weathered the early storm, leaned on his piston-like jab, and systematically took over before halting Wardley in the 11th round.

Heading into Saturday’s return bout, the prevailing consensus is that Wardley shot his bolt, and Dubois will simply repeat the feat. Most observers are writing the former champion off completely. But is it really that simple? If Wardley makes the necessary tactical adjustments, can he pull off the upset?

Who will win the upcoming heavyweight championship rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner will contemplate the question while providing a quick preview and official prediction. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: Chris Mannix Questions Jai Opetaia’s Return To Cruiserweight
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia could cash in on a massive heavyweight payday against Deontay Wilder, but that detour could easily backfire once he returns to cruiserweight. Packing on size for Wilder only to strip it off for David Benavidez is the exact trap Chris Mannix sees ahead.

Discussing the fight with Sergio Mora, Mannix estimated Opetaia might scale around 210 to 212 pounds at heavyweight. His real concern centers on what happens if the Australian tries dropping back to 200 to meet Benavidez within six months.

“Adding that weight, adding that muscle, and then like within six months later dropping back down to 200 to fight the toughest opponent you could possibly face in the cruiserweight division. I think there’s a little bit of risk there as well,” said Mannix.

Mannix pointed to Roy Jones Jr.’s struggles after jumping to heavyweight and cutting back to light heavyweight. While Opetaia’s weight jump would be much smaller, Mannix questioned how easily the Australian could shed that newly built muscle at 31 years old.

That reality makes camp preparation for Wilder critical. Opetaia has to determine how much extra size he genuinely requires against a faded puncher whose work rate has fallen off. Bulking up recklessly could leave him facing an agonizing weight cut before dealing with Benavidez’s relentless pressure.

Mora favors Wilder as an opponent because the former champion scales lighter than most modern heavyweights. He believes Opetaia’s movement would thoroughly confuse the aging veteran, delivering far more mainstream eyes than an ordinary cruiserweight title defense.

Mannix agreed on the financial appeal, calling it “a ton of money” and “a ton of visibility.” Even so, he warned that Wilder’s right hand remains an eraser regardless of career decline.

A bout with Benavidez is still just a possibility rather than a signed deal. If that remains the target, Opetaia cannot focus entirely on handling Wilder. His team must plan the weight management carefully so he can drop back to 200 pounds at peak strength.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Expects More Defenses Before Rafael Espinoza
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa has his sights set on Rafael Espinoza for a featherweight unification, though he admits fans might need to wait through a few more title defenses first. The delay sounds less about finding willing rivals and more about cooking the commercial appeal until it hits a boil.

First, Figueroa has business to handle on Saturday when he puts his WBA belt on the line against Tomoki Kameda. Espinoza sits at the top of his wish list right after that, even if calling for the fight doesn’t mean it lands immediately.

“[Espinoza] is the No. 1 in our division,” Figueroa said to The Ring, describing their potential meeting as a fight-of-the-year candidate.

Figueroa called Espinoza the number one guy in the division, telling The Ring that a clash between them would easily contend for fight of the year.

You can see the appeal for an inside grinder who loves breaking opponents down. Espinoza brings towering height and relentless activity, meaning Figueroa would have to walk through heavy fire just to cut the distance and work. Neither man would ever have to go looking for action.

The frustrating part for fight fans is Figueroa’s belief that promoters will keep the titleholders on separate tracks to build their profiles. In his view, he might need one or two extra defenses before those unification bouts actually materialize.

The business logic makes sense on paper. Keep winning, build the brand, and give promoters bigger numbers to sell once the belts finally collide. Still, every unnecessary detour opens the door to an upset, a bad cut, or endless delays that wreck the whole plan.

Figueroa targeting Espinoza definitely gives fans something exciting to look past Kameda for. At the same time, it makes you wonder how much more buildup a fight really needs when both guys hold world titles and their ring styles already guarantee pure fireworks.

For now, this is just Figueroa reading the landscape rather than an official plan on the calendar. Nothing is signed with Espinoza. His only real job this weekend is taking care of Kameda; anything after that just determines how long everyone has to wait for the showdown he wants.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Overrates Ben Whittaker After Wallace Struggles
Sports.content:
Paulie Malignaggi’s praise for Ben Whittaker is running ahead of his performances. Calling him an “amazing talent” is difficult to square with how he struggled once Conor Wallace refused to play along with the showboating.

Whittaker had been getting away with those antics against the lesser opposition Matchroom and Boxxer put in front of him. Wallace was his first quality opponent, and the tricks that looked impressive against overmatched fighters didn’t work nearly as well.

“I think Whittaker is a tremendous talent, an amazing talent, but he’s got some things to work on,” Malignaggi told Boxing King Media. “At a world-class level, there are things he’s got to fix if he’s going to be successful.”

Wallace exposed how much work remains. Whittaker struggled under pressure late, and there is an argument that he should have lost. The falls that went uncounted as knockdowns and the repeated holding he was allowed to get away with helped him survive with a decision.

That wasn’t simply a case of the entertainment falling flat. Whittaker needed answers when Wallace kept coming, and too often his answer was to grab. Making lesser opponents miss is one thing. Keeping a quality fighter off you when tired is another.

Malignaggi understands why Whittaker’s approach invites a harsh reaction when things go wrong.

“If you’re going to sell the sizzle, you got to sell the steak,” he said. “Ben Whittaker sells the sizzle a lot.”

Paulie argues that the showboating doubles the criticism when Whittaker leaves people disappointed. That is fair, but it doesn’t explain the scale of his praise. Against Wallace, Whittaker showed weaknesses that better light heavyweights could punish even more severely.

Whittaker has ability, but the Wallace fight gave us more reason to question his readiness than celebrate his gifts. Malignaggi believes there is an exceptional fighter there. Whittaker still has to prove it against opponents who can make him pay for his mistakes.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Captures His First World Title
Sports.content:
Chicago, Illinois – Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (20-0, 13 KOs) captured the vacant WBA lightweight world title Saturday night by defeating “Prince” Lucas Bahdi (20-1, 15 KOs at the Wintrust Arena.

Bahdi proved much more difficult than expected. Schofield told the media after the fight that he had surprising power: “I didn’t expect him to have as much power as he did. I was kinda sleeping on his power until he caught me, but then once he caught me I kinda want to get that back, but I was like what’s more important, showing I got ego or going to get the world title.”

Floyd won a unanimous decision victory but appeared much closer than what it was scored officially: Alfredo Gallardo had it 119-108, Dave DeJonge judged it 116-110, and Steve Weisfeld scored it the closest at 115-111.

Both fighters scored a knockdown, but the difference was in Schofield’s ability to land punches and utilize lateral movement effectively to evade Bahdi’s counterattack, which won him the fight. Lucas struggled with Floyd’s movement, saying, “He was really quick on his feet. He wouldn’t stop moving all f**king night. He didn’t want to engage, but he fought a smart fight.” Schofield outlanded Bahdi 117 to 74 in total punches landed, connecting on 37.2 percent of his power punches. Lucas was limited offensively and was only able to land 23.5 percent of his total punches (Compubox). It was a tough match for Kid Austin, but ultimately his tactical boxing won the match.

Floyd stated after the fight that he’s dedicated his life to boxing and that becoming a world champion was always a dream he strived for. Now that he’s become world champion, he’ll take some time to rest and assess who’s next for him. WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason has expressed interest in unifying and would like to fight Schofield in the near future. There’s also recently crowned WBC lightweight champion William Zepeda, who is also promoted by Golden Boy and would be the easiest fight to make in terms of negotiating a deal between fighters of the same promotional stable.

As to what promoter Oscar De La Hoya has in mind for the two, it remains to be seen. A fight between any of the lightweight champions would be highly entertaining and competitive, as all the current fighters are skillful. Shakur Stevenson took to X and provided his own personal assessment of the fight, posting, “A C-level fighter beat an F-level fighter!!” However, Kid Austin posted his own post stating, in essence, that the ship has sailed on that and would instead pursue fights against Zepeda and Gary Russell. Shakur Stevenson appears to have his eyes set on a super fight match against Devin Haney. As for Floyd, if he pursues a unification match against any of the other lightweight champions, he’ll begin an interesting championship reign.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Sees Power as Sebastian Fundora’s Weakness
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman claims raw one-punch power offers the only realistic avenue to stop Sebastian Fundora, yet his own loss exposed the weakness of that approach. Fundora had him backpedaling from the opening bell, reducing him to full flight, defensive shelling, and wild, sporadic lunges instead of any organized attack.

That reality presents a massive hurdle for Jaron “Boots” Ennis if they meet in the ring. Carrying fight-ending power only solves part of the puzzle. Ennis must find a way to unleash that heat while navigating the endless jabs and relentless flurries that neutralized Thurman.

“Anybody who’s going to really beat Fundora, it’s best to have that one-punch ability,” Thurman said to Fighthype.

He questions whether anyone can easily outbox Fundora over twelve rounds. The towering southpaw brings relentless stamina, immense work rate, and superior reach, trapping rivals in defensive shells for long stretches.

“He’ll throw a five-punch combo, and then he’ll get back to his jab, and then where’s your offense?” Thurman noted.

Thurman lived that nightmare in the ring. For most of the bout, he retreated under heavy fire, absorbing punishment as Fundora dictated every exchange. The sporadic power shots Thurman threw did nothing to slow the onslaught. He could never plant his feet long enough to turn his power into a true equalizer. Thurman did not test Fundora’s chin; he did not test his gas tank, and he barely tested his guard.

Hunting strictly for one massive counter can backfire against someone with Fundora’s dimensions. A power puncher risks losing minutes off the clock, hoping for a lapse that never arrives while Fundora banks points behind his jab. One whiff on a counter, and the cycle of absorbing incoming combos starts right back up.

Thurman did spot a technical flaw, however. He noted that Fundora often drops his hands instead of returning them to his chin, even if his sheer length makes exploiting that lapse tricky.

Ennis has to explode across the pocket instantly, capitalizing on those defensive gaps before the jab resets. Thurman respects Boots’ lightning speed along with his lethal killer instinct, but connecting with that first clean bomb remains the ultimate test. Fundora smothered Thurman’s offense from distance, and Boots faces the heavy task of finding room where none existed before.

Sports.title: Bill Haney Turns Up Pressure on Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Bill Haney is calling on Shakur Stevenson to back up his public words regarding a 145-pound clash with Devin Haney. Bill confirmed that Devin accepts the weight limit with zero rehydration restrictions attached.

With November 28 in Atlanta being discussed as the proposed date, the two sides still have work to do before the fight becomes official. Bill’s frustration is that Shakur’s public response made the weight issue look settled, yet they’re still waiting for a completed agreement.

“I think he came out and he said done deal at 145.0. So stand on it,” Bill said to 78SPORTSTV.

That puts pressure on Shakur to explain what remains unresolved. Accepting a weight publicly gives fans reason to expect the fight, especially when the other side says it accepts the same number. It doesn’t mean the date, money, and every other contract term have been agreed upon.

Bill made Devin’s position on the weight clear.

“145.0 cool with us. No hydration, no none of that. Straight up 145 cool with us.”

Removing a rehydration cap gives Devin full freedom to bulk back up after making 145. That reality presents serious tactical considerations for Shakur, though Bill stopped short of confirming whether both teams have formally agreed to that specific term.

Addressing how Devin is handling the prolonged talks, Bill brushed off the holdup as familiar territory.

“I think that the people now get a chance to see who’s really about it and who’s just talking,” he noted.

Bill also declined to get drawn into a discussion about Liam Paro. His focus remains on Shakur, and he said he isn’t trying to kill the fight.

The approaching proposed date makes the wait harder to ignore. A November 28 event would leave limited time to complete negotiations, promote the card, and prepare for an opponent of this level. Bill wants movement now, but the interview leaves the key question unanswered: what still needs to be settled before both fighters sign?

Ghana News.title: Haruna Iddrisu calls for limits on annual university accommodation fee increases
Ghana News.content:
Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu

Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has proposed a framework to regulate annual increases in accommodation charges at public universities, suggesting that adjustments could be guided by inflation and set within a range of five to 10 per cent.

He called for a committee to examine accommodation costs and recommend permissible annual increases to Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson under the Fees and Charges Act.

Speaking in a media interview, Mr Iddrisu expressed concern about high rents and said a defined adjustment mechanism could help make university accommodation costs more predictable.

“We do not support exorbitant rent prices being charged across the country,” he said.

“It is my view that we should constitute a committee to advise the Minister of Finance before he proceeds with the Fees and Charges Act on what percentage increase is permissible each year.”

The Minister suggested that prevailing economic conditions should inform any recommended adjustment.

“We can say, for instance, take inflation as a guide, 5 to 10 per cent increase annually,” he added.

The proposed committee would assess an appropriate benchmark for increases, with the aim of limiting arbitrary or disproportionate adjustments to accommodation charges.

The five to 10 per cent range remains a suggestion by the minister, rather than an approved cap.

Ghana News.title: Wealth Over Water: How Galamsey Is Threatening Ghana’s Water Security
Ghana News.content:
“Illegal mining ravages Ghana’s forest reserves.”

Ghana is Africa’s top gold producer. But as the country digs deeper for gold, it is confronting a different and potentially more consequential scarcity: clean water.

A new visual analysis by researcher and data visualisation analyst Fatah Maltaba Abass, titled Wealth Over Water: A Visual Analysis of Water Security and Environmental Governance Impacts of Illegal Gold Mining in Ghana, brings together data from the Water Resources Commission (WRC), Ghana Water Limited, COCOBOD, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Pure Earth, the World Gold Council and peer-reviewed studies.

The analysis maps a growing tension at the heart of Ghana’s resource economy: the country is generating wealth from gold while putting some of the natural resources that support its population, agriculture and industry under increasing pressure.

One of the clearest examples is water.

Scientists at the CSIR-Water Research Institute reported in August 2026 that about 60% of Ghana’s water bodies are polluted, with illegal mining identified as a major contributor alongside agriculture, industrial activity, household waste and other human activities. The researchers warned that some affected water bodies could be difficult to restore even if the pollution stopped immediately.

That distinction matters. Galamsey is not the only source of Ghana’s water pollution — but in several mining-affected basins, its impact is particularly severe.

A country moving closer to water stress

The pressure is not coming from pollution alone. Ghana’s renewable water availability per person has fallen from about 3,000 cubic metres annually in the 1960s to 1,650 cubic metres today, according to the Ministry of Works, Housing and Water Resources.

The figure is below the 1,700 cubic metres per person threshold commonly used to indicate water stress.

At the same time, Ghana’s population has grown from roughly seven million people in 1960 to more than 30 million today. The implication is straightforward: there is less renewable water available per person, while demand continues to rise.

The Wealth Over Water analysis warns that continued deterioration could eventually push Ghana towards a future where it has to consider importing water. That should be treated as a warning scenario rather than a formal government forecast.

When rivers become too dirty to treat

The deterioration is visible in Ghana’s river systems. Turbidity — a measure of the amount of suspended material in water — has reached extraordinary levels in some mining-affected rivers.

The analysis records readings of 94,800 NTU on the Ayensu, 64,000 NTU on the Birim and up to 32,000 NTU on the Pra. Other affected rivers include the Offin and Ankobra. The figures are not simply an environmental concern. They directly affect the cost and efficiency of producing drinking water.

Ghana Water Limited has previously reported that extreme turbidity can force it to lose up to 50% of water during treatment, compared with a normal loss rate of about 5%.

More polluted raw water requires more treatment chemicals and can increase operational and maintenance costs. In some cases, the problem becomes severe enough to threaten the continued operation of treatment plants.

There have, however, been measurable improvements at some locations following enforcement operations. The analysis records turbidity reductions of 70% to 90% at selected monitoring points, including Densu/Nsawam.

The broader picture remains troubling: large sections of the country's water resources continue to face contamination pressure.

The heavy metals behind the concern

The problem is not only mud. Research cited in the analysis identifies heavy metals including arsenic, lead and mercury in mining-affected environments.

Some studies have reported arsenic concentrations as high as 330 times national standards in specific contaminated locations, while lead and mercury have been recorded at levels many times above applicable safety limits. These figures need to be interpreted carefully.

They are site-specific measurements from contaminated locations, not evidence that Ghana’s entire water system contains those concentrations. But they illustrate the severity of contamination that can occur around poorly regulated mining and processing sites.

Mercury is particularly important because it can enter aquatic food chains and eventually reach people through fish consumption.

Cocoa is paying a price too

The damage does not stop at the riverbank. Galamsey has increasingly encroached on cocoa-growing areas, particularly in some of Ghana’s major producing regions. COCOBOD has reported that illegal mining has affected 81% of cocoa farmland in the Eastern Region, 74% in Western and 68% in Ashanti in areas assessed.

The impacts include destroyed cocoa trees, early pod dropping, wilting and yellowing leaves and reduced yields. But Ghana’s cocoa production decline should not be attributed entirely to illegal mining.

Weather conditions, swollen shoot disease, ageing farms and other structural challenges have also contributed significantly to the industry's recent difficulties. The distinction is important because the data show galamsey as one component of a wider cocoa production crisis, rather than a single explanation for it.

The risk to farmland, however, is immediate: once a productive cocoa farm has been excavated, restoring it is far more difficult than preventing its destruction.

From shovels to excavators

The scale of the environmental damage has also changed as mining has become increasingly mechanized. In 2024, Ghana imported GH¢6.2 billion worth of excavators, according to the Lands Minister, making the machines one of the country's largest import categories. The government subsequently introduced measures to track excavators and prevent their diversion into illegal mining.

The significance is simple. An excavator can disturb an area of land in hours that would take individuals with basic tools considerably longer to work. That changes galamsey from a collection of small pits into a potentially large-scale landscape transformation

By March 2026, the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) said its operations had resulted in the seizure of 94 excavators, the destruction of nearly 3,000 illegal mining sites and 237 arrests.

The figures demonstrate the scale of enforcement activity. They also raise another question: How much does Ghana spend fighting galamsey, and how much of that expenditure translates into lasting environmental recovery?

When the pollution reaches the food chain

The environmental damage can eventually become a food-safety issue. The analysis highlights studies reporting elevated concentrations of lead and mercury in food samples from mining-affected areas, including cassava, leafy vegetables, tomatoes and river fish. Among the reported results, lead in some tomato samples reached 48 times the applicable safety limit.

Again, these should not be interpreted as evidence that Ghanaian food generally contains dangerous levels of heavy metals. They are findings from specific samples and locations.

But they demonstrate a potential pathway particularly concerning for communities that depend directly on rivers for fishing, irrigation and household use.

Contaminated mining area → polluted water or soil → crops and aquatic life → human consumption.

The forest-water connection

The destruction also extends upstream. Forest reserves are important to Ghana’s water security because forest ecosystems help protect watersheds, regulate water flows and reduce erosion. That made the controversy surrounding L.I. 2462 particularly significant.

The 2022 legislative instrument created a framework under which mining could take place in protected forest reserves under certain conditions. It subsequently became the focus of sustained public opposition before being revoked by government in 2025.

Why the cycle is difficult to break

The Wealth Over Water analysis estimates that more than one million people are directly involved in artisanal and small-scale mining, with millions more dependent on the sector. For some miners, daily earnings can significantly exceed what is available from alternative livelihoods.

This is another reason galamsey has proved difficult to eliminate: the economics work for some of the people involved

That creates a difficult enforcement equation. A mining site can be destroyed. An excavator can be seized. A miner can be arrested. But if the economic incentive remains, another operation can emerge elsewhere. This is why the long-term response cannot rely solely on raids and equipment seizures.

It also requires action against illegal financing and gold-trading networks, effective regulation of legitimate small-scale mining, alternative livelihoods and sustained environmental monitoring.

The bill Ghana does not see

Ghana’s gold industry generates foreign exchange, employment and government revenue. But illegal and environmentally destructive mining creates another bill — one that does not appear neatly in the national budget. It is reflected in higher water-treatment costs, damaged cocoa farms, degraded river systems, lost agricultural land, threatened fisheries and environmental restoration.

Potentially in the rising cost of securing clean water for a growing population. That is the central tension captured by Wealth Over Water. Ghana is rich in gold, but the natural systems that support the wider economy are not limitless.

The country’s renewable water availability has already fallen to 1,650 cubic metres per person, below the commonly used water-stress threshold. At the same time, scientists estimate that about 60% of Ghana’s water bodies are polluted, with galamsey among the major contributors.

The question, therefore, is no longer simply how much gold Ghana can extract. It is how much of the country’s water, farmland, forests and ecological wealth can be consumed in the process — and who ultimately pays for the damage.

Ghana News.title: LA 2028: Black Queens pumped up for second leg of Mauritius tie
Ghana News.content:
Ghana will look to wrap up qualification in the second round of the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games when they host Mauritius in the second leg at the Essipong Stadium on Tuesday.

The Black Queens go into the fixture with a commanding advantage, having beaten their opponents 3-0 in the first meeting last week, Thursday, at the Côte d’Or National Sports Complex in Mauritius.

Kim Lars Bjorkegren's side are chasing Olympic Games football for the first time, having failed to reach the heights since the introduction of women's football at the summer games in 1996.

The winner of the tie over two legs will advance into the next stage of the competition, where they will face one of Uganda or Zambia in the third round of the qualifiers.

Mauritius, on the other hand, will be playing for pride and will hope to cause an upset away from home after a difficult first leg.

Björkegren’s team held their final training session at the Essipong Stadium on Monday evening, with the Swedish trainer going on to address the media.

The coach is expected to maintain the core of the side that won in Mauritius but could also rotate to give opportunities to other players.

The match is scheduled for Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at 15:00 GMT at the Essipong Sports Stadium in Sekondi-Takoradi.

Ghana News.title: Standards are not Seasonal: What the EC appointments teach both sides
Ghana News.content:
On Monday, 12 October 2026, President Mahama swore in two new Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission, Emelia Afi Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah. They fill the vacancies left by Dr Bossman Eric Asare, who resigned with effect from 31 July, and Samuel Tettey, who retired. At the ceremony, the President told them he expected "no preferential treatment" from the Commission for himself, his party or his government.

Within hours, the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) was on the attack. Its Director of Communications, Dennis Miracles Aboagye, described one of the appointees as an openly partisan operative, a campaign team member of a political party, and said the appointment undermines the independence of the Commission's leadership. The presidency has answered that she is not, and has never been, a card-bearing member of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), and that her involvement in campaign activities came from her advocacy for gender inclusion. I have not been able to verify either side's claim independently. Party membership is a matter of record, and the public deserves a clear answer.

I do not write this article to settle that dispute. I write because what we are watching is older than this appointment, and it will keep happening until we decide that politics needs standards that do not change with the seat a party occupies.

The same argument, in different mouths

Ghanaians have heard this argument before, with the speakers reversed.

In April 2023, the NDC, then in opposition, wrote to the Council of State asking it to reconsider its advice on two appointees to the Electoral Commission under President Akufo-Addo, Hajia Salima Ahmed Tijani and Dr Peter Appiahene. The party described one of them as a card-bearing NPP member and warned that the Commission's reputation would suffer unless the appointments were reconsidered. The NPP government of the day defended its choices. In 2019, the NDC's General Secretary went further and accused the then Deputy Chairman, Dr Bossman Asare, of acting as an NPP sympathiser after he spoke publicly in favour of the referendum on the election of district chief executives. The argument then was that a deputy commissioner must act as a neutral referee.

Read those statements today and the roles have simply been exchanged. The NDC now defends an appointee against the charge of partisanship, and the NPP now delivers the speech the NDC once gave. The Director of Communications says an appointment like this has never happened before in our democratic history. The record suggests that both parties have been accused of it, and that both parties have defended it when the accusation was aimed at them.

That pattern should trouble every citizen, whichever party they support.

Why the opposition's voice changes

There is a simple human explanation. In opposition, a party sees power from the outside. It sees the abuse of appointments, the sidelining of institutions and the quiet rewarding of loyalists, and it speaks about these things with real conviction. Then it wins, and the view changes. The loyalists are now friends who are qualified, the appointments are now reasonable judgement calls, and the critics are now people who are just playing politics.

The reverse is just as common. A party that spent eight years defending its own appointments leaves office and suddenly discovers the virtue of neutrality, independence and clean process. Its principles seem to arrive on the day it loses the keys.

I am not saying politicians are insincere. Many are sincere in both positions, which is exactly the problem. When a principle is held only by those who lack power, it was never a principle. It was a tactic.

Why the Electoral Commission is different

Some will say that all governments appoint people they trust, and that is true. Presidents appoint ministers, ambassadors and board chairs who share their outlook, and nobody is surprised. The Electoral Commission is a different kind of institution, and Article 46 of the Constitution explains why: it states that the Commission shall not be subject to the direction or control of any person or authority in the performance of its functions.

The Commission is the referee of the contest in which the President's own party competes. A referee does not have to be a person without opinions, but must be someone whom both teams can trust, and the perception of fairness matters almost as much as fairness itself. A losing candidate who believes the referee was on the other side will not accept the result. Ghana has already seen how heated the arguments about electoral credibility can become. We do not need more suspicion built into the system before the next election cycle begins.

This is why the question to ask about any appointment to the Commission is not only whether the person is qualified. It is also whether a reasonable citizen from the other side could look at that person and believe the contest will be fair. If the answer is no, the government has chosen the narrow route when a wider one was available. Dr Asamoah, for example, comes with more than seventeen years of experience across electoral administration, public service, law, accountancy and teaching, including earlier service within the Commission itself. That kind of record is what makes an appointment easier to defend.

What each side owes the country

To the government, I say this: the President's own words at the swearing-in set the bar. He asked the deputies to be impartial and to protect the right of Ghanaians to choose their leaders freely. That standard applies first to the person who made the appointments. If there is a real doubt about an appointee's independence, the answer is not to attack the critics. It is to answer the specific allegations openly, publish the evidence of the person's record, and let the public judge. A government that once complained loudly about partisan appointments to the Commission has more reason than most to hold itself to the standard it demanded.

To the opposition, I say this: your criticism will be taken more seriously if it is consistent. If you believe partisan appointments to the Commission are wrong, then say so about your own past appointments as well. Acknowledge what was said about the appointees under your government and explain what you would do differently. Otherwise, your complaint, however valid in substance, will be dismissed as the temporary anger of those out of office. And let the allegations be accurate. Where a claim is disputed, say what you know, say what you do not, and allow the person concerned to be judged by what she actually does in office.

To both, I say that the accusation "your appointee is a partisan" should never again be a statement whose truth depends on who is speaking.

What would real standards look like?

Standards need to be written down, because memory is too short and convenience too strong. Parliament and the political parties could agree on a plain code for appointments to constitutional bodies such as the Electoral Commission: a stated cooling-off period for people who have held party office or played prominent campaign roles, public disclosure of any party membership or campaign involvement, and a transparent vetting process in which the Council of State publishes its reasoning. None of this requires a constitutional amendment to begin, and all of it can be proposed by a party that is in opposition today and might be in government tomorrow, which is precisely why both parties should want it.

The test is easy to state. Before criticising an appointment, ask what you said when your own side made a similar one. Before defending an appointment, ask what you said when the other side made it. If your answers differ, you do not have a position. You have an interest.

The country that outlasts its parties

Governments change in Ghana, and that is something to be proud of. The NDC and the NPP have each held power and each lost it, and one day each will again. The institutions they pass between are the only things that remain constant, and they stay trusted only if each side leaves them in better shape than it found them.

We should therefore judge the new deputies by what they do. If they act fairly, show restraint and treat every party alike, the doubts will fade. If they do not, the opposition will have been right and the government will have wasted public trust it could ill afford to spend.

Either way, the larger lesson stands. Standards are not seasonal. They do not belong to the party in power or the party in opposition. They belong to the people, and the people are watching who keeps them when keeping them is costly.

Ghana News.title: King Mohammed VI urges private sector to create youth jobs and spread benefits of growth
Ghana News.content:
Morocco’s King Mohammed VI has urged businesses to increase investment and create more jobs for young people, while calling for the benefits of economic growth to be shared more fairly across the country.

Addressing Parliament at the opening of the 12th legislature, the King outlined a new phase of development aimed at strengthening Morocco’s economy, reducing regional inequalities and improving citizens’ living conditions.

He called on the private sector to play a greater role through productive investment, innovation, exports and sustainable job creation. Economic transformation, he stressed, requires businesses to complement state policies and reforms by expanding productive activities.

Youth employment was a prominent development priority. The King advocated an integrated approach linking education, skills development and access to economic opportunities, with training better aligned to labour-market needs.

The aim is to give young people clearer prospects, support social mobility and ensure equal opportunities, while responding to their aspirations for freedom, dignity and stability.

The King also emphasised that sustained growth should translate into better public services and tangible improvements in everyday life. Reducing disparities between regions and distributing economic gains more equitably would be central to that effort.

To support Morocco’s competitiveness and resilience, he called for new national strategies covering water, energy and food security, industrial development, the digital economy and artificial intelligence.

He also urged faster action to establish strategic reserves and secure supplies of essential goods, helping the country reduce external dependence and withstand crises.

On territorial reform, the King called for an end to delays in implementing advanced regionalisation and administrative deconcentration. He urged the transfer of powers, staff and financial resources to regions and provinces so that policies could better reflect local needs and stimulate investment.

Turning to migration, he announced that Morocco would present its partners with a new strategic vision based on co-development, economic competitiveness and regional stability. He said international commitments should rest on reciprocity and respect for Morocco’s sovereignty.

The King reminded parliamentarians that their mandate carried both political responsibility and a moral commitment to citizens, urging them to fulfil their legislative and oversight duties and help turn national ambitions into concrete results.

Ghana News.title: KGL U17 Colts 2026: Greater Accra win title after penalties win over Western Region
Ghana News.content:
Greater Accra Region were crowned champions of the 2026 KGL Foundation Inter-Regional U17 Colts Championship after defeating Western Region 5-4 on penalties following a goalless draw in Sunday’s final at the Ghanaman Soccer Centre of Excellence in Prampram.

In a tense and closely contested encounter, neither side could find the breakthrough during regulation time, forcing the final to be decided from the penalty spot. Greater Accra held their nerve in the shootout to secure their maiden title and bring an eight-day championship to a memorable conclusion.

The triumph marks a significant milestone for the capital region, which joins an illustrious list of past winners of the youth competition. Desmond Asare, who played a key role in Greater Accra’s campaign, was named Most Valuable Player of the final.

For Western Region, however, the defeat extended a painful run of near misses on the tournament’s biggest stage. Having reached the final for the third consecutive edition since 2024, they have now suffered back-to-back final defeats, following their loss to Ashanti Region in 2025.

Western Region lifted the trophy in 2024 but were unable to reclaim it, with Greater Accra ending their latest title challenge in dramatic fashion.

Prempeh Academy claim bronze

Earlier, Prempeh Elite Academy secured third place with a deserved 3-0 victory over Brong Ahafo in the third-place playoff at the GFA technical centre.

Thomas Asante delivered an outstanding performance, scoring twice, while Dennis Duah added the other goal to give the Kumasi-based academy a comfortable win.

Asante opened the scoring in the 20th minute before Duah doubled the advantage five minutes into the second half. Asante then completed his brace in the 74th minute to seal the emphatic victory and ensure Prempeh Elite Academy finished the tournament on a high.

Greater Accra join the Championship's roll of honour

The 2026 edition marked the sixth staging of the Inter-Regional U17 Colts Championship, which continues to provide a competitive platform for emerging football talent across Ghana.

MAL FC won the inaugural edition in 2021, followed by Great Corinthians in 2022. Ashanti Region claimed the title in 2023, before Western Region triumphed in 2024 and Ashanti Region returned to the summit in 2025.

Greater Accra’s victory adds a new name to the roll of honour and underlines the growing competitiveness of the tournament.

Sponsored by the KGL Foundation, the championship forms part of the Ghana Football Association’s Talent Development Scheme (TDS), which is designed to identify, develop and nurture the next generation of Ghanaian footballers.

The competition gives promising under-17 players the opportunity to demonstrate their technical ability, tactical understanding and potential while testing themselves against some of the country’s finest emerging talents.

As the curtain falls on the 2026 edition, Greater Accra celebrate a historic first title, while Western Region are left to reflect on another painful final defeat after three consecutive appearances on the championship’s biggest stage.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
