World.title: Palestine weekly: Gaza marks year of ‘ceasefire’ with more Israeli killing
World.content:
The Gaza “ceasefire” marked its first anniversary on October 10, but more than 100 humanitarian and human rights organisations said it exists “in name only”.

Islamic Relief noted that Israeli forces have killed or wounded a Palestinian in Gaza on average every 90 minutes since the ceasefire took effect.

Gaza’s Health Ministry put the toll since the truce at 1,493 killed and 5,299 wounded as of October 12, up from 1,460 a week earlier; the cumulative death toll since October 2023 stood at 74,382.

Among the Palestinians killed in Gaza over the past week:

Four Palestinians were killed in a drone strike near Panda Mall in western Gaza City on Saturday, which Israel said targeted members of Hamas’s Nukhba force.

Also on Saturday, eight-year-old Shahd al-Najjar was killed by Israeli fire that struck her inside her tent in western Gaza City.

Seven-year-old Jihad al-Ghandour died of wounds from a separate shooting near Jabalia camp north of Gaza City on Sunday.

A child and his mother were killed Thursday when Israeli warplanes struck a home in Gaza City’s al-Sabra neighbourhood after an evacuation warning.

A drone strike on a charging point west of Khan Younis killed four people on Sunday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

Two more men were killed in a strike near a mosque in al-Mawasi in the south on Monday.

In statements describing attacks, Israel’s military claimed several of those killed this week were Palestinian fighters.

The Israeli military said two men killed near the Jordanian Field Hospital were Islamic Jihad operatives; Wafa identified one as a recently released former prisoner.



It separately said a civil defence worker killed while responding to the wounded near Kamal Adwan Hospital in northern Gaza had been a Hamas sniper; Hamas rejected the claim, and it has not been independently verified.

Gaza’s health system continued its collapse:

Gaza’s Ministry of Health said that 44 percent of essential medicines are completely out of stock.

A Physicians for Human Rights Israel report found that a year into the ceasefire, not one of Gaza’s 36 hospitals is operating at full capacity.

More than 18,500 patients need medical evacuation and more than 1,000 have died waiting, according to the joint NGO statement.

The Health Ministry said this week that no patient had been permitted to leave through Rafah crossing in the last week.

Israeli forces have also continued pushing the so-called Yellow Line demarcating Israeli control further into residential Gaza City neighbourhoods this week, triggering fresh displacement.

One year into the ceasefire, the Board of Peace – Gaza’s transitional oversight body – has failed to meet most of its central commitments: no international stabilisation force has deployed, aid trucks are entering at roughly a third of the agreed rate, and Israel now controls nearly two thirds of the Strip — well above the roughly 50 percent it was supposed to retain before further withdrawal and a future handover of control to Palestinians.

Olive harvest under coordinated assault

The Palestinian olive harvest – traditionally a time of family and celebration – gathered pace as Israeli settlers and soldiers intensified efforts to disrupt it. Harvesters were killed, attacked and blocked, while isolated families faced dayslong settler sieges.

Pogrom attacks included:

On October 7, Ali Hassan Yasser al-Bazzari, 44, was shot dead when settlers and soldiers opened fire on olive pickers on farmland between Burqa and Ramin, northwest of Nablus in the occupied West Bank. At least 16 others were wounded during the pogrom, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said Israeli forces assaulted ambulance crews trying to reach the wounded olive pickers and briefly detained three paramedics. Soldiers later raided the nearby village and made arrests, while the settlers who carried out the attack marched past unimpeded.

The Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission recorded 19 settler attacks on Friday alone, another 12 on Saturday and 18 more on Sunday, according to Wafa.

The Israeli rights group Yesh Din had already documented 109 harvest-related settler incidents across 75 Palestinian communities in a 10-day period between September 27 and October 6.

The commission says settlers and soldiers have destroyed roughly 50,000 trees so far this year.



The attacks followed a familiar shape village to village, according to Wafa and field reports from local residents and activists:

Settlers in Qusra stole a farmer’s olives before bulldozing more than 50 of his trees.

In Birin, settlers from the recently established Adorim outpost set a dog on a 79-year-old woman harvesting nearby, hospitalizing her.

Settlers from the same outpost cut power to roughly 20 homes repeatedly over the week.

In al-Mughayyir, northeast of Ramallah, soldiers followed settlers into the village’s residential streets on Sunday, kicked an elderly woman trying to reach her home, and fired live rounds and tear gas into houses “without apparent reason,” according to Israeli field monitor Jonathan Pollack. The daily incursions are part of a monthslong campaign by settlers against villagers there.

At Deir Abu Mash’al, a solidarity harvest organised by the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission drew an attack by settlers in Area B that left eight people wounded, including a photojournalist shot in the thigh, Wafa reported.

Israeli forces frequently blocked the harvest, too. Soldiers used drone-mounted loudspeakers to drive farmers out of Wadi Abwein and turned pickers away in several locations elsewhere.

Israeli settlers’ own chat groups reveal how they frame such attacks in reverse — through a messianic lens, casting Palestinian harvesters reaching their own land in Deir Abu Mash’al as attempting to “seize” the land, and the olive harvest itself as cover for Palestinians gathering “intelligence” rather than picking olives that families have harvested there for generations. Settlers have been documented repeatedly stealing olives from Palestinians’ lands since harvesting unofficially started late last month.

Political jockeying ahead of elections

Once again, Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas postponed Palestinian legislative elections – this time to September, citing Israeli restrictions on election materials and observers entering Gaza and East Jerusalem, and ongoing settler violence. Mustafa Barghouti, of the Palestinian National Initiative, said the decision reflects that “everything is concentrated in the hands of the executive authority”, with no parliament or independent judiciary to check it.

In Israel, with high-stakes parliamentary elections scheduled for October 27, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said his alliance – made up predominantly of Palestinian citizens of Israel – was prepared to support a coalition against current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from outside government.

The support would be given in exchange for policy commitments, including a pathway to Palestinian statehood, The Times of Israel reported – a potential route to a majority that polls suggest neither bloc can reach without Arab party support.

Israeli authorities also began demolishing homes this week in al-Dahiya, an unrecognised Bedouin village in the Naqab, after a district court rejected a request to freeze the orders; roughly 60 homes face demolition.



In diplomatic news, the UK’s consulate in occupied East Jerusalem formally became a reduced “mission” after Israel’s deadline for its closure passed; it has long handled the UK’s relations with Palestinians.

World.title: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, PM says
World.content:
Two ships were hit in the attack, including the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which sustained damage.

Share Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, PM says on social media

Two ships have been hit in drone attacks off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, with one of them sinking, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

The Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which was sailing under a Maltese flag, was hit by three drones and damaged about 18 nautical miles (33km) off Bulgaria at about 1:30am on Tuesday (22:30 GMT on Monday), Radev said.

Radev said its 15-man crew, seven of them Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, was rescued. Five crew members received medical assistance, and no one was seriously injured.

He added that one crew member from the ship that sank was also rescued.

Radev called the incident “absolutely unacceptable”.

“Another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters,” he said in a televised address, adding, “I am due to speak with NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.”

Radev said there was no clear evidence of who carried out the attack, but “the outcome benefits” Russia and that the Russian ambassador would be summoned over the incident.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the attack on the ships.

“The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine,” she said.

“This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea,” she wrote on X.

“We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable,” von der Leyen added.



As a member of the NATO military alliance, Bulgaria holds a strategic position on the Black Sea, where Russia and Ukraine have vital ports.

The incident comes as concerns grow over hybrid attacks involving Russia.

Last week, drones hit two ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, causing one to sink. All 10 crew members from the ship that sank remain unaccounted for.

World.title: Emir says Qatar has shown resilience in the face of ‘exceptional events’
World.content:
Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani says Qatar has demonstrated its strength and cohesion.

Share Emir says Qatar has shown resilience in the face of ‘exceptional events’ on social media

Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani has told the Shura Council that the region has faced “exceptional events” during months of instability amid the United States-Israel war on Iran.

Speaking in the capital, Doha, on Tuesday, Sheikh Tamim said Qatar’s response had shown its resilience.

“Our country and the region have faced exceptional events that have once again proven the cohesion of state institutions,” the emir said.

Qatar has found itself caught up in the war, which began on February 28 and triggered a global energy crisis.

The Gulf state has been directly attacked by Iran on several occasions, including in March, when Tehran struck Qatar’s Ras Laffan gas facility, the world’s largest liquefied natural gas (LNG) production site.

Sheikh Tamim said Qatar had been able to absorb the consequences of the regional instability due to policies implemented before the war. The emir maintained that the Gulf Cooperation Council’s (GCC) security was non-negotiable.

“The security of Gulf Cooperation Council states and the preservation of their sovereignty are matters that cannot be compromised on,” he said.

The war on Iran has disrupted global supply routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blocked since the start of the conflict.

Sheikh Tamim said efforts to safeguard maritime routes must be increased.

“Efforts must be doubled to secure navigation in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz and to protect energy facilities and civilian infrastructure.”

Reporting from Doha, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi said Sheikh Tamim had used the address to reiterate Qatar’s preference for ending wars and resolving disagreements through peaceful dialogue, while reaffirming the country’s commitment to the Palestinian cause.



“He highlighted how the attacks on LNG facilities have effectively hurt Qatar’s capacity; it has hurt Qatar’s economy directly,” Basravi said.

“He also cautioned and said that ‘we should not be like we were before this crisis going forward.’ Certainly, a signal that will be taken seriously by those in this chamber; by people heading up institutions.

“If you read between the lines, the signal is clear: That they will lean into non-carbon-related industries.”

Sheikh Tamim said Qatar has invested more than $60bn across a variety of areas, including infrastructure projects, public-private partnerships and private sector investment.

Rashid Al-Mohanadi, vice president of the Center for International Policy Research, told Al Jazeera that Qatar has a history of “turning crises into opportunities”.

“In the last 10 years, Qatar has been through many challenges and usually the output is we become more resilient. The hope is that after this war, which has been very challenging on the population [and] on the economy, that Qatar will turn out stronger and more resilient,” Al-Mohanadi said.

World.title: Malaysia’s Firefly cancels flights to Singapore over haze from Indonesia
World.content:
Move comes as haze from Indonesian fires makes Singapore and Kuala Lumpur the world’s most polluted cities.

Share Malaysia’s Firefly cancels flights to Singapore over haze from Indonesia on social media

Firefly, a Malaysian low-cost airline, has extended the suspension of its flights between Kuala Lumpur and Singapore through Wednesday as smoke from fires in Indonesia continued to blanket the region.

The announcement came as IQAir, an air quality monitor, ranked Singapore and the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur as the world’s two most polluted cities on Tuesday.

Firefly said in a statement that flights between the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (SZB) near Kuala Lumpur and the Seletar Airport in Singapore (XSP) have been cancelled up to Wednesday due to “weather and haze conditions”.

It called the action a “proactive safety measure”.

The fires, mostly on the Indonesian islands of Sumatra and Borneo, are the country’s most intense in 11 years. They have been spurred by El Nino, a weather pattern expected to be among the strongest in four decades.

IQAir, a Swiss air quality monitoring company, said Air Quality Index in Singapore stood at 199 on Tuesday and 183 in Kuala Lumpur. Readings above 150 are generally considered unhealthy, and those above 300 are classified as hazardous.

Firefly, a subsidiary of Malaysia Aviation Group, which includes Malaysia Airlines, first announced the flight cancellations on October 10, citing “low visibility” due to the haze conditions.

Firefly said that affected passengers were being rebooked on Malaysia Airlines flights between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Singapore’s Changi Airport, subject to seat availability.

The Singapore government has reintroduced subsidised care for haze-related illnesses, as it last did in 2015, when smoke from Indonesian fires hung over the region for weeks.



In Malaysia, schools reopened in most states on Tuesday as air quality improved slightly, but they remain closed in three states, one federal territory and several districts.

Malaysia’s foreign minister, Mohamad Hasan, said on Monday that he would press for stronger regional mechanisms when foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meet next month.

“We already have an ASEAN mechanism for natural disasters, but haze is not included or classified as a natural disaster,” he told reporters in Sepang, according to Bernama, Malaysia’s state news agency.

The Philippines, which chairs the bloc this year, confirmed that the issue would be on the agenda.

“It’s in the agenda,” Dominic Xavier Imperial, a spokesman for the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs, said of the November meeting, which will precede the 49th ASEAN summit in Manila.

Mohamad, the Malaysian minister, said Indonesia had deployed about 60,000 personnel to fight the fires, but thick smoke had grounded 34 aircraft, including planes and helicopters.

Remote terrain and limited water supplies have also hindered the effort, he said, and cloud seeding is not possible without suitable rain clouds. He acknowledged Indonesia’s efforts but urged more effective action, citing the toll on Malaysian communities.

World.title: Imran Khan’s PTI braces to fight federal takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
World.content:
Islamabad says the PTI failed to lead the fight against armed groups, but analysts question the takeover.

Islamabad, Pakistan – The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party of jailed ex-Prime Minister Imran Khan is planning to legally challenge the federal government’s Sunday takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a province that the party governed.

Sheikh Waqas Akram, the PTI’s central information secretary, told Al Jazeera that the party would challenge the imposition of emergency laws – suspending civil liberties – and governor’s rule in the province in court on Tuesday. A petition had been drafted by a legal committee headed by PTI Secretary-General Salman Akram Raja, but Akram did not say whether it would be filed in the Supreme Court or the Federal Constitutional Court.

The federal government’s moves have emerged as Pakistan’s latest political flashpoint, with competing narratives from the government and the PTI, at a time when the party was in the middle of a delayed march towards Islamabad, aimed at pressuring authorities to release former PM Khan, who has been jailed for more than three years.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday justified the government’s moves by arguing that federal rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was needed for Pakistan to effectively combat “terrorism” in the province that shares a porous border with Afghanistan.

“No war can be won, however many resources you bring, whatever you do, until the government there leads it,” Naqvi said in Peshawar on Monday.

On Sunday, President Asif Ali Zardari imposed emergency rule and governor’s rule, suspending the PTI government in the northwestern province. The party has governed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa since 2013.



Sohail Afridi, the suspended chief minister, and some members of his cabinet have been taken into preventive custody, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry confirmed on Monday. Afridi had been leading the march towards Islamabad seeking to free Khan, and despite the setbacks to the party, PTI leaders said the protest was still on.

“The long march has not ended. But a historic crackdown against the party has begun,” Akram said.

The case for intervention

According to the proclamation signed on Sunday, the provincial government had “failed to demonstrate the ownership, will and intent to adequately deal with the menace of terrorism”.

“The federal government’s position is clearly described. ‘A deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’ as communicated after cabinet meeting. That’s the constitutional premise needed for imposition of emergency,” Aasiya Riaz, joint director of the independent political think tank the Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency (PILDAT), told Al Jazeera.

However, Hassan Abdullah Niazi, an adjunct faculty member at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS) and a lawyer based in Lahore, disputed that premise.

“If all of this was true, then KP would be in a state of anarchy, but we know that is not the case. It had a functioning legislature and executive that commanded the confidence of the people, hence this entire exercise is an unconstitutional move against provincial autonomy,” he told Al Jazeera.

A more detailed case was set out last month in a 14-page white paper presented in Islamabad by Ikhtiar Wali Khan, a political adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif from the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PMLN).

The paper pointed to rising police deaths, staff and equipment shortages in the provincial counterterrorism department, and spending priorities.

However, Akram rejected the charge that the PTI had failed to lead the fight.

He said the provincial government had paid 1.83 billion rupees ($6.6m) from its own funds to the families of more than 900 soldiers, police and paramilitary personnel killed fighting armed groups, a contribution he said no other province had made.

What Islamabad wanted

Naqvi said at a news conference in Islamabad on Sunday that the federal government had been involved in negotiations with the PTI on a proposed “sit-in” by the party in support of Khan.

“We have no problem with the sit-in. Do the sit-in as eagerly as you like; we have no issue with the sit-in. Our issue is entirely terrorism-related, and we want to get you on board on that,” he said.



Taimur Jhagra, a PTI leader and former provincial finance and health minister, said the talks with the government that the party had agreed to were meant to focus on Khan.

“It’s absurd that a negotiation about a protest movement to give Imran Khan Supreme Court-ordered medical and visitation rights becomes a negotiation about terrorism strategy,” he told Al Jazeera.

Naqvi also said the PTI had agreed during the talks that emergency rule should be imposed in 12 districts of the province.

Akram rejected that claim and said the party had refused. The party feared residents would bear the cost of military operations, he said.

“We said ‘No, this cannot be. You cannot do whatever you like with them. We took the votes from them. Tomorrow they will blame us: ‘You got us killed,’” he said.

Akram said the PTI negotiators referred the federal government’s proposal to Afridi, who rejected it.

Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar went further at Sunday’s news conference.

“This government, which has been suspended through a constitutional option, is responsible for the deaths of thousands of citizens of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he said, accusing Afridi’s PTI government of being hand in glove with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan – an armed group known as the Pakistan Taliban – and the Afghan Taliban.

There is no known or public evidence of any such links.

Security or politics?

According to a government white paper, 122 police personnel were killed in the province in the first half of this year, up from 63 during the same period in 2025.

Independent trackers also point to rising violence. The Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), an Islamabad-based think tank, recorded 556 violence-linked deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between July and September, up from 475 in the previous quarter and 311 in the one before.

Balochistan was hit harder. Deaths there rose by 213 percent to 829, making it the worst-affected province, according to CRSS.

The government says it acted because the provincial administration would not lead the fight against armed groups, but analysts disagree over the takeover’s purpose.

“I would say this decision is political, administrative and security. All three elements are present in it,” Zaigham Khan, an Islamabad-based political analyst, told Al Jazeera.

Ali Arqam, a longtime observer of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, disagreed.

“This is not really about security at all. It is basically a political move that they are just dressing up as some kind of administrative necessity,” he told Al Jazeera.

Jhagra said the government believed the takeover would break the PTI, but argued that people across the country still saw Khan as their leader.

“It is trying to solve for legitimacy,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to the government.

For his part, Federal Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said at a news conference in Islamabad on Sunday that the decision was a purely constitutional step.



A party under pressure

For the PTI, the immediate concerns are its leaders and the courts.

“There has been no contact. No one in the party has had any contact with the chief minister,” Akram said.

But the party remains widely popular, in the province and nationally.

At Monday’s meeting, Naqvi said results against “terrorism” would not come in a day. There would be ups and downs, he said, and harder times lay ahead.

But Arqam, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa observer, said Islamabad should be judged by the same measures as the PTI government.

“You test this government by looking at the exact same hard metrics: Does security actually improve, do the basic services get better, and do the promised fiscal resources finally show up?” he said.

World.title: Middle East and Central Asia’s economy to shrink in 2026 amid war, IMF says
World.content:
Iraq, Bahrain, Kuwait and Qatar face double-digit declines in GDP amid the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran.

Share Middle East and Central Asia’s economy to shrink in 2026 amid war, IMF says on social media

The economy of the Middle East and Central Asia is set to shrink in 2026 amid the fallout of the US-Israel war on Iran, with countries such as Kuwait and Qatar facing double-digit contractions, according to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The region’s gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to contract by 0.3 percent this year, a sharp downgrade from the 1.9 percent expansion projected in April, the IMF said in its latest economic outlook on Tuesday.

The IMF cited the prolonged disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for one-fifth of global oil supplies in peacetime, for the downgraded outlook.

Kuwait, Iraq and Qatar are forecast to have the most severe economic contractions, with their GDPs expected to shrink by 16.7 percent, 16 percent and 15.6 percent, respectively.

Bahrain’s GDP is forecast to contract by 11.3 percent, while Iran’s economy is projected to shrink by 7.6 percent.

Saudi Arabia, which has partially offset the hit to its energy sector by boosting oil exports through the East-West pipeline, is projected to record negative growth of 3.3 percent.

Kyrgyzstan is expected to have the strongest growth in the region, with GDP forecast to expand 9 percent.

The Middle East and Central Asia is the only region that is expected to experience negative growth in 2026.

Emerging and developing Asia’s GDP is forecast to grow 5.1 percent, while the economies of Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean are projected to expand 4.5 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively.



The United States and China, the world’s two largest economies, are forecast to register growth of 2.3 percent and 4.5 percent, respectively, while the eurozone’s GDP is estimated to grow 1.1 percent.

The IMF said it expected global GDP to grow 3.1 percent, up from 3 percent in its previous outlook.

The Washington, DC-based institution said while economic activity had proved resilient this year, the global economy faced multiple risks.

“Further escalation in conflicts, a reassessment of expectations surrounding artificial intelligence (AI), renewed trade tensions, and fiscal vulnerabilities could weaken growth,” it said.

“On the upside, stronger momentum in AI investment and productivity gains from AI or a sustained easing of geopolitical and trade tensions could strengthen growth.”

World.title: Michael Jordan’s ‘Last Dance’ NBA Finals jersey sells for record $14m
World.content:
The jersey Michael Jordan wore during ‌‌Game 2 of the “Last Dance” 1998 NBA Finals has sold for a ⁠⁠record $14m.

Hunt Auctions ⁠⁠announced on Monday that the game-worn, autographed Chicago Bulls jersey was bought by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale.

It is the highest ⁠⁠price ever paid for a piece of basketball memorabilia and, according to the auction house, the newly sold Jordan jersey ranks as the second-largest sale in history ⁠⁠among game-worn sports jerseys.

The New York Yankees jersey worn by Babe Ruth in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series – during which Ruth called his shot before a home run – went for $24.12m in 2024.

Jordan and the Bulls defeated the Utah Jazz in ‌‌six games to win the 1998 championship, the sixth and final title of his career in Chicago.

Game 2, played on June 5, 1998, in Salt Lake City, saw Chicago even the series 1-1, largely thanks to a dominant performance by its superstar guard.

Jordan put up 37 points, five rebounds, and three assists in a 93-88 victory. He would go on to collect his sixth ⁠⁠and final Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) award, two more than anyone ⁠⁠else in NBA history, nine days later.

The wildly popular “Last Dance” documentary, released in 2020, was centred around that 1997-98 Bulls season.

“The record-setting price achieved for the related Michael Jordan jersey is yet another corroborative result as ⁠⁠to the significance of Jordan within the industry and popular culture. This remarkable garment bore witness to one of Jordan’s most ⁠⁠hallowed NBA Finals appearances as part of his ‘Last ⁠⁠Dance’ season to complete his illustrious career,” David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement.



“While Michael Jordan’s importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite ‌‌asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art. We are very pleased to have been able to facilitate this historic sale which serves as another benchmark for our ‌‌industry.”

This sale becomes at least the third time a Jordan jersey from that 1998 Finals has fetched at least $10m. A jersey from Game 1 was sold at auction for about $10.1m in 2022, and a jersey from Game 3 was auctioned last month for about $12.3m via an auction in September.

“Michael Jordan was an incredibly talented player who is admired around the world,” Firman said in a news release distributed by the auction house. “I’m very excited about the purchase.”

The jersey that Firman bought was originally bought from the Bulls by a private collector in 2003, Hunt said, adding that it “has remained within a succinct chain of custody, having only changed hands once from the original purchaser”.

Just about anything related to the 1998 Finals and Jordan’s final season with the Bulls has been the subject of huge interest in the collector space. In 2023, a pair of Air Jordan sneakers that he wore in Game 2 against the Jazz was sold by Sotheby’s for $2.2m, touted at the time as “a new world record for the most valuable sneakers ever sold”.

World.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
World.content:
Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC.

Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.

He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.

Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.

Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.

UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes, external Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.

He says this difference in death toll â as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts â accounts for the current stalemate at the front.

In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."

The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports, external says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.

World.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
World.content:
Mitte, who grew up in Louisiana, was a young teen when he auditioned for the breakthrough role after moving to Los Angeles to support his younger sister's acting career in 2005.

He had said that his first audition in Los Angeles was for a California state public service announcement for an anti-meth commercial.

"Fast forward to auditioning for Breaking Bad, which is still, in my opinion, an anti-meth thing because it doesn't end well for anyone," he said on the Joe Vulpis Podcast earlier this month.

His character was based on Gilligan's late friend who had a more severe case of cerebral palsy and used forearm crutches, which Mitte did not require.

Mitte was seen as playing the role with honesty and accessibility, cracking jokes as a teen whose health condition was rarely mentioned in the series.

Breaking Bad aired on US cable broadcaster AMC for five seasons from 2008-13.

After shooting to fame, Mitte fought for more varied roles and complex depictions of characters with disabilities, both visible and invisible.

"Whenever awards season rolls around, we always hope to see a diverse group of projects that reflect all of us, in body and mind," he told the BBC in 2021.

"Watching the awareness grow around disability representation has been great to see, but breakthroughs sometimes come in pieces and moments instead of larger change," he said.

Mitte's other on-screen credits include Hannah Montana, Switched at Birth, Westhampton and his latest project, Talking to Strangers, which came out earlier this year.

Additional reporting by Rebecka Pieder.

If you have been affected by the issues raised in this story help and support is available via the BBC Action Line.

World.title: One dead and several hurt after rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
World.content:
One person has died and several others were injured after an incident on a rollercoaster at an amusement park in the state of Georgia.

The Cobb County Police Department said it was investigating the fatality at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24km) from Atlanta, according to the BBC's news partner CBS.

Police did not specify what ride was involved, but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, with riders being helped off by workers.

Six Flags Over Georgia said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones."

Officials have not said how the person was killed. The BBC has contacted local police and fire authorities, as well as park officials.

Witnesses told local media they saw a man ejected from the ride, accounts that the BBC has not verified.

Local outlet 11Alive quoted a witness saying the man fell from the rollercoaster on to the roof of a haunted house attraction.

A park spokesperson said in a statement that its team and local authorities had responded immediately, and they were co-operating on an investigation into the incident.

Mableton Mayor Michael Owens said the city's public safety director was co-ordinating with local police and park security on the situation.

The Goliath ride opened in 2006, and it has an elevation of 200ft (60m), a 170ft plunge, a 540-degree spiral, and a speed of up to 70mph (112km/h), according to the park website. On its "thrill scale", Six Flags ranks Goliath at level four out of five.

Six Flags is the largest amusement park operator in North America, with 20 amusement parks, 14 water parks and nine resorts across Canada, the US and Mexico.

The incident comes just weeks after one of its parks in southern California announced it would close the popular X2 roller coaster after more than 100 people alleged brain injuries from the ride.

Six Flags said the ride had passed a range of safety tests, but that it had decided to retire it because it was "the right thing to do".

World.title: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released to US media
World.content:
A series of newly-released calls made after the failed execution of US death row inmate Christa Pike reveal emergency services were delayed by confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials.

The recordings, first obtained by the Associated Press, show that minutes passed as officials and responders attempted to confirm whether the request for emergency help in the execution chamber at Riverbend Prison was legitimate.

The Nashville Department of Emergency Communications released several calls between the agency and other departments - including police and highway patrol.

"We are trying to find out if that is an actual thing that is happening and we need to send an ambulance and, or if you need police assistance or if this is someone that is just basically prank calling or, like, swatting us," one dispatcher can be heard saying during a call.

Another recording shows Kelly Gleason, Christa Pike's defence attorney, calling for help.

"She is still alive and breathing and needs immediate life-saving care," she says.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995. She survived two injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September and was taken to hospital in a critical condition.

World.title: India 'cockroach' leaders detained after entering barricaded protest site
World.content:
Leaders of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were detained early on Tuesday after they entered a heavily-guarded protest site and chanted slogans demanding the country's election chief resign over a controversial revision of electoral rolls.

Party founder Abhijeet Dipke shared a video showing Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das being taken away by police from Jantar Mantar, a historic Delhi observatory popular for protests.

Footage showed the two - along with others - climbing over police barricades before chanting slogans while holding the Indian flag.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's opponents allege the voter list revision benefits his party, a charge it and the Election Commission reject.

There have been days of protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

Police have stepped up security across Delhi as demonstrators challenge restrictions on where protests can be held.

Early on Tuesday, Dipke, Das and Ranka all shared videos showing Das and Ranka entering Jantar Mantar.

"You cannot denotify the resistance," Dipke wrote on X.

Das also posted a message declaring that the site had been "reclaimed" and that they were being detained.

It was not immediately clear where police had taken the leaders.

Ranka later appeared on an Instagram live broadcast from a police bus alongside other detainees where they appeared cheerful and said they would not back down.

World.title: Six Ukrainian energy sites hit by Russia since Trump announced ceasefire, Zelensky says
World.content:
Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities hours after US President Donald Trump announced the two countries had agreed to an energy ceasefire, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.

Despite Trump stating on Sunday the truce would be "effective immediately", the Ukrainian president said Russia had hit "our gas stations, energy infrastructure, and other facilities".

There were blackouts in the city of Izyum after a Russian strike destroyed power grids, Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform said, while energy and railway infrastructure in western Ukraine was also targeted overnight.

On Monday, Russia's Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Ukraine does not deserve the "respite" a ceasefire would bring.

World.title: The island where locals say data centres are taking their water
World.content:
"Water! Water!" the crowd shouted as it stormed a compound with data centres, armed with empty plastic bottles and jerry cans.

There were about 300 of them, all residents on the Indonesian island of Batam, and they were furious that the taps at home had run dry, while the data centres in the new Nongsa Digital Park seemed to have enough water to protect their machines from overheating.

"Not a single drop has come through our taps for the last three months... Our water supply had been reliable until the data centres came," Dewi Susanti, one of the protesters, told the BBC.

People in her village, Bakau Serip, were now depending on tanker trucks that dispensed "dirty, cloudy and smelly" water, she said.

Batam's water utility told the BBC it was working to improve supply, but did not comment on whether the disruption was linked to demand from the data centres.

But BP Batam, the agency overseeing trade and industry, blamed it on a prolonged dry spell and denied allegations from locals that water meant for homes was being channelled to data centres.

This is not the first such protest in Batam, whose shrinking reservoirs find themselves under more pressure as the island tries to transform itself into a digital hub.

Following protests in August and September, authorities told the firms opening data centres in Batam that they must build their own desalination plants instead of relying on reservoirs for freshwater.

But locals say they are increasingly concerned that they must now compete with servers for water.

"Reliable data on data centre water use in Indonesia remains scarce, partly because companies treat it as proprietary information," says Agus Hasan, a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology.

"We should build [data centres] rationally, transparently, and responsibly, and insist on seeing the numbers... [Otherwise] those kept in the dark while their taps run dry will push back, and rightly so," he adds.

World.title: Watch: US man eyes pumpkin world record after fifth contest win
World.content:
A five-time US giant pumpkin contest winner tells the BBC he'd "love" to break the world record for a second time.

Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California, for the annual pumpkin weighing event.

His whopping gourd took home the prize, tipping the scales at 2,389 pounds (1,083kg).

But Gienger says he's eyeing off a different prize â the world record title â which was set in England's south coast last week with a squash weighing in at 2,857 pounds (1,300kg).

As a previous holder of the world-record mantle, Gienger says he's focused on the challenge ahead.

World.title: Family demands probe of police officer’s killing
World.content:
The family of a mobile police officer, Abdulrahman Auwal, reportedly killed along Kwi-Beco Road between Barkin Ladi and Riyom local government areas of Plateau State, on Monday, called on the Inspector-General of Police to investigate the officer’s death.

The family said several questions remained unanswered about the incident, including how the officer was attacked and why the motorcycle rider who was reportedly conveying him survived.

Mr Auwal was reportedly killed while returning from a community service. He was buried at Zaria Cemetery in Jos on Saturday.

His mother, Larai Musa, said she had accepted her son’s death as the will of Allah but wants the police to establish what happened.

“There are still unanswered questions surrounding the death of my son. He was reported to have been cut with a sharp object while on a motorcycle with an okada rider. My son was killed, and the okada rider is alive,” she said.

Ms Musa questioned the circumstances of the attack and urged the police to identify and question the commercial motorcycle rider.

“The okada rider who reported the death should be able to explain where he took him to, who stopped them and who attacked only the passenger,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The family urged the police to provide a clear account of the incident and establish the circumstances that led to the officer’s death.

It also expressed disappointment that, four days after the incident, no police officers or colleagues of the deceased had visited to offer their condolences.

The Plateau State Police Command had not issued an official statement on the incident as of the time of filing this report.

Attempts to get a reaction from the command were unsuccessful, as the police spokesperson could not be reached immediately by phone.

World.title: Science, research and investment key to Jigawa’s agric transformation- Namadi
World.content:
Jigawa State Governor, Umar Namad has identified strong political leadership, agricultural research, and sustained investment as the three critical pillars for achieving agricultural transformation, strengthening food security and creating economic opportunities for farmers in the state.

The governor made this assertion on Monday while delivering the keynote address as a guest speaker at the 11th National Annual Conference of the Crop Science Society of Nigeria (CSSN), held at the Nuhu Muhammad Sunusi Auditorium, Federal University, Dutse.

The conference had the theme, “Advancing Sustainable Crop and Climate-Smart Technology for Food Security and Economic Growth.”

Governor Namadi said that Nigeria’s growing population and the increasing effects of climate change have made it necessary to rethink agricultural production through improved technologies, stronger research institutions, and policies that support farmers, stating that traditional farming methods alone would not be sufficient to address contemporary food production challenges.

“A farmer with a hoe and old seeds cannot out-produce climate change,” he said.

He said agriculture was central to his administration’s 12-Point Agenda, supported by the Jigawa State Agricultural Policy 2024–2030 and State Agricultural Investment Plan, alongside strengthened institutions to improve coordination, investment, and service delivery across the sector.

The governor highlighted the importance of scientific research in translating agricultural policies and investments into measurable improvements in productivity.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the state government had repositioned and equipped the Jigawa State Agricultural Research Institute, supported postgraduate research through its Wheat Value Chain Research Programme, and facilitated advanced studies for more than 80 Jigawa academics in relevant agricultural disciplines.

He also cited partnerships with the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA), AfricaRice, CGIAR institutions, and other international research organizations, alongside collaboration with the Sasakawa Africa Association, saying that demonstration results from these partnerships recorded rice yield increases of between 43 and 48 percent and sorghum yield improvements of more than 60 percent compared with farmers’ usual practices.

“We are building a durable pipeline of specialist knowledge because the true test of science is not publication alone, but adoption: better varieties, healthier soils, more efficient water use, lower losses, higher yields, and stronger farmer incomes.”

On extension services and farmers’ access to technology, Namadi disclosed that the State had deployed about 1,700 J-AGRO extension agents and distributed 1,185 motorcycles in 2026 to strengthen field-level agricultural advisory services.

“We have established a digital farmer database and input voucher system so that support reaches real farmers, not ghost farmers. We have set up Climate-Smart Agriculture Centres and twenty modern greenhouses for technology demonstration and vegetable production, and we are extending mobile veterinary services to all 287 wards in the state. When extension works, adoption follows, and when adoption follows, yields and incomes rise.”

The governor further outlined investments in irrigation and mechanization, including collaboration with the federal government to develop approximately 18,000 hectares in the Hadejia axis and the provision of 6,000 solar-powered irrigation pumps and borehole-based upland irrigation facilities.

He said more than 250,000 farmers had benefited from agricultural inputs, mechanization, and irrigation support over the past three years, while fertilizer support for the 2026 wet-season farming programme was targeted at 90,000 farmers.

Governor Namadi said the state was developing 200 integrated rice-processing clusters and supporting investments in the processing of rice, sesame, hibiscus, and wheat to improve value addition, reduce post-harvest losses, and expand market opportunities for farmers and agribusinesses.

He called for closer collaboration between government, universities, research institutions, development partners, and the private sector, stressing that agricultural research must respond directly to the needs of farmers and the wider economy.

At the conference, the governor was conferred with the Fellowship of the Crop Science Society of Nigeria in recognition of his administration’s agricultural achievements and contributions to agricultural development in Jigawa State.

World.title: 2027: APC to inaugurate presidential campaign council for Tinubu’s re-election Wednesday
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) says it will inaugurate President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 presidential campaign council on Wednesday, 14 October, as the party steps up preparations for the next presidential election.

The party announced this in a press statement issued on Monday by the National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka.

INEC has scheduled the presidential election for 16 January, 2027.

According to the statement, the inauguration will take place at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

“The All Progressives Congress (APC) will inaugurate the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja,” the statement said.

The party said the list of members of the various directorates expected to attend the inauguration would be released shortly.

The Presidential Campaign Council is expected to coordinate the APC’s campaign activities ahead of the 2027 election, including mobilising party members and supporters, communicating the party’s manifesto and the administration’s policies, engaging voters across the country and coordinating campaign events.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It is also expected to oversee campaign messaging, media engagement and collaboration among party leaders, elected officials and state campaign structures to promote Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Mr Tinubu, who won the 2023 presidential election on the APC platform, is seeking a second term in office in 2027 alongside his deputy, Kashim Shettima.

World.title: NUFBTE urges House of Representatives to halt the passage of CETA Bill
World.content:
The leadership of the National Union of Food, Beverage, and Tobacco Employees, NUFBTE, has urged the House of Representatives to withhold concurrence on Customs, Excise Tariffs, Etc. (Consolidation) Amendment Bill, 2025 (CETA Bill), is currently before the chamber.

In an open letter addressed to the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, which was co-signed by the President, NUFBTE, Comrade Garba Dankama, the union warned that passing such legislation at this time would place an additional burden on Nigerian workers and the manufacturing sector, given the impact of ongoing economic reforms on their shoulders.

The 2025 CETA Bill proposes replacing the predictable ₦ 10-per-litre specific tax on soft drinks with a percentage levy per litre on the retail price of the products.

Dankama said Nigerian workers cannot survive an additional, poorly designed tax burden, warning that the proposed legislation could turn an already difficult operating environment into a catastrophic one for the sector.

He explained that with the manufacturing sector, and the food, beverage, and tobacco sectors in a state of acute distress, passing the CETA Bill would inflict irreversible damage to an already fragile industrial base and threaten the livelihood of workers who depend on it.

“Capacity utilization across manufacturing has declined sharply as producers contend with prohibitively high borrowing costs, rising energy and logistics expenses, persistent constraints in foreign exchange access, and weakened consumer purchasing power. Several production lines have been scaled back or shut down entirely. The NAD sector, which anchors hundreds of thousands of jobs across farming, haulage, distribution, and retail, cannot absorb an additional tax escalation without triggering a wave of further closures, retrenchments, and value chain collapse,” he stated.

Dankama expressed confidence that the leadership of the House of Representatives would protect the interests of Nigerian workers while supporting the manufacturing sector through the current economic difficulties.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, workers have already borne the brunt of the Federal Government’s fuel subsidy removal and foreign exchange reforms and may not be able to shoulder another financial burden. He added that workers’ incomes had not kept pace with the sharp increases in transportation, food, housing, and other essential costs.

“The sector needs room to adjust to the current economic realities and remain sustainable. An aggressive percentage-based tax at this time could place a serious strain on the industry, with consequences for investment, jobs, and livelihoods. We should not put further pressure on an industry that provides employment and supports the livelihoods of so many Nigerians,” he said.

The NUFBTE president further noted that a percentage-based tax would increase the burden on producers, asmanufacturing costs remain exposed to external volatility driven by global commodity price fluctuations and geopolitical uncertainty. He warned that the proposed levy would lead to higher prices, weaker demand, and further factory closures.

“Taxing a product category that contributes only 5% of national sugar intake will not yield real public health benefits. It will simply push consumers toward cheaper, unregulated alternatives, while destroying the livelihoods of over a million Nigerians who have already borne the brunt of recent economic reforms,” he added.

World.title: Shettima to North: You have nothing to fear if Tinubu wins Second Term
World.content:
The Vice President, Kashim Shettima, has issued a rallying cry to the North for President Bola Tinubu’s reelection in the 2027 presidential election, declaring that the region has absolutely nothing to fear from a second term for the president.

With urgent intensity, he implored northern leaders and citizens to unite behind the president’s re-election bid, framing the administration’s second-term agenda as a secure, bulletproof guarantee for the region’s future prosperity and stability.

Mr Shettima made the call on Monday when he received, on a courtesy visit, a delegation from the Arewa for Tinubu (A4A) – a northern-based think tank -working for the re-election of President Tinubu.

He called on leaders across the region to unite into a single front and work for the progress of the area and the well-being of its people, which are top priorities for the Tinubu administration.

According to the VP, the North has no reason to be scared of the re-election of Mr Tinubu, as it has benefitted immensely in terms of appointments and game-changing projects and programmes.

His words: “Let’s unite as a people and work for the development of our region and the progress of our people through the re-election of this administration. We are benefiting, and we stand to benefit more from this government in many ways.

“The Bank of Agriculture has disbursed N450 billion to 700,000 smallholder farmers in Nigeria, and about 70 per cent of the beneficiaries are from the north.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The present administration is working towards completing landmark and groundbreaking projects in parts of the country. I can assure you that the president loves the north and the president will work for the north.”

The vice president thanked the group for their steadfast support for President Bola Tinubu at all times and appealed to them to work harder and galvanise across wards, communities and local governments in the northern region for the president’s re-election.

Earlier, the Director General of the Area for Asiwaju and former Jigawa State Governor, Abubakar Badaru, said the organisation will not rest on its laurels until they make the North proud by reelecting President Tinubu.

He said the group plans to meet with religious leaders, including Muslim and Christian clerics, as well as other prominent Nigerians to explain to them the need to support the Tinubu/Shettima ticket in 2027.

“On discussions with the high profile, we have gone far. We have met them several times, and the BoT is meeting them again to consolidate our gains and to tell them why there is need to support this ticket.

“We are also supporting the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) with whatever they want us to do that is micro in nature because they are so big and we really don’t want to lose sight of the bigger arrangement that is there. We want to focus very well on the contacts at the grassroots – the local government areas and the wards.”

Also, Chairman of the organisation’s Board of Trustees (BoT) and former Kano State Governor, Ibrahim Shekarau, said the think tank which worked for President Tinubu’s election in the 2023 general election will repeat the same feat in 2027.

He said the organisation had been meeting with northern governors and other stakeholders to compare notes and collaborate on areas of working together to achieve the President’s reelection.

He noted that the organisation has concluded plans to have a full-fledged secretariat for purposes of coordination, where there will be offices for directors and state coordinators to compare reports, analyse them, and give out instructions to its members.

The BoT chairman formally invited the vice president to officially commission the A4A office complex on Saturday, October 17, 2027.

Also present at the meeting were former Governors of Plateau, Joshua Dariye and Simon Lalong; Taraba, Jolly Nyame; Kogi, Yahaya Bello; Katsina, Ibrahim Shema; Bauchi, Isa Yuguda; Special Adviser to the President on Policy and Coordination, Hadiza Bala Usman; Chairman of NDLEA, Buba Marwa, some top officials of government, and other members of the A4A BOT and Secretariat.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice)

12th October, 2026

World.title: INEC List: Jigawa ADC candidate fumes over running mate replacement
World.content:
Jigawa State Governor Umar Namadi and 11 others have made the final list of governorship candidates in Jigawa released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Saturday.

However, one of his main challengers—African Democratic Congress (ADC) candidate Sabo Nakudu—is protesting the replacement of his nominated running mate on the list.

Mr Nakudu had submitted the name of Aminu Ibrahim to the electoral body, but Nasiru Kaugama was published as his running mate on INEC’s official list instead.

The substitution stunned Mr Nakudu and his supporters, who have accused a faction within the party of orchestrating the replacement.

The development has thrown the opposition party into internal turmoil, causing members to trade accusations at a crucial time when campaign efforts should be gaining momentum.

While INEC did not provide a reason for replacing Mr Ibrahim, sources suggested the move may be tied to a decision by the party’s national headquarters to appease a rival faction.

That faction had accused Mr Nakudu of hijacking the ADC structure despite being a late entrant from the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The ADC crisis in Jigawa stems from its governorship primary, which pitted four-term House of Representatives veteran Adamu Jumbo against Mr Nakudu, a recent defector from the ruling APC.

Following the primary election, Mr Jumbo petitioned the party’s election appeal committee, alleging widespread irregularities, intimidation, and interference by the party leadership.

His camp views Mr Nakudu’s emergence as a takeover by wealthy latecomers, while Mr Nakudu’s faction has dismissed his opponents as bitter losers.

A leaked document revealed a proposed 60:40 power-sharing agreement between the two camps—which included conceding the deputy governorship slot and promising key cabinet appointments—in an attempt to broker a truce.

Despite these efforts and an intervention by the party’s leadership, the dispute over the running mate slot remains unresolved and continues to fuel ongoing division within the party.

Below is the list released by INEC:

2) Sabo Mohammed Nakudu — ADC

3) Suleiman Ibrahim — ADP

4) Namadi Umar A. — APC

5) Yero Ahmed — APGA
