7) Musa Mubarak — APP

8) Abdulaziz Aminu — LP

9)Dutse Aminu Sani— NDC

10)Aminu Hassan Ibrahim — NRM

11) Sule Mustapha Lamido — PDP

12) Musa Namadobi Garba— SDP

World.title: Why ADC plans to restore petrol subsidy – Spokesperson
World.content:
Nigeria’s opposition party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), said it will subsidise domestic crude oil production to reduce petrol prices if it wins the 2027 presidential election, arguing that Nigerians are too poor to bear the full cost of petroleum products under market forces.

The National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said the administration of President Bola Tinubu had removed fuel subsidy without adequately preparing Nigerians for the resulting economic hardship.

Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, Mr Abdullahi said the ADC, under its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, would prioritise reducing the cost of living rather than leaving citizens to absorb the full impact of market-driven prices.

“Nigerians are too poor to be left to market forces. We cannot have people so poor and leave them without subsidy,” he said.

He said the party’s proposed approach would focus on subsidising crude oil production and making the commodity available to domestic refineries at lower costs, rather than returning to the previous system of subsidising petrol consumption.

“Whatever we need to do to subsidise the production of crude and make it cheap and deliver it to the people of Nigeria, we are going to do it,” he said.

Mr Abdullahi argued that the government had a responsibility to protect citizens from economic hardship, likening the need for intervention to a country defending itself during wartime.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He criticised the Tinubu administration for transferring the burden of economic reforms to Nigerians without providing sufficient protection against rising living costs.

The ADC spokesperson also questioned the government’s spending priorities, citing the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as an example of a project he considered unnecessary amid widespread economic hardship.

He argued that Nigeria should not be compared with countries such as the United States without considering the public services available to their citizens, particularly affordable education and a more developed public transport system.

Mr Abdullahi said the quality of public education in Nigeria had declined, forcing many families to turn to private schools for better education.

He recalled that Nigeria introduced universal basic education in 1999 as a free and compulsory programme, but argued the system has become less effective over time.

The spokesperson asked the government to prioritise policies that directly improve citizens’ living conditions instead of pursuing projects that do not adequately address their immediate needs.

ADC criticises finance minister

Mr Abdullahi also criticised the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, saying that Nigeria needed an economist with the appropriate training to manage the country’s economic challenges.

“We need a serious-minded economist who has gone to school to fix the economy,” he said.

He argued that an accountant’s approach to economic policy differs from an economist’s, particularly when decisions involve questions of economic ideology and development.

The criticism came amid a dispute over the federal government’s recently announced 30-day petrol price discount at Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) retail outlets.

The government has said the discount does not amount to a return of fuel subsidy, arguing that the NNPCL would bear the cost through reduced retail prices rather than public funding.

The ADC has maintained that government intervention is necessary to reduce fuel costs, with its proposed model centred on supporting domestic production.

2027 election will be APC versus Nigerians

Mr Abdullahi said Atiku would make life more affordable for Nigerians, adding that international crude oil prices alone do not determine the cost of petrol at filling stations.

He said the ADC’s economic proposals would focus on reducing production costs and easing the pressure of rising prices on households.

When asked about the exchange rate during the interview, Mr Abdullahi said he lacked the technical expertise to discuss the issue in detail. Still, he insisted his party would pursue policies to reduce the cost of living.

He also defended Atiku’s decision to make economic hardship a central issue in the debate ahead of the 2027 general election.

Mr Abdullahi predicted the election would pit the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) against Nigerians dissatisfied with the government’s economic policies.

“Nigerians are saying they can’t continue with the government, and that’s why we are saying 2027 is going to be between the people and the APC,” he said.

World.title: 2027: Kaduna APC vows massive turnout as Tinubu’s presidential campaign begins
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kaduna State says it is ready to receive President Bola Tinubu and other party leaders as the ruling party prepares to kick off its presidential campaign in the state on 24 October.

The party’s State Publicity Secretary, Muhammad Sani, stated this on Monday at a news conference in Kaduna, monitored by PREMIUM TIMES.

He described the decision to begin the campaign in the state as a significant development for the party.

“There is no better city the president could have chosen than Kaduna. With his choice of Kaduna, we do not doubt that the march to victory has started,” Mr Sani said.

He assured the president, APC members, and Nigerians that the state was prepared to host the campaign and accommodate party supporters expected to attend.

“We are proud that the march to Aso Rock in 2027 is beginning from Kaduna on Oct. 24, 2026.

“We want to assure Mr President, all APC members and the whole of Nigeria that Kaduna State is well prepared to receive party members and to spearhead the campaign for the President’s victory,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

APC plans mass mobilisation

Mr Sani said the party was mobilising supporters across the state under Governor Uba Sani’s leadership to welcome Mr Tinubu and other APC leaders.

He said the mobilisation was expected to attract hundreds of thousands of supporters, adding that the party intended to use the event to demonstrate its solidarity with the president.

“We are going to mobilise, under the leadership of our governor, Senator Uba Sani, hundreds of thousands of people to welcome Mr President. We are going to show love and solidarity,” he said.

The publicity secretary also expressed confidence in the party’s target of securing two million votes for Mr Tinubu in Kaduna State during the 2027 presidential election.

He described the state’s political atmosphere as favourable to the APC, insisting the party enjoyed widespread unity among its members.

“Kaduna is united under one roof,” he said.

Party targets Tinubu’s re-election

Mr Sani said Kaduna would play a leading role in the APC’s efforts to secure a second term for Mr Tinubu, whose current four-year term will end on May 29, 2027.

“Today in Kaduna State, there is no opposition. We assure Mr President that Kaduna State will lead the pack that will return him to Aso Rock on May 29, 2027,” he said.

His remarks reflect the APC’s efforts to consolidate its political support in Kaduna ahead of the next general elections.

However, his claim that the state has no opposition reflects the party’s position rather than an established description of the state’s political landscape.

Kaduna is one of Nigeria’s politically significant states, with a diverse electorate and a history of competitive political contests.

The APC’s proposed two-million-vote target will therefore be tested by the strength of its grassroots mobilisation and rival parties’ performance during the election campaign.

Mr Sani also assured party leaders and other visitors that the state would provide a peaceful and harmonious environment for the campaign.

“We also want to assure Mr President that visitors to Kaduna State will see a peaceful, united, and harmonious state,” he said.

The campaign is scheduled to take place on October 24, 2026, with the APC hoping to use the Kaduna rally to launch its drive for Mr Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

World.title: IMF upgrades forecast for Nigeria’s economic growth to 4.2%
World.content:
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva speaks at the Milken Institute ahead of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund annual meetings in Washington, DC on October 8, 2025. The global economy is doing better than expected, even as it faces prolonged uncertainty and underwhelming medium-term growth prospects, Georgieva said Wednesday. The world economy is doing “better than feared, but worse than we need,” Georgieva told reporters in Washington. (Photo by Brendan Smialowski / AFP)

*Warns of tougher times as global growth slows to 3.1%

*Says AI boom, energy shocks threaten global economic outlook

By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has upgraded its forecast for Nigeria’s economic growth for 2026 to 4.2 per cent but warned that rising energy and food prices, geopolitical tensions and potential market corrections linked to artificial intelligence (AI) threaten the global economic outlook.

The new forecast was contained in the IMF World Economic Outlook report October 2026, titled Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices”, released on Monday during the ongoing annual meetings of the IMF/World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand.

Furthermore, the new forecast represents one percentage point above the 4.1 per cent earlier projected by the IMF in the July 2026 edition of its WEO.

According to the IMF, “Growth in sub-Saharan Africa is expected to remain stable at 4.5 per cent in 2026, though this masks substantial divergence across countries, reflecting differences in policy space, reform implementation, commodity exposure, climate shocks, and access to external financing.

“Oil-importing, non-resource-intensive economies are more adversely affected by higher energy and food prices, whereas some larger economies continue to benefit from earlier stabilisation and reform efforts, even though they are largely absent from the AI-driven global technology upswing and face headwinds from declines in official development assistance.

“Nigeria is supported by improved macroeconomic stability and favourable terms-of-trade effects, though higher prices for essentials are expected to further aggravate poverty and food insecurity.”

Global growth under pressure

However, the IMF warned that the global economy’s resilience was under increasing pressure, with growth projected to slow from 3.5 per cent in 2025 to 3.1 per cent in 2026, before recovering to 3.4 per cent in 2027.

Speaking at the press briefing on the WEO report, Sylvana Tenreyro, the IMF’s Economic Counsellor and Director of the Research Department, said, “The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is under strain, with risks tilted to the downside.”

She added, “The task ahead is to move from coping to rebuilding,” stressing the need to restore fiscal space, strengthen supply-side resilience and improve countries’ capacity to withstand future economic shocks.

Explaining the global outlook, Tenreyro identified energy and commodity price increases as major factors weighing on economic activity, while investment associated with artificial intelligence had provided support for growth.”

The IMF report noted that the global economy had withstood repeated shocks, including geopolitical conflicts and trade tensions, but cautioned that “these margins of adjustment are not unlimited.”

According to the IMF, the interaction between geopolitical tensions and technological investment has created divergent growth outcomes across countries.

While economies benefiting from technology-related investment and favourable commodity trade conditions have received some support, others face higher import bills, exchange-rate pressures and weaker real incomes.

The Fund warned that prolonged geopolitical tensions could keep energy and food prices elevated, revive inflationary pressures, worsen fiscal and external balances, and weigh on economic growth.

Global headline inflation is projected to rise from 4.1 per cent in 2025 to 4.7 per cent in 2026 before easing to 4.1 per cent in 2027, with higher energy and food prices driving the temporary increase.

AI boom raises fresh risks

The IMF also cautioned that the technology investment boom, particularly in artificial intelligence, could become a source of financial instability.

Although AI-related investment has supported economic activity and international trade, the Fund warned that investment gains were concentrated in a relatively small number of firms, sectors and economies.

It cautioned that “a reassessment of AI-related profitability and productivity prospects could sharply reduce investment, trigger equity market corrections, and tighten financial conditions.”

Such a correction, the report said, could spill over into economies integrated into technology supply chains and markets with significant exposure to technology stocks.

Urges fiscal discipline

Against this backdrop, Tenreyro called on governments to rebuild fiscal buffers, safeguard financial stability and strengthen private-sector dynamism.

“Fiscal policy must be restrained and help contain demand pressures at a time of heightened inflationary risks,” the IMF chief economist said in the report.

The Fund also stressed the importance of monetary policy focused on price stability, adding that “central bank independence is instrumental in achieving that goal.”

“The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits,” urging countries to strengthen their capacity to withstand future disruptions and achieve sustainable growth,” Tenreyro added.

World.title: Edo: I stopped Ighodalo from becoming governor to prevent Obaseki choosing a successor – Wike
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, says he opposed the 2024 Edo governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Asue Ighodalo, because he wanted to prevent former governor Godwin Obaseki from installing his successor.

Wike disclosed this on Monday during a stakeholders’ meeting of the rainbow coalition in Abuja, where he credited an alliance between factions of the PDP and the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the ruling party’s victory in the election.

“In the last election that took place in Edo State, the victory was as a result of the coalition between the legacy of PDP and the APC,” he said.

“We had to work together to make sure that the former governor, Governor Obaseki, did not produce his successor. And that is the truth. I was behind it, and I don’t have any regrets about it. So when people say that nothing like coalition, they tell lies.”

According to Wike, Ighodalo, whom he described as a “good candidate”, visited his residence more than three times to seek his support, but he turned him down because of his opposition to Obaseki.

“He came to my house more than three times. I said, ‘Listen, you’re a good candidate, but for this election, I’m sorry, because this election is between us and the man who is bringing you, called Obaseki, ungrateful person, so returning you is like bringing him back, so I’m sorry. You have to fail,’ and he failed,” Wike said.

He added that Governor Monday Okpebholo and Adams Oshiomhole, the senator representing Edo North, could attest to the role the alliance played in the election.

“The truth of the matter is that it has been there, depending on how it is worked out. So the governor today, Senator Okpebholo, will know sincerely that it was that coalition,” he said.

“Senator Adams Oshiomhole will also attest to the fact that it was that coalition that made us to defeat the PDP, even though I’m a member of PDP, but for that purpose I said I would not support the incumbent governor to produce a successor, even though the candidate was a very good candidate, who was the former managing director of a bank.”

Wike’s comments come amid renewed attention on the rainbow coalition, which has been associated with efforts to build political alliances ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Musk spent $276m to boost Republicans in midterms – Report
World.content:
File: Elon Musk

Tech billionaire Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, has contributed $276 million to organizations boosting the campaigns of right-wing American candidates ahead of upcoming midterm elections, US media reported Monday.

The sum, all contributed since July, positions Musk as the largest single donor for the November 3 elections, according to the New York Times. He has spent a total of $366 million this election cycle.

The largest funding recipient was the Republican’s Senate Leadership Fund, receiving $158 million, aimed at maintaining the party’s control of the upper house of Congress despite a slim margin.

The SpaceX and Tesla boss is no stranger to massive US election spending, having contributed $290 million in 2024 to help US President Donald Trump win reelection.

Trump allowed Musk to work in the White House for several months overseeing his cost-cutting Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) venture, but exited the role after a public falling out with the president.

They’ve since reconciled, and Trump awarded Musk the National Medal of Science at an event in DC last week.

Though individual campaign donations in the United States are capped at $3,300 per person, loopholes in the US campaign finance system allow political mega donors to contribute to funds known as political action committees or “PACs,” which support candidates.

Musk donated $76 million this summer to his own America PAC, the New York Times reported.

Other recipients of Musk’s political funding include $20 million to the Republican’s Congressional Leadership Fund, $10 million each to the Republican Governors Association and the Lone Star Liberty PAC, and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association.

World.title: IMF advocates cash transfers to cushion hardship in Nigeria
World.content:
*Says Nigerians still suffer high cost of living despite economic growth

*Urges FG to cut debt without worsening hardship

By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor, Bangkok, Thailand

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advocated targeted cash transfers and temporary income support for vulnerable households in Nigeria to cushion the impact of high living costs, reduce poverty and improve food security.

The Fund said the intervention should be accompanied by improved public expenditure quality and stronger revenue collection to help the Federal Government achieve fiscal consolidation and put public debt on a sustainable downward path without worsening the hardship faced by ordinary Nigerians.

Chief of the IMF Research Department’s World Economic Studies Division, Deniz Igan, stated this during a press briefing on the Fund’s World Economic Outlook at the ongoing IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Thailand.

Igan said that despite Nigeria’s economic growth and status as an energy exporter, the cost of living remained high, leaving many Nigerians struggling to meet their basic needs.

“Although economic growth has held up in Nigeria, given that it is an energy exporter, living costs are still very high, and we are very mindful that the population is suffering,” she said.

She noted that the pressures were particularly severe because of the rising cost of essential goods, especially food and energy, which account for a significant proportion of household consumption.

“In our chapter on fiscal policy, we also examine the pressures countries are facing from the rising cost of living, particularly increases in the prices of essential goods, which account for a significant proportion of the consumption basket,” Igan said.

Against this backdrop, she said the IMF was advocating targeted and temporary support for the most vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising prices.

“In this environment, we advocate cash transfers and targeted, temporary income support for the most vulnerable households in Nigeria,” she said.

According to her, the intervention would help address the immediate effects of economic hardship on poor households.

“Such transfers can help reduce poverty and improve food security,” she said.

However, Igan stressed that social protection measures must be accompanied by fiscal reforms to ensure that governments can sustainably finance public spending and gradually reduce their debt burden.

“This should be accompanied by a credible medium-term fiscal framework. That framework should focus on improving the quality of public expenditure and strengthening revenue collection,” she said.

Responding to the broader policy challenge, specifically how fiscal and monetary policies could be better positioned to ensure that the burden of economic stabilisation did not fall disproportionately on ordinary citizens while preserving price stability and investor confidence, Igan explained that monetary authorities must also balance the need to control inflation against the effects of policy measures on economic activity, particularly when economies face supply-side shocks.

On how central banks should respond to an oil price shock that pushes up inflation without a corresponding increase in demand, she said, “This is a classic case of a policy trade-off. Inflation is high, but economic activity is being constrained or reduced by the shock. This is where the central bank needs to manage the trade-off.”

She explained that such a situation differs from one in which inflation is driven by strong demand, requiring policymakers to consider the underlying causes of price increases before deciding on the appropriate response.

“This is a different situation from what we see in economies experiencing a demand-driven shock,” she said.

According to Igan, central banks must nevertheless maintain their focus on price stability and ensure that inflation returns to target within the policy horizon.

“It must ensure that inflation returns to target within the policy horizon, which we typically consider to be two to three years,” she said.

She added that monetary policy should remain sufficiently restrictive to bring inflation back to target, while policymakers take account of the implications for economic activity.

“In such circumstances, the central bank must continue to focus on price stability and ensure that its monetary policy stance remains sufficiently restrictive to bring inflation back to target, while also taking account of the effects on economic activity,” Igan said.

She noted that the appropriate policy response would depend on the nature of the shock and the circumstances of each economy, including labour-market conditions, the initial level of inflation and the economy’s exposure to the shock.

For Nigeria, the IMF’s recommendations underscore the need to combine measures to restore fiscal sustainability and maintain price stability with targeted interventions to protect vulnerable households from rising living costs.

The approach, as outlined by Igan, would require improved public spending efficiency, stronger revenue mobilisation and temporary income support for households most affected by economic pressures.

World.title: 2027: APC women promise issue-based campaign
World.content:
Edu says Tinubu’s record will drive re-election bid

The Director of Women Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Dr Betta Edu, has said the party’s 2027 presidential campaign will be issue-based, expressing confidence that the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration will strengthen his re-election bid.

Edu said on Monday in Abuja that Nigerian women were intensifying grassroots mobilisation across communities, households and voting constituencies to secure another mandate for Tinubu and sustain the implementation of his policies and development programmes.

She said the APC would focus its campaign on the administration’s record, ongoing infrastructure projects, economic reforms, educational opportunities and initiatives aimed at improving Nigerians’ livelihoods.

According to her, the party has achievements to present to voters and would focus on policies, programmes and measurable results rather than empty promises or personality-driven rhetoric.

Edu expressed appreciation to Tinubu for his leadership and commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda, as well as the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her advocacy for women, families and national development.

She also commended Vice-President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana Shettima; the Senate President and his wife; the Speaker of the House of Representatives and his wife; the Director-General of the PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the PCC secretary; the Chairman of the Progressives Governors Forum, Governor Hope Uzodimma; APC governors and other party leaders for their contributions to grassroots mobilisation.

The APC women mobilisation director also appreciated women’s groups, associations, support organisations and political structures within the party for their commitment to the administration and its mobilisation efforts.

She acknowledged the contributions of governors’ wives, women leaders and grassroots organisers, whose activities across states, local government areas and communities, she said, had strengthened the party’s engagement with women.

Edu said women remained a formidable force in Nigeria’s electoral process because of their numerical strength and influence within families, community associations, markets, professional bodies and local political structures.

She stressed that the APC’s mobilisation strategy would extend beyond rallies and public declarations to sustained engagement, political education, direct communication with voters and election-day sensitisation and mobilisation.

The objective, she said, was to ensure that Nigerians understood the administration’s policies, assessed their impact on their lives and made informed decisions about the country’s future.

NELFUND, reforms feature in campaign message

Edu identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the initiatives through which the Tinubu administration was expanding access to higher education and creating opportunities for young Nigerians.

She said the student loan programme was helping to address financial barriers that could prevent eligible students from accessing or completing tertiary education, while providing families with additional support in meeting educational costs.

According to her, NELFUND reflects the administration’s recognition that investment in education is essential to human capital development, economic productivity and the country’s long-term prosperity.

She said the programme, alongside infrastructure development, economic reforms and other sectoral interventions, would form part of the administration’s record that the APC would present to Nigerians during the campaign.

Edu maintained that the party would communicate its policies and achievements in clear, practical terms to help citizens understand the reforms and opportunities available to them.

She said the 2027 election would offer Nigerians an opportunity to assess the administration’s performance, adding that the party believed the country was moving towards a period of prosperity despite the challenges associated with its reforms.

For the Women Mobilisation Directorate, she said the immediate priority was to consolidate existing structures, improve coordination among women’s groups and ensure that the party’s message reached voters in rural and urban communities.

She emphasised that effective mobilisation required more than assembling crowds at political events, noting that consistent engagement, credible information and meaningful interaction with citizens were essential.

Edu particularly commended the First Lady for her role in the women’s campaign and efforts to promote women’s inclusion, family development and better opportunities for vulnerable groups.

She said women’s participation in governance should go hand in hand with efforts to strengthen their economic prospects and improve their quality of life.

The directorate, she added, would continue working with the APC national leadership, state chapters, women leaders and affiliated groups to communicate the administration’s policies and encourage active participation in the democratic process.

Edu expressed confidence that cooperation between the party’s leadership and its women’s structures would strengthen nationwide mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general election.

She urged APC women to remain united, organised and committed to the party’s objectives, saying their contributions would be vital to communicating the administration’s record and consolidating support ahead of the polls.

World.title: ‘He lacks right education’: ADC spokesperson questions finance minister’s capacity to manage economy
World.content:
Bolaji Abdullahi, spokesperson for the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has questioned whether Taiwo Oyedele, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, has the appropriate educational background to manage Nigeria’s economy.

Abdullahi made the remarks on Monday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today, while commenting on the Federal Government’s 30-day fuel price reduction initiative.

He argued that subsidy policies were ideological and that economic decisions should be guided by the expertise required to understand the country’s economic realities.

“I’m not saying he’s incompetent, but I think he doesn’t have the right education,” Abdullahi said.

“Because, look, the issue of subsidy is ideological. And we have to understand where you are coming from. I mean, I’m talking about an economy, this Nigerian economy.”

The ADC spokesperson, however, said his criticism was not a personal attack on Oyedele, whom he described as intelligent and said he respected.

“No, I’m not going personal. Like I said, I have utmost respect for him. And I think he’s quite a smart guy. I’m not taking that away from him,” he said.

Abdullahi argued that different academic disciplines approach economic issues differently, stressing the need for people with relevant training to manage the country’s economy.

“But what I’m saying is that the way an accountant reviews an economy is not the same way an economist reviews it. And the same way a classical economist would look at it is not the way a development economist would look at it.

“We need people who are trained to do this job to do it,” he added.

Oyedele holds a Higher National Diploma in Accountancy and Finance from Yaba College of Technology and a bachelor’s degree in Applied Accounting from Oxford Brookes University in the United Kingdom.

He also completed executive education programmes at the London School of Economics, Yale University, Gordon Institute of Business Science and Harvard Kennedy School.

Before his appointment as Minister of State for Finance, Oyedele spent 22 years at PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), where he rose to become the firm’s first fiscal policy partner and Africa tax leader.

World.title: I’m most experienced among Kwara guber candidates — Danladi-Salihu
World.content:
By Demola Akinyemi

ILORIN — The Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Rt. Hon. Engr. Yakubu Danladi-Salihu, has described himself as the most experienced and competent among those seeking to become the state’s next governor.

Danladi-Salihu made the claim during an interview with BBC News Yoruba while responding to allegations that Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq had handpicked him as his preferred successor.

Dismissing the allegation, the Speaker said his record in the legislature and years of experience in governance had prepared him for the governorship.

He cited his seven-and-a-half-year tenure as Speaker of the state Assembly as his strongest credential, arguing that his continued leadership reflected the confidence of his colleagues in his ability.

“If I had not measured up to the task, my colleagues — the 23 members I led for seven years — would have removed me from office. For someone to lead the legislative arm for about seven and a half years without any trouble or conflict implies that the person is highly competent,” he said.

Danladi-Salihu said competence should be assessed through a candidate’s track record in public service, governance and education.

“Among all those vying for the governorship, considering the experience I have garnered, who else has achieved what I have? I possess more experience than all of them. And regarding education, I hold all the necessary qualifications required to steer the affairs of Kwara State,” he added.

The APC candidate said his tenure had been characterised by stability in the Assembly, a cordial working relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government, and lawmaking in support of the state administration’s development agenda.

He said the ninth and 10th Assemblies, under his leadership, had remained united and focused on development, without internal crises or confrontations with the executive.

Danladi-Salihu described the record as a significant achievement, which he said demonstrated his capacity to manage governance and build consensus.

He promised that, if elected governor in 2027, he would build on the achievements of the AbdulRazaq administration, particularly in attracting investment, promoting industrialisation and expanding agricultural development across the state.

World.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 13, 2026
World.content:
The Nigerian Naira continues to reflect mixed movements across the foreign exchange market as businesses and individuals monitor currency values on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.

At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the Naira has maintained a relatively stable trajectory, trading at approximately 1,332.49 to the US dollar.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria and market trackers indicate that the official window has seen increased forex turnover, helping to stabilise the currency within the 1,329 to 1,333 band in recent trading sessions.

Meanwhile, in the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, the dollar continues to trade at a premium. Bureau De Change operators and street dealers are currently quoting the US dollar at an average of 1,365 to 1,370 for buying and between 1,375 and 1,390 for selling. This leaves a margin of roughly 45 to 55 Naira between the official and parallel market rates, driven by persistent demand from individuals and businesses seeking foreign exchange for international travel, tuition, and imports.

The relative stability in the official market is largely attributed to recent monetary policy adjustments and liquidity management by the Central Bank of Nigeria. Financial analysts have also pointed out that Nigeria’s rising net foreign reserves have strengthened the country’s external buffers and improved investor confidence.

Despite these positive economic indicators, the gap between the official and unofficial windows persists, reflecting the ongoing pressure of dollar demand outside the conventional banking system. Citizens exchanging dollars for naira are advised to confirm the prevailing rates with their commercial banks or authorised dealers, as figures may vary slightly depending on the transaction volume, location, and the specific exchange platform used.

World.title: IMF: Poverty Remains High in Nigeria Despite Economic Growth
World.content:
. Raises country’s 2026 growth forecast to 4.2%, retains 4.3% for 2027

Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday said despite Nigeria’s economic growth holding up, poverty remains high and the population continues to suffer, urging the government to provide targeted, temporary support to vulnerable households.

The Fund said the disproportionate increase in food and energy prices had intensified the cost-of-living crisis, highlighting the need for policymakers to balance the immediate needs of households with medium-term fiscal stability.

The IMF also upgraded Nigeria’s economic growth projection for 2026 by 0.1 percentage point to 4.2 per cent, while retaining its 2027 forecast at 4.3 per cent.

The projections were presented in the IMF’s 2026 World Economic Outlook, titled “Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices,” released at the ongoing Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

Speaking on fiscal policy responses to rising living costs in Africa, Research Department Division Chief, Deniz Igan, said policymakers needed to address immediate household needs, particularly food and energy security, while maintaining medium-term economic stability.

“The thing to emphasise here is that what we are advocating for is for policymakers to balance the near-term needs of the population, and that involves food security. That involves energy security. Given that the prices of food and energy are increasing disproportionately, while also keeping in mind medium-term stability, how to do that is, of course, a great question,” she said.
