World.title: How often should you call your mom? Be clear and kind when setting boundaries, expert says
World.content:
Article content

“Asking questions that are open-ended allows you to think a little bit deeper and it kind of prevents one party from curating answers to a simple question ahead of time,” Chandhok said. “It also shows if mom is asking their child, ‘What’s one thing that made you laugh today?’ or ‘What’s something that happened that made you go, huh, that was interesting?’ It kind of shows to the child that mom is interested in my day, and they’re not just asking me mundane questions that really don’t ask about me as a person in general.”

World.title: Colombia declares official start of El Niño, warns of strong impacts
World.content:
Colombia’s meteorological institute IDEAM officially declared the arrival of El Niño, and warned that the climate phenomenon could trigger water shortages and forest fires.

In a press statement, the IDEAM said that its “confirmation reflects the sustained warm conditions in the Pacific Ocean, which, according to the latest measurement, broke records, reaching a sea surface temperature anomaly of +3.49°C.”

The meteorological institute said it expected that this year’s “Godzilla El Niño” could continue to disrupt local climate patterns until March next year.

Initially, the weather phenomenon is expected to reduce rainfall between October and December, which is normally the rainy season in large parts of the country.

“Given this situation, and in light of the alerts issued since the beginning of the year, the national government launched an interagency response,.. with specific instructions for the responsible agencies to have their contingency plans formulated and activated by November 30 at the latest,” said the President’s Office in a statement.

The National Unit for Disaster Risk Management (UNGRD) coordinates response capabilities across the country and enhances the monitoring of wildfires using satellite technology. For its part, the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development is taking steps to protect strategic ecosystems, water sources, and the most vulnerable areas. President’s Office

The Mining Ministry “is implementing an emergency plan aimed at ensuring the country’s energy security by strengthening thermal power generation, securing fuel supplies, and implementing efficiency and conservation measures,” according to the President’s Office.

EPM, the local utilities firm in Medellin, has been testing the effectiveness of water rations as they fear the lack of rain could affect the hydro-electric power plants that provide the northwest of Colombia much of its energy.

Before leaving office on August 7, former President Gustavo Petro ordered the mass purchase of solar panels to reduce the pressure on the electric grid.

World.title: Colombia’s draft counterterrorist statute “creates foundations of dictatorial and inquisitorial regime:” opposition
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella’s antiterrorist statute would criminalize political opposition, social movements, and social protest, and essentially form a dictatorial regime, said opposition leader Ivan Cepeda on Wednesday.

In a video, Cepeda said that the true purpose of the bill that was leaked earlier seeks “to advance in the formation of essentially a dictatorial regime,.. which, moreover, has such a regime prostrate to drug trafficking.”

“The true objectives of this statute are to wage a crusade against the political opposition, social movements, and social protest, which is a legitimate right of citizens,” said the Senator of the Historic Pact party.

“Most of the articles in this draft are devoted to provisions that seriously undermine civil liberties, human rights, and the right to protest—not to illegal armed groups,’ according to Cepeda.

The broad legal definition of the word terrorism would allow the government to prosecute protest organizers on terrorism charges if any clashes occur between protesters and police.

This law could serve to intensify the persecution already underway in Colombia against journalists, judges, students, teachers, union members, peasants, indigenous people, people of African descent, LGBTIQ+ individuals—in short, any person or group that criticizes the citizen Abelardo de la Espriella, his government, law enforcement, or any state institution. Such a person could be taken to prison—without even prior warning—and subjected to abuse and torture. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Furthermore, the creation of a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors would allow the government to criminalize citizens based on an administrative rather than a legal basis, and “grants extraordinary powers to the president to regulate a statutory judicial procedure, specifically the expedited preventive detention proceeding,” said the opposition leader.

The aim is to criminalize social protest; the alleged crime of “manipulating the civilian population” punishes anyone who promotes, finances, organizes, or leads crowds—this is the language of the draft statute—and this is nothing less than the institutionalization of political persecution and the criminalization of free speech. Senator Ivan Cepeda

The antiterrorism statute will be facing opposition when the government tries to push the legislation through Congress, Cepeda said.

“The Historic Pact rejects this and will do whatever is necessary to ensure that the opposition’s rights and guarantees are respected,” said the opposition leader.

World.title: De la Espriella announces first $309M in aid for earthquake reconstruction
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that his Miracle Fund received COP1 trillion ($309 million) for the reconstruction of western Colombia, which was hit by a 7.4M earthquake on August 10.

The announcement followed announcements by the press, which reported that the Finance Ministry allocated ($192 million) COP625 billion to the fund almost two months after the disaster.

Thank you for your patience, but please understand that the government’s bureaucratic inertia and the situation we’ve inherited are extremely complex. However, we’re working to resolve the issue, and the Milagro Fund is now up and running, thanks to God and the efforts of all the officials in this administration. President Abelardo de la Espriella

“In November, the government will move forward with contracting another COP2.7 trillion ($835 million),” Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo told Caracol Radio.

The money is the first of an estimated COP30 trillion ($9.3 billion) that would be needed to rebuild the damage to airports, roads, hospitals and other public works.

The fund will be managed by De la Espriella’s general secretary, Carlos Rios, and a handful of businessmen with ties to the administration.

The announcement followed increased unrest about the government’s lack of response to the earthquake, which affected more than 400,000 people in the Valle del Cauca and Choco province, and the coffee region.

The government’s initial response was delayed because De la Espriella suspended the process to transfer power a month before he took office on August 7.

World.title: Colombia seeks to expand definition of terrorism in draft “counterterrorism statute”
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella will present Colombia’s Congress with a comprehensive “counterterrorism statute,” which would give authorities enhanced powers to fight designated terrorist organizations.

A 116-page draft bill, which was leaked to Caracol Radio, would facilitate a military approach to combat illegal armed groups and organized crime groups, for example through air strikes.

The Antiterrorism Statute would additionally create a National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors, which would make it easier to freeze the assets of suspected terrorists and their financiers.

Last but not least, the bill creates a presidential Terrorism Commissioner and a special prison regime for leaders of designated terrorist organizations.

Broader definition of terrorism

The bill seeks to change Colombia’s criminal law and define terrorism as any individual or collective conduct that produces “fear, panic or terror, creating risks, threats or the use of violence.”

A technical body of the National Security Council (NSC) will advise the council on the inclusion of organizations or individuals that ought to be included to its public National Registry of Terrorist Organizations and Actors.

Anyone who believes he was falsely put on the terror list can challenge this decision before the NSC and the Council of State, Colombia’s top administrative court.

The bill additionally seeks that “the Council of State shall hear, in the first instance, constitutional protection lawsuits filed against the President of the Republic or against defense authorities for acts or omissions related to operations by law enforcement agencies to preserve national security.”

This would make the suspension of military operations more difficult for citizens, who now can seek legal support to protect their constitutional rights at lower courts.

The bill also creates new crimes and modifies the penalties for conduct related to “terrorism,” such as the use of drones, illegal mining, oil theft, the extraction and sale of gold, kidnapping, smuggling, human trafficking, drug trafficking, extortion, cybercrimes, election crimes, riots, and attacks on critical infrastructure.

In the case of riots, “the penalty shall be increased by up to double when the riot is directed against law enforcement units conducting operations; or is carried out in conjunction with listed terrorist organizations.”

The bill also allows Colombian authorities to investigate and prosecute terrorism, terrorism financing or providing material support for terrorist organizations abroad.

High Counterterrorism Commissioner

The bill additionally seeks to expand presidential powers to create the Office of the High Counterterrorism Commissioner.

The expanded power would additionally give De la Espriella six months to regulate the powers of this new advisory office and to appoint its first commissioner.

World.title: Mayor from Colombia’s north claims De la Espriella’s armed men intimidated him
World.content:
The mayor of Sincelejo claimed Sunday that armed men intimidated him during a meeting with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a video message, Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña said that armed men positioned themselves behind him while the president accused the mayor of corruption and threatened to pull municipal funds.

The accusations were partly published on the social media pages of the president, who accused Acuña of being “a person who, like you, faces 13 corruption charges, has a video in which he explains how to embezzle funds from the PAE, and, on top of that, is set to stand trial in the Supreme Court of Justice on charges of illicit enrichment.”

So let’s see what we do with Sincelejo, but I do not work under your scheme of corruption. And if you think you can continue engaging in those practices, know that someone has arrived who is going to prevent it and that I am going to concentrate on it. This money, mister mayor, I will take care of it, and to take care of it I have to keep it away from your control. President Abelardo de la Espriella

In his response, Acuña claimed that De la Espriella’s video “has been edited and digitally manipulated.”

I ask you, please, to show the full video, where you can see how disciplinary and criminal codes are being violated in Colombia, where you can see how a mayor is being intimidated with rifles in the hands of civilians. How can a mayor be constantly flanked—for the entire duration of an event—by a person armed with a rifle, with the sole purpose of intimidating him? Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

Investigative journalist Laura Ardila said on social media platform X that sources from the province confirmed Acuña’s allegations.

Sources from the department who were present say—fearing they might be named—that they left the scene terrified. They claim that Acuña was indeed surrounded by heavily armed men in civilian clothing, that the president’s office was recording the entire time, and that, based on details like these, they believe it was a scene staged in advance to go viral. Journalist Laura Ardila

The mayor subsequently pointed out that the investigations into his alleged corruption existed before the presidential campaign, during which the De la Espriella campaign may have violated electoral laws, according to Acuña.

Among other things, the mayor said that he had been approached by De la Espriella’s parents to support the far-right president’s campaign and that local print shops may have received unreported campaign funds.

Since this needs to be clarified, mister President, it would be a good idea for the oversight agencies to investigate whether any printing shops in Sincelejo incurred campaign expenses that have not yet been reported to the National Electoral Council, whether there was campaign financing, and where that campaign financing came from, Mister President. Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

The mayor also pointed out that two members of the De la Espriella administration are being investigated on corruption charges and that the president had ties to the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

The president has repeatedly used corruption allegations to target political enemies.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: “Falkland Islanders will is to remain British, and we will uphold it”, PM Burnham told Trump
World.content:
“Falkland Islanders will is to remain British, and we will uphold it”, PM Burnham told Trump

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 09:13 UTC Full article

The Prime Minister believes a UK/EU summit will enhance chances for an open discussion “about our relationship with the EU in the longer term”.

“In my meeting with President Trump I raised the Falkland Islands and the clear and declared will of the Islanders to remain British”, revealed United Kingdom Prime Minister Andy Burnham in an oral statement to the House of Commons this Monday.

PM Burnham also emphasized that the point was made very clear in his speech to the UN General Assembly, “we will also always do whatever it takes to uphold Islanders’s will”.

The oral statement on his 22 September intervention before the UN General Assembly Burnham also reiterated support for Ukraine rejecting Russian aggresion, UK’s commitment with NATO and the proposal for a new National Centre for Information Defense, deepeniong collaboration with Germany, Italy and Japan.

On the Middle East situation he confirmed support for the US and Saudi Arabia, and protective security for shared bases.

“I want to thank our police and military personnel for their swift response. to the incidents at RAF Fairford and RAF Molesworth”, which he said is highly likely to have been coordinated and certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.

As to relations with the European Union, the PM anticipated a UK/EU summit in Brussels on 20th November, with the purpose of boosting UK growth and controlling illegal immigration. And this includes cutting costs and bureaucracy for sectors like farming and its food trade with EU.

On immigration, “we could link up our law enforcement efforts once again, sharing more data and criminal records of foreign nationals as well as faster electronic evidence from the phones of those behind the gangs”.

And “I believe our chances of doing so will be enhanced by being open to a discussion about our relationship with the EU in the longer term”.

Beyond Europe, a confident Britain is ready to play our part on the global stage as we take up the presidency of the G20 in 2027. “I confirmed in New York that we will place AI centre stage in our presidency, capturing the incredible opportunities it presents while guarding against the risks”.

Finally, the message at the UN and to the world is clear, after a decade of turbulence, Britain is back and can be relied upon as a consistent and stable partner in an uncertain world, always upholding the shared values set out in the UN Charter.

World.title: Brazil blames human action for the fires sweeping the Amazon
World.content:
Brazil blames human action for the fires sweeping the Amazon

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 06:29 UTC Full article

The fires coincide with an El Niño episode that forecasts place among the most intense in recent decades and that is usually associated with drought in the Amazon

The Brazilian government has blamed deliberate human action for the wave of fires in Amazonas state, where 540 new hotspots were recorded in 48 hours, more than half of those detected in the whole of October 2025, according to the National Institute for Space Research. The situation has led to a state of emergency in 36 municipalities.

Environment and Climate Change Minister João Paulo Capobianco flew over the region on Sunday with Integration and Regional Development Minister Waldez Góes and observed fire in hard-to-reach forest areas. Since fires do not occur spontaneously in the Amazon biome, the minister argues the outbreaks are the result of deliberate action, possibly to degrade the forest and prepare the ground for future clearing. “It is essential that those acting criminally see that they will be punished,” he said.

According to the institute’s data, 494 fires started in the state on Saturday 10, the highest figure of the month; on the same day in 2025, none were recorded. There were 874 hotspots in the whole of October 2025.

The smoke led civil defence authorities in Manaus, the state capital, to issue a health warning on Friday over air pollution. A joint municipal, state and federal operation is fighting the fires. The federal environment agency, Ibama, sent four water-bombing aircraft, two helicopters and 290 firefighters, and the air force added two KC-390 aircraft on Sunday. “It is one thing to deploy all the forces we can to put out the fire. It is another to assist people who need humanitarian aid and medical care because of the fires,” Góes said.

The fires coincide with an El Niño episode that forecasts place among the most intense in recent decades and that is usually associated with drought in the Amazon, while it brings extreme rainfall and flooding to the south of the continent.

World.title: IMF trims Latin America’s outlook to 2.3% and sharply cuts Argentina’s
World.content:
IMF trims Latin America’s outlook to 2.3% and sharply cuts Argentina’s

13th Tuesday, October 2026 - 06:19 UTC Full article

Globally, the Fund forecasts growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while global inflation would rise to 4.7% this year, driven by energy and food

The International Monetary Fund has lowered its 2026 growth forecast for Latin America and the Caribbean to 2.3%, a tenth of a point less than in July, and sharply cut Argentina’s, from 3.5% to 2.1%. Chile and Uruguay are also among the region’s largest downward revisions, according to the World Economic Outlook presented on Monday in Bangkok, during the annual meetings of the Fund and the World Bank.

For Argentina, Fund economist Petya Koeva Brooks attributed the 1.4-point cut to “lower activity observed through the third quarter of this year” and to “weaker domestic demand in a context of still tight domestic financial conditions and the continued structural transformation of the economy”. The Fund also raised its forecast for average inflation this year to 32.5%, from 30.4% in April, and for 2027 to 21.2%, from 15.7%. It projects unemployment of 7.6% in 2026 and 7.1% in 2027. Argentina’s growth forecast for next year was revised from 4% to 3.5%. Economy Minister Luis Caputo is attending the meetings.

Uruguay’s forecast was cut by half a point to 1.3%, in line with the Fund mission that visited the country in September, which attributed the slowdown to the impact of drought on farming. Chile saw the largest adjustment, of 1.8 points. Brazil would grow 2.2% this year and 1.9% in 2027, two and three tenths less than in July, because of still-tight monetary conditions and the withdrawal of fiscal support. For the region, the Fund expects 2.5% growth in 2027 and inflation of 6.8% this year, excluding Venezuela. According to the report, higher energy prices benefit commodity exporters and hurt importers.

Globally, the Fund forecasts growth of 3.1% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while global inflation would rise to 4.7% this year, driven by energy and food. It assumes an average oil price of US$95.74 a barrel in 2026, against US$67.74 in 2025, and that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen in March 2027.

In the United States, headline inflation would rise to 3.6% this year and fall to 2.8% in 2027, while the economy would grow 2.3% in both years, supported by consumption, fiscal policy and investment in artificial intelligence. The Fund identifies a prolonged war in the Middle East and an abrupt correction in expectations about artificial intelligence as the main risks.

World.title: Iguazú Falls closed as the river’s flow tops 12,000 cubic metres per second
World.content:
Iguazú Falls closed as the river’s flow tops 12,000 cubic metres per second

12th Monday, October 2026 - 22:09 UTC Full article

The river rose just over two metres between Sunday and Monday at Puerto Iguazú and reached a level of 24.30 metres, and was still rising

Iguazú National Park, in Argentina’s Misiones province, closed access to the falls’ walkways on Monday because of an exceptional rise in the Iguazú River, whose flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second. The flood is part of an episode of heavy rainfall linked to El Niño that has also caused the Uruguay River to burst its banks, with evacuations on both sides.

According to the Argentine Naval Prefecture, the river rose just over two metres between Sunday and Monday at Puerto Iguazú and reached a level of 24.30 metres, and was still rising. The alert level is 25 metres and the evacuation level 28. The park authority and the concessionaire halted ticket sales during Monday’s public holiday and inspected trails and infrastructure, where some small trees fell. “We may be able to open normally tomorrow,” park authorities told the newspaper La Nación. The flood had been forecast weeks in advance by the National Parks Administration.

Cierre total en las Cataratas del Iguazú por crecida histórica Las intensas y extraordinarias lluvias registradas en las cuencas de los ríos Paraná e Iguazú obligaron a las autoridades a cerrar de manera preventiva el acceso al público en el Parque Nacional Iguazú. De acuerdo con las autoridades, el flujo de agua superó los 12.000 metros cúbicos por segundo, lo que representa casi 10 veces el volumen normal de los saltos. Imágenes : Tiempo_AMBA en X y lucasdiaz.birding en Instagram — EL TIEMPO (@ELTIEMPO) October 12, 2026

Rain in the upper basin, in southern Brazil, has also swollen the Uruguay River. In Uruguay, the first families were evacuated in Salto on October 10, and the departmental emergency committee has gone into permanent session. In Paysandú, the river reached 6.25 metres on Sunday, close to the evacuation level of 6.89, and 35 people had to leave their homes, some housed in army tents. The ferry service between Monte Caseros and Bella Unión was suspended.

On the Argentine side, seven families were evacuated in Concordia, where the river is expected to stay around 11.60 metres until Thursday, and 31 people in Paso de los Libres. The binational Salto Grande dam is releasing about 18,000 cubic metres per second.

Forecasts place the current El Niño among the most intense in recent decades. Last week, an atmospheric river intensified by the same phenomenon brought Santiago, Chile, its wettest October on record and a mudslide in the Las Condes district.

World.title: Republican senators urge Trump to cancel the Putin diesel deal as unlawful
World.content:
Republican senators urge Trump to cancel the Putin diesel deal as unlawful

12th Monday, October 2026 - 21:57 UTC Full article

Four Republican and three Democratic members of the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee have urged President Donald Trump to “immediately reverse course” on his diesel supply deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin, arguing it contravenes the law banning Russian energy imports. It is the most direct Republican criticism of a Trump foreign policy decision in his current term.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians,” said a statement released on Sunday by Republicans Lisa Murkowski, Susan Collins, Thom Tillis and John Curtis and Democrats Jeanne Shaheen, Ron Wyden and Richard Blumenthal. “Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin’s brutal war against Ukraine,” they added. Shaheen, the committee’s ranking Democrat, said the law requires consultation with Congress and a formal review process, and that the administration “appears to have bypassed both”.

Tillis said the deal may be illegal. Murkowski urged Trump to use the law to increase sanctions and tariffs on Russia “instead of allowing Russia to export diesel, rake in revenues, and continue its catastrophic war in Ukraine”. Senator John Barrasso, the number two in the Republican majority, defended the decision, saying the president “has to make tough decisions”.

Trump announced on Friday that Russia would supply some 4.8 million tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, and the Treasury issued a licence temporarily suspending sanctions on Russian diesel until April 2027. The deal comes weeks after Trump himself signed a law tightening sanctions on Russia’s energy and financial sectors. On Sunday, following the criticism, the president announced that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other’s energy infrastructure.

Diesel prices, near record highs because of the war with Iran, are a central issue in the November 3 midterm elections, in which Republicans trail in the polls. According to a Financial Times poll, only a quarter of voters approve of Trump’s handling of the economy. At a rally in Tennessee on Saturday, the president blamed the rise in diesel prices on Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.

World.title: Lula takes to the streets of São Paulo to close the gap two weeks before the runoff
World.content:
Lula takes to the streets of São Paulo to close the gap two weeks before the runoff

12th Monday, October 2026 - 10:50 UTC Full article

With so few undecided voters, the Workers’ Party strategy is focused on the roughly 33 million Brazilians who did not vote in the first round

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva led a large rally on São Paulo’s Avenida Paulista on Sunday to relaunch his campaign two weeks before the October 25 runoff, in which he trails Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. “This country cannot lose its democracy,” he told a largely young crowd.

The first Datafolha poll since the first round, published on Thursday, gives Bolsonaro 49% of voting intentions and Lula 45%; in valid votes, 52% to 48%. The pollster considers it a statistical tie at the limit of the margin of error. Only 1% say they are undecided. Some 46% of respondents say they would never vote for Lula, and 43% reject Bolsonaro. In the first round, the Liberal Party candidate won 47.03% of valid votes and Lula 45.16%, according to the Superior Electoral Court’s final count.

With so few undecided voters, the Workers’ Party strategy is focused on the roughly 33 million Brazilians who did not vote in the first round. The campaign has stepped up its social media presence with testimonies from beneficiaries of social programmes and messages aimed at people over 70 and 16- and 17-year-olds, for whom voting is not compulsory. Lula heads a seven-party alliance ranging from the left-wing Socialism and Liberty Party to the centre-right represented by his running mate, Geraldo Alckmin.

At the rally, the president promised for a new term “a technological revolution” to boost the digital industry and “a revolution in public security so that people are safe and criminals are put in jail”.

Bolsonaro, for his part, urged supporters not to relax and met the ten allied governors elected in the first round. “Brazil has had enough of Lula. Enough,” he said. The senator, who has won the backing of former candidates Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, proposes a constitutional reform to overhaul the judiciary, lower the age of criminal responsibility and abolish re-election.

Since direct presidential elections returned in 1989, no candidate who came second in the first round has won the runoff.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV to undergo surgery on a lung nodule a month before his tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV to undergo surgery on a lung nodule a month before his tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru

12th Monday, October 2026 - 08:59 UTC Full article

The tour will begin in Uruguay, from November 6 to 8. The Pope will then travel to Argentina, where he will stay until the 11th, with events in Buenos Aires, Córdoba and Luján

Pope Leo XIV will undergo surgery in Rome this week to remove a lung nodule detected at an early stage, less than a month before the start of his first tour of South America, which will take him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17. The Vatican has announced no changes to the trip.

“Recently, during some check-ups, doctors found a circumscribed nodule in my lung. It was detected at a very early stage and is well localised,” the 71-year-old pontiff said after the Angelus prayer in St Peter’s Square on Sunday. He said he had accepted the medical recommendation to have it removed.

Holy See spokesman Matteo Bruni confirmed that the operation will take place early this week at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and that the Pope will remain in hospital for about seven days. The Vatican has not specified the nature of the lesion.

The tour will begin in Uruguay, from November 6 to 8. The Pope will then travel to Argentina, where he will stay until the 11th, with events in Buenos Aires, Córdoba and Luján and a meeting with President Javier Milei. The final stop will be Peru, from the 11th to the 17th, where Leo XIV served as bishop of Chiclayo. The Holy See said the final decision will depend on the Pope’s progress after surgery.

Milei expressed his support on X: “All of Argentina is with Your Holiness in affection and prayer, wishing you a speedy and complete recovery.”

World.title: Lawyers and opposition challenge Milei’s citizenship-by-investment scheme as unconstitutional
World.content:
Lawyers and opposition challenge Milei’s citizenship-by-investment scheme as unconstitutional

12th Monday, October 2026 - 08:56 UTC Full article

The programme, presented in Paris on October 2 by Economy Minister Luis Caputo and Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli, is based on a May 2025 emergency decree

The citizenship-by-investment programme launched by Javier Milei’s government, which allows foreigners to obtain Argentine nationality in exchange for a US$350,000 contribution to the Treasury or the purchase of a US$800,000 bond, faces challenges from constitutional lawyers and from the opposition, which is trying to block it in Congress.

The programme, presented in Paris on October 2 by Economy Minister Luis Caputo and Cabinet Chief Diego Santilli, is based on a May 2025 emergency decree. It also provides for additional payments of US$100,000 for a spouse and for each child aged 18 to 25, and US$25,000 for each minor, so a family with two minor children would pay US$500,000.

“The national Constitution, in its Article 20, is very clear: Argentine citizenship by naturalisation is obtained with two years of residence or by rendering some exceptional service to the country. It does not allow citizenship to be bought,” constitutional lawyer Andrés Gil Domínguez told the newspaper El País. In his view, the decree does not meet the necessity and urgency requirements that allow the executive to bypass Congress, and the measure is “totally discriminatory on the basis of economic status”. According to the newspaper, the courts have already declared the decree null in two individual cases.

In Congress, the opposition has filed requests for information and bills to repeal it. “It is unacceptable for Argentina to put its citizenship up for sale,” said Peronist deputy Agustín Rossi, a former defence minister, who called the proposal “classist” and argued it is aimed at attracting billionaires seeking to avoid restrictions that apply to foreigners, such as on buying land.

The government argues that the programme “will encourage investment and job creation” and that the funds will be used to strengthen the country’s fiscal position. Caputo attributed investor interest to “Argentina’s optimal geopolitical situation, particularly in a world in conflict”, and said applicants will undergo a “rigorous” vetting of their identity, criminal record and sources of funds.

Representatives of five private firms specialising in residence and citizenship-by-investment programmes — Latitude Group, Arton Capital, Apex Capital Partners, Passport Legacy and AIM Global — took part in the announcement and said they had formed a consortium and signed an unpaid technical collaboration agreement in May with the Economy Ministry agency managing the programme.

Argentina would be the first South American country with such a programme.

World.title: Dozens hurt in major protest against contaminated water in Guadalajara
World.content:
Dozens of people were hurt and 39 arrested Sunday when a march demanding clean tap water ended in clashes outside the Jalisco governor’s residence, with police firing tear gas canisters and blasting protesters with water cannons.

About 10,000 people participated, according to state authorities, amid anger over cloudy, foul-smelling water reaching homes across the Guadalajara metropolitan area — a “crisis” (as the governor himself has termed it) that has persisted for months.

Policías estatales rodean y retiran a un joven entre empujones, mientras manifestantes se acercan y graban la detención. El momento ocurrió al término de la marcha por agua limpia en #Guadalajara, que este domingo avanzó de La Minerva a #CasaJalisco. Frente al inmueble hubo enfrentamientos y se reportaron detenciones; hasta el momento no se había informado una cifra oficial. 📹: Redes sociales AC. — La Silla Rota (@lasillarota) October 11, 2026

Officials reported 28 injured police officers, two seriously, and 31 civilians who required medical attention.

The Jalisco prosecutor’s office said 12 detainees were released Sunday night and early Monday, leaving 27 in custody. Those freed remain under investigation, according to news reports.

Demonstrators marched about 1.5 kilometers from the Minerva roundabout in western Guadalajara to Casa Jalisco, the official residence of Jalisco’s governor, Pablo Lemus of the Citizens’ Movement (MC) party — who last week announced a water rationing plan aimed at addressing the crisis.

Some tore down a barricade and threw rocks and sticks before riot police deployed tear gas and water cannons, according to media reports.

State officials blamed the violence on roughly 400 people, many wearing hoods, saying the march had proceeded peacefully before their arrival. That account has not been independently verified.

In her morning press conference Monday, President Claudia Sheinbaum questioned the police response, saying authorities must distinguish between containing violence and repressing demonstrations. She demanded that Lemus explain the use of force and identify those arrested.

Lemus said he had requested a case-by-case review of the arrests and an examination of video footage for possible police abuses.

The Jalisco State Human Rights Commission received five complaints alleging abuses and requested medical attention and prompt determinations of detainees’ legal status.

The University of Guadalajara said Sunday that three of its students had been arrested and called for their safety and release.

ITESO, a Jesuit university in Tlaquepaque, also said members of its community had been detained but did not specify how many.

The protest followed months of complaints, dating back to April and even last year, about discolored water. Lemus blamed deteriorating infrastructure and irregular discharges into a canal feeding the Las Pintas dam.

The state announced a six-month suspension of supplies from the dam, reducing available water and potentially requiring tanker deliveries to some neighborhoods.

While the Jalisco government estimated attendance at Sunday’s protest at about 10,000, an AI-assisted analysis by University of Guadalajara researchers put the midday crowd at about 21,400, with a probable range of 16,200 to 27,200, UDGTV reported.

With reports from Infobae, El Financiero, SDP Noticias, Uno TV and UDGTV

World.title: Nestlé to invest additional US $1B in Mexico before 2030
World.content:
Swiss food and beverage multinational Nestlé plans to increase its announced investment in Mexico from US $1 billion to $2 billion during President Claudia Sheinbaum’s administration, Sheinbaum announced on Thursday after hosting CEO Philipp Navratil at the National Palace on Wednesday.

“In 2028-2030, they will boost national production and local supply with 70,000 coffee plants and the incorporation of 2,000 producers from Veracruz,” added Sheinbaum.

Ayer recibimos en Palacio Nacional al director ejecutivo de Nestlé, Philipp Navratil; nos informó que duplicarán la inversión en México, al pasar de mil a dos mil millones de dólares durante el sexenio. En 2028-2030, impulsarán la producción nacional y el abastecimiento local con 70 mil plantas de café y la incorporación de dos mil productores de Veracruz. — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) October 9, 2026

This marks the second time Sheinbaum has met with Nestlé executives during her presidency, following discussions at the National Palace in January 2025.

Then, Sheinbaum met with Nestlé CEO for the Americas, Steve Presley, and the CEO of Nestlé Mexico, Fausto Costa, who had announced a $1 billion investment for the 2025-2027 period. “That investment has already been completed,” Sheinbaum said during her Oct. 9 morning press conference.

The prior investment supported the expansion of production lines at plants in Veracruz, Guanajuato, Querétaro and México state, as well as a new US $180M distribution center in Zumpango, México state, which aims to transform Mexico into an export hub for Nestlé.

In 2025, Mexico was Nestlé’s fourth-most-important market worldwide and its second-most-attractive market for investment.

Mexico and the European Union signed a modernized economic agreement in May 2026 aimed at deepening trade, investment and political cooperation. The agreement could create additional expansion opportunities for European businesses operating in Mexico, although its full implementation remains subject to ratification.

With reports from El Economista, Infobae and Imagen del Golfo

World.title: Did the killing of ‘El Mencho’ in February change the cartel he led? US report offers clues
World.content:
The death in February of Nemesio Rubén “El Mencho” Oseguera Cervantes did not lead to “large-scale fragmentation” of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), but there are signs that “some structural weakening” of the criminal organization “may have occurred,” according to a U.S. State Department-affiliated security body.

Osegeura, the founder and erstwhile leader of the CJNG, was fatally wounded during a Mexican military operation in Jalisco on Feb. 22.

In an Oct. 9 report titled “CJNG After El Mencho,” the Overseas Security Advisory Council (OSAC) — a public-private partnership between security professionals from global U.S. organizations and the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service — noted that “armed CJNG personnel attacked businesses and implemented roadblocks across Mexico” in retaliation for the operation against Oseguera.

It also wrote that “El Mencho’s death sparked fears of potential intra-cartel violence, as some believed CJNG ranking members might compete for control over CJNG.”

Why hasn’t ‘large-scale fragmentation’ of the CJNG occurred?

OSAC said that “analysts can evaluate the law enforcement action against El Mencho as an example of a decapitation strike, in which a government attempts to limit the power of a criminal group by removing its leader and thereby fragmenting operations that rely on a central figure of authority.”

“In this case, the intention may have been to remove the top-level leader that inspired loyalty among high-ranking CJNG members and cause the franchise cells to fragment without executive-level direction,” OSAC said.

However, “large-scale fragmentation” of the CJNG “has not occurred” since El Mencho’s death, OSAC said. It suggested such fragmentation hasn’t occurred because “El Mencho had been under such intense pressure from the looming threat of arrest that the daily operations of CJNG had already begun to function without him.”

“The success of the brand of CJNG might have outgrown loyalty to El Mencho as an individual,” OSAC said.

No ‘significant violent competition for the top spot in CJNG’

OSAC noted that “some sources,” including the U.S. Department of State, have identified Juan Carlos Valencia González — El Mencho’s stepson — as the new leader of the CJNG.

“Other analysis suggests that CJNG has not named a new single top leader but instead relies on its network of several powerful regional leaders,” OSAC said.

“In either case, there was not a significant violent competition for the top spot in CJNG, which some analysts feared following El Mencho’s death.”

OSAC said that the absence of “significant violent competition” to succeed Osegura “may have been due to the slow shift away from centralized authority under El Mencho.”

“The relatively stable continuity of leadership has left most of CJNG’s regional operations intact,” OSAC added.

“For example, residents of Michoacán began reporting the resumption of drone attacks by CJNG members in March, just weeks after … El Mencho’s death. Furthermore, CJNG is reportedly engaging in renewed inter-cartel violence with the Mayiza faction of the Sinaloa cartel, suggesting CJNG’s resources are robust enough to defend territory.”

Are authorities winning the fight against the CJNG?

While the CJNG continues to operate across much of Mexico, the criminal organization was “not entirely unaffected” by the death of El Mencho, according to OSAC.

“CJNG has not conducted a large-scale attack or territorial push since February,” OSAC wrote.

“This suggests that although they are not dismantled, some structural weakening may have occurred, limiting their capacity to impose themselves against rivals.”

OSAC noted that law enforcement actions have “continued to successfully capture CJNG personnel throughout Mexico,” including Audias “El Jardinero” Flores Silva, a former security chief for El Mencho.

“In August, Mexican security minister Omar García Harfuch announced that law enforcement operations across Hidalgo, Jalisco, and Michoacán had resulted in the arrest of 32 CJNG members,” OSAC wrote.

“Arrests have been particularly effective against the money laundering facilitators of CJNG, the Cuinis, whose leadership has been arrested, limiting their influence. Both Mexican and U.S. authorities have also been effective at freezing accounts and assets linked to CJNG and its members,” OSAC said.

The Overseas Security Advisory Council said that “[c]larity as to how strong CJNG remains since El Mencho’s death will become apparent as more reliable crime data is produced, including a clearer picture of homicides, disappearances, and measures of illicit activity in areas where CJNG predominates.”

“A precipitous fall in homicides in areas like Jalisco and Michoacan where CJNG controls large swaths of territory would be a sign that law enforcement actions have been effective at limiting CJNG’s influence,” OSAC wrote.

Data presented by the federal government on Sept. 8 showed that homicides declined 39.6% in annual terms in Jalisco in the first eight months of 2026. The year-over-year decline in homicides in Michoacán in the same period was slightly higher at 40.5%.

The significant reductions in homicides in Jalisco and Michoacán, as well as the arrests of numerous alleged CJNG members, indicate that the government is indeed making progress in weakening the powerful criminal organization in those states.

However, there is still plenty of work to do. Jalisco and Michoacán ranked among the 11 most violent states in Mexico in terms of total homicides between January and August, and some states where the CJNG operates, such as Guanajuato, México state and Guerrero, recorded even higher murder rates in the first eight months of 2026.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Acapulco will work with Quintana Roo’s tourism sector to lure back international visitors
World.content:
The resort and port city of Acapulco, Guerrero, is seeking to attract more international visitors by working together with the tourist mecca Quintana Roo.

One of the main aims is to capitalize on the new direct air route between Cancún, Quintana Roo, and Acapulco, with operations by Viva Aerobus scheduled to begin on Nov. 3. The connection will facilitate travel between the Mexican Caribbean and Pacific coasts, thus opening up opportunities to encourage visitors arriving in Quintana Roo to extend their visit to Acapulco.

The cooperation initiative, spearheaded by Acapulco Mayor Abelina López Rodríguez, entails the signing of collaboration agreements to strengthen commercial ties between the two destinations and expand opportunities for mutual tourism promotion.

To that end, Acapulco Tourism Minister Noé Peralta Herrera will undertake a working tour of Cancún and Playa del Carmen this week, where he will hold meetings with travel agencies, tour operators and industry representatives.

“We must form alliances and work together with travel agencies, tour operators, and our business partners to recover the foreign market,” Peralta said in a statement.

More Acapulco tourism additions — and one setback

Acapulco welcomed back Monday the Eurodam — a Holland America Line cruise ship owned by Carnival Corporation — after a 17-year hiatus in the port city.

Another novelty includes a new direct Puebla-Acapulco air route, operated by Volaris, which will launch on Dec. 1, 2026.

With a duration of 55 minutes, the flight is part of Puebla International Airport’s expanded offerings and provides an alternative for travelers wishing to visit Acapulco without making the journey by road.

Details released for the inaugural flight indicate a departure time of 11:55 a.m., with ticket prices starting at 457 pesos per person (US $25).

Furthermore, in an interview with the newspaper Milenio, Peralta shared plans to advance the recovery of flights to and from destinations in Canada, as well as Los Angeles and Chicago. According to Peralta, Chicago is home to a community of more than 500,000 people from Guerrero.

Efforts to boost tourism in Acapulco suffered a recent setback as rough seas associated with Hurricane Simon led to the cancellation of the scheduled Oct. 11 arrival of the Norwegian Joy, a cruise that was expected to bring 3,555 passengers and 1,623 crew members.

With reports from El Universal and Quadratín Guerrero

World.title: FT: Trump raised energy deals with Sheinbaum amid stalled trade talks
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexico to sign energy deals with U.S. companies, “triggering alarm in Mexico City,” according to the Financial Times (FT).

The British newspaper’s reporting is based on information it received from three people said to be familiar with a telephone conversation between Trump and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum in mid-September.

“Donald Trump has pressed Mexico to ink energy deals with U.S. companies as trade talks between Washington and its largest trading partner stall, triggering alarm in Mexico City where foreign investment in the sector is highly sensitive,” FT wrote in a report published last Friday.

“The U.S. president insisted in a call with his counterpart Claudia Sheinbaum last month that there should be more deals and tie-ups between Mexican and U.S. energy companies, according to three people familiar with the call.”

FT wrote that one of its sources said that Trump initially asked Sheinbaum about a deal to sell Mexican assets to the U.S. The completion of such a deal would be highly unlikely given that the Mexican government is seeking to strengthen energy sovereignty, rather than sell off assets.

Citing two of its sources, FT reported that Trump and Sheinbaum “also discussed a deal similar to the one signed last year with South Korea, in which Seoul agreed to buy [US] $100bn of U.S. energy products and invest billions more in the U.S.”

Citing a U.S. official, FT said the two leaders “discussed the prospect of Mexico increasing purchases of U.S. natural gas, on which it already depends for about three-quarters of its demand.”

“The official added that the talks were focused on reducing Mexico’s trade surplus with the U.S.,” the newspaper wrote.

That surplus increased more than 20% year over year in the first eight months of 2026, climbing to almost $156 billion. The size of Mexico’s surplus has drawn the ire of Trump, who argues that the U.S. has long gotten a raw deal on trade with countries around the world.

State control of energy meets US trade pressure

FT didn’t disclose anything about Sheinbaum’s response to Trump’s apparent push for energy deals and asset sales.

However, the newspaper did write that Sheinbaum’s party, Morena, “has put state control of energy at the heart of its agenda.”

Just last week, Energy Minister Luz Elena González told reporters that the government is targeting a 60% public share of electricity generation, above the 54% share mandated by law. The government, like its predecessor, has poured money into Pemex to strengthen the state oil company after what Sheinbaum and former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador describe as decades of neglect during Mexico’s so-called “neoliberal period.”

Under López Obrador, the Mexican government rolled back parts of a 2014 reform that opened up Mexico’s energy sector to foreign and private companies.

However, FT reported that “Sheinbaum is cautiously trying to restart pockets of private investment in the ailing [energy] sector as oil production hits record lows and cities have experienced blackouts due to strain on the electricity grid.”

“State companies Pemex and CFE, however, will remain dominant,” the newspaper added.

Trump’s reported pressure on the Mexican president came at a time when the United States and Mexico continued to engage in trade talks. On July 1, the U.S. government announced that it had declined to renew the USMCA trade pact in its “current form,” and since then it has been discussing a range of trade issues with Mexico.

While the USMCA remains in effect, and most Mexican exports enter the U.S. tariff-free, the Mexican government is seeking to have U.S. duties on steel, aluminum and vehicles reduced, if not eliminated.

FT’s reporting indicates that Trump could be conditioning tariff reductions on energy sector concessions from Mexico. Citing two of its sources, the newspaper said that the United States’ “new request on energy” contributed to a delay of a formal round of trade talks which were scheduled for September and which have not yet been rescheduled.

Earlier this year, the Office of the United States Trade Representative strongly criticized Mexico’s energy sector framework, raising a range of concerns that it says disadvantage U.S. energy companies.

US gas imports rise despite sovereignty push

Mexico’s imports of natural gas from the United States increased in the first seven months of 2026 to reach a record high of 6.8 billion cubic feet per day, according to data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The year-over-year increase in the period was 1.8%.

Mexico’s natural gas imports from the U.S. have now increased in the January-July period of four consecutive years. In May, June and July, daily imports of U.S. natural gas — a key fuel for industry and electricity generation — averaged more than 7 billion cubic feet per day. The newspaper El Economista reported that it was the first time that imports exceeded that mark during three consecutive months.

Sheinbaum is determined to reduce Mexico’s reliance on imported natural gas and, to that end, has changed her stance on fracking, asserting that the controversial gas and oil extraction technique can now take place sustainably and safely.

However, her government has not yet authorized fracking projects in northern Mexico, where significant non-conventional gas and oil reserves are believed to be located, and even if it were to do so soon, it would likely be years before Mexico could meaningfully reduce its gas imports from the U.S.

Whether Mexico is prepared to further increase its purchases of U.S. natural gas — as Trump would apparently like to see happen — remains to be seen. While Sheinbaum is determined to strengthen Mexico’s energy sovereignty, the need for imported gas will ultimately depend on domestic demand and supply.

One potential supplier of additional natural gas to Mexico is the U.S. state of New Mexico. New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham traveled to Mexico City last month, with the aim of advancing “potential trade deals in natural gas exports,” according to the governor’s office.

With reports from Financial Times and El Economista

World.title: Senate unanimously approves measure amending Tourism Law to prevent child sexual exploitation
World.content:
The Mexican Senate has approved an amendment to the General Tourism Law aimed at preventing the sexual exploitation of children and adolescents.

A new measure will require tourism service providers to verify, via official documentation, the kinship, parental authority, guardianship or care and custody status of minors traveling with adults. If such a relationship cannot be proven, service providers, such as hotels and rentals, must refuse their booking — regardless of whether it is made in person or electronically — and immediately notify authorities for further investigation.

It has yet to be established which official documents will serve as proof of identity, and what specific tourism providers will be obliged to comply. As noted by the lawyer Magda Zayas in an opinion piece for the newspaper Diario del Istmo, the amendment’s effective implementation will require training of front-line personnel and critical back-end updates to online booking systems that operate in Mexico.

Citing data from World Vision Mexico, the Senate said in a statement that the country is the second-largest destination for the sexual exploitation of children and adolescents, and it ranks first globally in the consumption of child pornography.

PAN Senator Laura Esquivel Torres said that Mexico will stop being a destination for sexual exploitation of minors thanks to the amendment.

“Pedophiles don’t come to Mexico by chance; they come because they have the opportunity to do so here, because they know Mexico is a pedophile’s paradise. Well, starting today, we will begin to shut down these opportunities,” Esquivel said.

Meanwhile, PRI Senator Carolina Viggiano Austria mentioned that more than 16,000 children are trapped in sexual exploitation networks in Mexico, primarily in tourist destinations.

According to the bill, the Tourism Ministry has defined the sexual exploitation of minors in the tourism sector as occurring when an offender poses as a domestic or foreign tourist and travels to a specific destination to initiate sexual contact with minors.

The bill was approved unanimously, with 104 votes, and sent to the president’s office for signing.

Similar initiatives are taking place at the local level. In May, the Association of Hotels of Cancún, Puerto Morelos and Isla Mujeres (AHCPMIM), Quintana Roo, formalized its commitment to “The Code,” a global initiative seeking to eradicate the sexual exploitation of children and adolescents in the travel and tourism sector.

With reports from Reportur and Uno TV

World.title: MND Local Guadalajara: October food and music fests abound, while officials investigate contamination at Huaxtla Falls
World.content:
Music and gastronomy take center stage this month with celebrations in Zapopan’s historic center, a beer tasting at Foro Expo Guadalajara, and free mariachi performances. But first, we cover the recent investigations into sewage contamination at the popular nature spot Huaxtla Falls in north Zapopan.

Local residents complain of sewage contamination at Huaxtla Falls

Located in the Sierra de Huaxtla in the municipality of Zapopan, Jalisco, about 40 to 60 minutes (about 28 miles) from Guadalajara, Huaxtla Falls is a popular nature spot for locals and tourists. The site’s normally turquoise rock pools and idyllic setting within the Cañón del Jaguar, with the tallest waterfall reaching a height of 24 meters (about 78 feet), are a stunning natural wonder.

Now, area residents, local environmental groups and researchers are up in arms over the discovery of a thick, foul-smelling toxic leachate runoff turning the once-pristine waters an opaque brown.

The local environmental group Center for Studies and Research of the Barranca (CEIBA) has pointed the finger at the Picachos and Hasar’s landfills, which operate upstream from the falls, processing the GMA’s considerable waste stream. Both have a history of dumping garbage runoff into the river basin, with contamination carried by the Milpillas River downstream to the Santiago River, which feeds Huaxtla Falls.

In addition to spoiling Huaxtla Falls, several communities downstream — including Ixcatán, La Soledad, San Lorenzo and Milpillas — rely on this water for their livestock and crops.

Nearby residents have expressed anger over governmental inaction. Notably, the federal environmental watchdog agency, Profepa, missed a scheduled inspection in mid-September, while previous cleanup agreements dating back to 2009 by the Zapopan city council have gone unfulfilled.

Following the most recent complaints, Jalisco Gov. Pablo Lemus Navarro confirmed that Profepa has intervened and placed closure seals on the specific area where the leachate leak occurred. He added that the immediate runoff has been contained to prevent further damage to the river basin and natural areas, including Huaxtla Falls.

For its part, Zapopan’s City Council acknowledged operational failures in managing wastewater at the Picachos landfill during the recent rainy season.

At the end of September, representatives from Profepa and the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat) finally carried out a “verification” tour of the Huaxtla Waterfalls. During the visit, they documented the deterioration in water quality, took samples and announced several remedial measures to clean up the pollution.

Park representatives, ejido (farming collective) members, residents and small landowners from Ixcatán, La Soledad, Huaxtla, San Lorenzo and Milpillas also participated in the tour.

Formal technical and scientific investigations are ongoing to determine the source of the contamination and extent of the environmental damage before assigning legal blame.

Chela Fest 2026 is coming to the Guadalajara Expo

Attention beer lovers! Chela Fest GDL celebrates its first edition this coming weekend at Expo Guadalajara, bringing together artisanal breweries, gastronomy, live music and immersive experiences under one roof.

Attendees will have the opportunity to meet and mingle with owners and brewmasters from 25 different breweries and sample different beer styles from among 100 different brands. The event also promises live music from local artists, including Bahía Colors, Softgun and Punch, plus interactive experiences on both days, including a costume contest on Saturday and Cowboy Sunday, where guests can don their Stetsons and enjoy camaraderie with friends and family.

Confirmed brewers participating in this year’s event include local favorites Cervecería Fortuna and Loba Cerveza, as well as Mula Prieta, Gulden Draak and HereXe. For more details, check the event’s social media.

Dates: Oct. 17–18, 2026, from noon to 10 p.m.

Location: Foro Expo Guadalajara

Cost: Tickets start at 150 pesos and are available on BoletoMóvil or at local brewpubs such as Loba Cerveza in Colonia Americana.

Free mariachi nights in downtown Guadalajara this month

Recognized as part of UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity since 2011, mariachi music is synonymous with Jalisco.

This month, downtown Guadalajara is hosting free mariachi performances on Paseo Alcalde, directly across from the Rotonda de los Hombres Ilustres, so come out and enjoy the festivities with family and friends. The pedestrian promenade should offer plenty of room for dancing and delighting in one of Jalisco’s most cherished pastimes.

The final mariachi performance of this series is happening Oct. 16, starting at 7 p.m. The concert is free to all, with no reservations or tickets required.

Day of the Dead Gastronomic Festival in Zapopan

The Day of the Dead Food Festival returns to downtown Zapopan for two days, Oct. 31 and Nov. 1, in Plaza de las Américas.

Beyond the ubiquitous pan de muerto, guests can expect a diverse offering of hearty dishes to sample, including tamales, tacos, pozole rojo and sweet treats, with traditional hot drinks such as café de olla (coffee seasoned with cinnamon and piloncillo) to wash it all down.

In addition to Day of the Dead culinary classics, attendees will also be treated to live music and a Catrina bride parade on Saturday evening starting at 5:30 p.m., with participants decked out in resplendent embroidered gowns, French hats and painted skull makeup.

Free admission, with snacks available for purchase. For more details, visit Turismo Zapopan‘s social media.

MND writer Dawn Stoner is reporting from Guadalajara.

World.title: Simon, a Category 2 hurricane, churns up the Pacific coast, heading for Puerto Vallarta
World.content:
Listen to this article

Hurricane Simon continues to churn slowly off Mexico’s Pacific coast on Monday, pounding western states with dangerous winds, heavy rain and ​flooding that put coastal communities on alert for possible evacuations.

With its center still whirling parallel to the coast, Simon’s most damaging winds and rain were forecast to persist near the Puerto Vallarta area.

Maximum sustained winds had decreased to near 110 mph (175 km/h) late Sunday and the storm had weakened to a Category 2 hurricane, though it was featuring gusts of up to 135 mph (220 km/h).

As of 6 a.m., the hurricane was located approximately 80 kilometers west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes (just south of Puerto Vallarta), and 120 km southwest of Punta Mita, Nayarit.

Simon is skirting the coast at approximately 3 km/h and is expected to continue northwest through Tuesday before turning northeast and approaching the coast late Wednesday.

The U.S. National Hurricane Center said hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km).

Although some weakening is forecast through Monday, Simon could re-intensify on Tuesday and Wednesday and is expected to remain a hurricane until landfall.

Heavy rains of up to 6 to 8 inches are forecast for parts of Jalisco and Nayarit Monday and Tuesday, while Sinaloa is expected to see similar rainfall on Wednesday and Thursday.

10/11 – Hurricane #Simon continues to parallel the Jalisco coast with max winds of 105 kt. Simon-generated swells will bring life-threatening surf and rip currents to portions of SW and west-central Mexico over the next few days.

More: https://t.co/Wk7xxBlxYC #GOESWest #marinewx https://t.co/sMQI2gz8wI — NHC_TAFB (@NHC_TAFB) October 12, 2026

Sustained winds of 60 to 80 km/h with gusts of 90 to 100 km/h are expected in Jalisco, but should decrease throughout Monday, while Nayarit and Sinaloa can expect to see winds of 30 to 40 km/h with gusts of 50 to 60 km/h.

Additionally, waves of 4 to 5 meters high (up to 16 feet) are evident along the Jalisco coast, with waves from 2.5 to 3.5 meters high (up to 11 feet) on the coasts of Nayarit and Sinaloa.

At the same time, isolated heavy rainfall is forecast for portions of the states of Michoacán and Colima.

President Claudia Sheinbaum on Monday urged residents of affected states to stay informed and follow Civil Protection recommendations as life-threatening flooding and mudslides are a real possibility.

The National Meteorological Service issued a Hurricane Warning area extending from Playa Pérula, Jalisco, to El Roblito, Nayarit — including the Islas Marías — and a Hurricane Watch area extending from El Roblito, Nayarit, to Bahía Tempehuaya, Sinaloa.

With reports from IMER Noticias, The New York Times, Reuters, CNN and CBS News

GUATEMALA · SECURITY

Key Facts — The country Guatemala, in Central America, borders Mexico and sits on a main cocaine route to the United States.

— What happened On Monday, 12 October, High-Risk Court A sentenced Kevin Castellanos to 79 years and 4 months for killing two police officers.

— The US angle Authorities blame the attack on Barrio 18, a street gang the US State Department designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization in September 2025.

— The terrorism count The sentence includes 13 years and 4 months for terrorism, under a 2025 law that classes street gangs as terrorist groups.

— The attack Officers Diana Chávez and Juan Antonio Paredes were killed on 18 January in El Limón, a neighbourhood in Guatemala City’s zone 18.

— Still open A hearing on compensation for the officers’ families is due on Thursday; no appeal has been reported.

A Guatemalan court on Monday, 12 October, sentenced Kevin Castellanos to 79 years and 4 months for killing two police officers. Authorities blame the January attack on Barrio 18, a street gang the United States lists as a Foreign Terrorist Organization.

Of that total, 13 years and 4 months are for terrorism, a charge a 2025 law opened up for gang crimes. The Guatemala City daily La Hora reports that he is the first alleged gang member convicted of terrorism since that reform.

What the Court Decided

High-Risk Court A is one of Guatemala’s special trial courts for organised crime and other dangerous cases. Castellanos followed Monday’s hearing by video link, Prensa Libre reported.

The judges convicted him of murder, illegal carrying of military-grade weapons, illicit association and terrorism. They gave him 50 years for murder, 10 for the weapons and 6 for illicit association.

The terrorism count added 13 years and 4 months, bringing the total to 79 years and 4 months. The court also imposed a fine of US$33,000, payable in its equivalent in quetzales, Guatemala’s currency.

Prosecutors had asked on Friday, 9 October, for 76 years and 6 months, including 10 years for terrorism. The judges went beyond that request on the terrorism count.

Police seized a rifle from Castellanos when they arrested him, and authorities say it was used in the attack. At the 9 October hearing, his defence asked for acquittal and argued that he does not belong to the gang.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The January Attacks on Police

Officers Diana Chávez and Juan Antonio Paredes of the National Civil Police, Guatemala’s national force, died on Sunday, 18 January 2026. Gunmen attacked them in El Limón, a neighbourhood in zone 18 of Guatemala City.

Police came under attack in several places that day. Authorities blamed Barrio 18 and called the attacks revenge for the state retaking three prisons where gang inmates had rioted.

The riots hit Renovación 1 in Escuintla, Fraijanes 2 and the men’s pretrial jail in zone 18, Prensa Libre reported. Rioters held more than 40 prison guards, according to Estrategia y Negocios, a business magazine.

President Bernardo Arévalo, an anti-corruption reformer in office since January 2024, declared a 30-day nationwide state of siege on 18 January. The wave of attacks eventually left 11 police officers dead, Prensa Libre reported, citing the authorities.

The Law That Labels Gangs Terrorists

Guatemala’s Congress approved Decree 11-2025, an anti-gang law, on 21 October 2025 with 145 votes. It declares street gangs, including Barrio 18 and its rival Mara Salvatrucha, transnational criminal and terrorist groups.

Arévalo welcomed it, saying it would give the security forces the tools needed to fight the gangs, Emisoras Unidas reported. The law took effect after its publication in the official gazette on 10 November 2025.

It raises terrorism sentences by one third when a designated group commits the crime, Prensa Libre reported when the law took effect.

According to La Hora, Castellanos is the first person accused of gang membership to be convicted of terrorism since that reform.

Washington’s Terrorist Label on Barrio 18

The US State Department designated Barrio 18 a Foreign Terrorist Organization in a notice published in the Federal Register on 24 September 2025. Under US law, giving material support to such a group is a federal crime.

Guatemala’s neighbours are moving in the same direction. Honduras declared three unnamed criminal groups terrorist on 19 September, under a gang law published in May.

In El Salvador, prosecutors said on 11 October that a court had sentenced 71 members and collaborators of a Barrio 18 cell in one case.

What It Means for You

For American readers, the verdict shows a close US partner using terrorism law against a gang Washington already treats as terrorist.

For travellers and companies, it signals tougher prosecution, not an end to gang violence. Twenty police officers had been killed in Guatemala in 2026 by late July, Emisoras Unidas reported, citing official sources.

The ruling does not mean the gang has been broken. Nor does it mean every gang case will now carry a terrorism charge.

What Is Not Known

The Public Ministry, Guatemala’s prosecution service, had posted no statement on the ruling on its website by Tuesday morning. Whether the defence will appeal has not been reported.

It is not clear what became of the sedition charge, for which prosecutors had sought six months. Prensa Libre notes that some of the January police killings are still under investigation.

A hearing on compensation for the officers’ families, known in Guatemala as reparación digna, is scheduled for Thursday, La Hora reported.

More: Guatemala news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Barrio 18?

Barrio 18 is a street gang active in Guatemala and El Salvador. Guatemalan authorities blame it for the January attacks on police, and Washington designated it a terrorist organization in 2025.

Why did a murder case include a terrorism charge?

Guatemala’s 2025 anti-gang law classes street gangs as terrorist groups and reformed the Penal Code. The court found Castellanos took part in coordinated attacks on police, which added 13 years and 4 months.

What happens next in the case?

A hearing on compensation for the two officers’ families is scheduled for Thursday. No appeal by the defence has been reported.
