PARAGUAY · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — The country Paraguay, a landlocked nation in the heart of South America and the only country on the continent that recognises Taiwan.

— What happened On Monday, 12 October, Paraguay’s Foreign Ministry rejected China’s sanctions on technology minister Gustavo Villate, hours after Beijing announced them.

— Why it matters Beijing’s spokesperson linked the sanctions to claims of Chinese cyberattacks, which Paraguay made jointly with the US Embassy in July.

— The sanctions An asset freeze in China, a ban on dealings with people and organisations there, and no entry to mainland China, Hong Kong or Macao.

— The minister’s reply Villate called the measure foreseeable, compared it to a medal of honour and said joint projects with Taiwan will speed up.

— Still open Whether Beijing adds more names, and whether Paraguay takes any step beyond its statement.

Paraguay rejects China sanctions on one of its ministers, the government said on Monday, 12 October. The Foreign Ministry said the measures against technology minister Gustavo Villate create unnecessary friction with the country.

The China sanctions reach Washington because Beijing tied them to cyberattack accusations that Paraguay made jointly with the US Embassy in July. Paraguay is also one of Taiwan’s last 12 diplomatic allies.

What Paraguay Said

The Foreign Ministry posted its response on X on Monday, ABC Color and La Nación reported. “The Government of Paraguay rejects the sanctions imposed by Popular China on the MITIC minister, Gustavo Villate,” it said.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Paraguay ranks 10th of 14 with 36.0 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (55); weakest: future resources (13). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The ministry added that the measures “generate unnecessary friction with our country.” It said Paraguay “once again ratifies its firm support for the Republic of China (Taiwan),” the official name Taipei uses.

MITIC is Paraguay’s Ministry of Information and Communication Technologies, which oversees the state’s digital networks. Popular China is the name Paraguayan officials use for the People’s Republic, which governs the mainland.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Paraguay Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Beijing Decided

China’s Foreign Ministry imposed the measures on Monday on Villate and on Belize’s foreign minister, Francis Fonseca. Belize, in Central America, is another of Taiwan’s allies.

Both men face a freeze of any assets in China and a ban on dealings with people and organisations there. They are also denied visas and entry to mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao, as reported in China sanctions Paraguay minister over Taiwan.

At a press briefing in Beijing on Monday, spokesperson Mao Ning said “individual politicians” in Paraguay and Belize had interfered in China’s internal affairs. She accused them of spreading “false information” about “Chinese cyberattacks” and of smearing China, the ministry’s transcript shows.

That charge goes back to 10 July, when Paraguay’s technology ministry and the US Embassy jointly blamed China-linked hackers for intrusions into state networks. A joint review had found “multiple threat actors related to the Chinese government,” the Asunción daily Hoy reported then.

Asked whether this was the first such step against ministers of Taiwan’s allies, Mao Ning did not answer directly. She said China will take “all necessary punitive measures” against people who stubbornly back Taiwan independence.

She also urged Taiwan’s “few remaining so-called diplomatic allies” not to let separatist forces keep manipulating and using them.

How Villate Answered

Villate called the China sanctions foreseeable and compared them to “a medal of honour,” ABC Color and La Nación reported. He linked them to Paraguay’s technology work with Taiwan, including a binational data center planned in Chaco’i, across the river from Asunción.

“No outside sanction conditions our decisions,” Villate wrote on X, according to Última Hora. “Together with Taiwan, we are going to speed up every joint project.”

He named Yguazú Digital, a planned artificial intelligence hub, and a technology park among the projects. He also cited Foxconn, the Taiwanese electronics giant that assembles Apple’s iPhones, which Peña has invited to invest in Paraguay.

Foxconn could also join the Yguazú hub, according to Villate. He said the data center plan includes security standards to stop interference by foreign powers.

Taiwan Steps In

Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry called the China sanctions “absolutely absurd” and an open interference in independent nations’ sovereignty, Última Hora reported. It said China’s coercion only strengthens its allies’ resolve to keep backing Taiwan.

Taiwan’s embassy in Asunción relayed the statement, ABC Color reported. It accused Beijing of using political intimidation to subdue sovereign nations.

Paraguay’s conservative president, Santiago Peña, leads the Colorado Party, which has governed Paraguay for most of the past seven decades. He has made the Taiwan alliance a centrepiece of his foreign policy.

Villate said Peña has instructed him to speed up cooperation with Taiwan rather than slow it down.

What It Means for You

For American readers, the China sanctions show Beijing raising pressure on the few countries that still recognise Taiwan, an issue Washington follows closely. China’s complaint about “Chinese cyberattacks” also ties the dispute directly to Paraguay’s cybersecurity work with the US Embassy.

For investors, Paraguay’s answer points the other way: more Taiwanese technology investment, not less. Ordinary travellers and Paraguayan exports are not affected, because the measures target one minister personally.

What Is Not Known

ABC Color’s 730 AM radio reported that Villate ruled out owning any assets in China, so the freeze may have little practical effect. Beijing has not said whether more Paraguayan officials could face similar measures.

Paraguay’s statement announced no counter-measures to the China sanctions. It is also unclear when the Chaco’i data center and the Yguazú Digital hub will move from plans to construction.

More: Paraguay news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did China sanction a Paraguayan minister?

China’s Foreign Ministry says Gustavo Villate stubbornly backed Paraguay’s ties with Taiwan and spread “false information” about Chinese cyberattacks. Beijing claims Taiwan as its own territory.

What do the sanctions do?

The China sanctions freeze any assets Villate has in China and bar people and organisations there from dealing with him. They also bar him from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao.

How did Paraguay respond?

The Foreign Ministry rejected the sanctions on 12 October, said they create unnecessary friction and restated its firm support for Taiwan.

Will Paraguay switch recognition to Beijing?

Nothing points that way. President Santiago Peña backs the Taiwan alliance, and Villate said joint projects with Taipei will now speed up.

World.content:

HONDURAS · HEALTH

Key Facts — The country Honduras, a Central American country tied to the United States by the CAFTA-DR free-trade agreement since 2006.

— What happened On Monday, 12 October, Armando Urtecho, executive director of the business council Cohep, called the leaders of the doctors’ association a “cartel.”

— What he wants Urtecho asked the Labor Ministry, led by Fernando Puerto, to send inspectors and draw up formal records against doctors who keep care suspended.

— Why doctors protest Honduras doctors, protesting since 7 September, want overdue pay, dismissed colleagues reinstated, pay adjustments, contracts, more staff and a bigger health budget.

— The government’s figure Deputy health minister José Miguel Castillo says 95% of the doctors in the assemblies have now received their overdue salaries.

— What it means for you Emergency rooms stay open, but outpatient clinics in public hospitals run by the Health Secretariat remain disrupted.

— The doctors’ reply Samuel Santos, president of the doctors’ association, called the remarks regrettable, and the assemblies continue.

Honduras doctors have kept outpatient clinics in public hospitals shut for more than five weeks in a protest over unpaid salaries. On Monday, 12 October, a top executive of the country’s business council called their leadership a “cartel” and demanded sanctions.

Armando Urtecho is executive director of Cohep, the Honduran Private Enterprise Council, which groups the country’s business chambers. For American visitors, and for US families with relatives in Honduras, the standoff means long waits for routine care, although emergency rooms remain open.

What Urtecho Said on Monday

The CMH, or Colegio Médico de Honduras, is the professional college that represents Honduras doctors. Its president, Samuel Santos, has spoken for the protesting doctors since the assemblies began on Monday, 7 September, La Tribuna reported.

Speaking to reporters in Tegucigalpa on Monday, Urtecho said: “We believe the cartel that runs the Colegio Médico should search its conscience.” He added that the doctors hurt “the ordinary citizen,” not the government or business, La Prensa reported.

He also told the Labor Secretary to “get moving and enforce the law,” according to El Heraldo and its sister paper La Prensa. The daily El Mundo reported that the request was aimed at Labor Minister Fernando Puerto.

Urtecho asked the ministry to draw up formal infraction records, known as actas, against those “paralyzing the medical service,” El Mundo reported. La Tribuna added that he wants labor inspectors sent to public hospital wards at once.

His argument rests on the Labor Code, which he says treats health care as an essential service. Urtecho first raised the demand on Sunday, 4 October, asking on a TV debate program why doctors had not been sanctioned, TuNota reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Honduras Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Honduras Doctors Are Holding Assemblies

Honduras doctors call their protest asambleas informativas, or informational assemblies, rather than a strike. Outpatient clinics close while emergency rooms stay open, La Tribuna reported.

The action began over salaries left unpaid for months, while three state agencies argued over who should process the payments. The CMH has said the assemblies will continue until the authorities offer a concrete solution.

The demands now go further, El Heraldo and TuNota reported. They include reinstating dismissed doctors, pay adjustments, contracts, more staff, extra “prophylactic” leave and a larger health budget.

The CMH has called a new nationwide extraordinary assembly, held from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., El Heraldo and La Prensa reported on Monday. Our earlier report explains how the 95% payment figure is counted.

What the Government Says

The row also exposes a gap at the top, because Honduras has no separate health minister. President Nasry Asfura, a conservative, runs the health ministry himself, TuNota and La Tribuna reported.

Urtecho said no health minister is needed to apply labor rules, according to El Mundo. In his view, it falls to Asfura to make the public administration work.

Deputy health minister José Miguel Castillo says 95% of the doctors in the assemblies have received their overdue salaries. The other 5% still have unresolved cases, he said, as reported by El Heraldo and La Prensa.

The Honduran Social Security Institute (IHSS), the state health insurer, reached a separate deal with its own doctors. Its clinics were due to resume consultations on 12 October, La Tribuna reported on 6 October.

How the Doctors Answered

Santos hit back the same afternoon. “Those kinds of statements from Cohep are regrettable,” he said, as reported by La Tribuna.

He described Urtecho as an employee with a right to his views, and added: “Those of us who reach old age often talk that way.”

Santos accused some health officials and “busybodies” from other organizations of using the dispute to raise their profile. The CMH said talks have moved to the presidency and that the assemblies end once back pay is settled, La Tribuna reported.

What It Means for You

For US visitors and residents, the Honduras doctors’ protest has not closed emergency rooms in public hospitals. Outpatient clinics run by the Health Secretariat are the services affected.

The US State Department says staff, facilities and supplies in Honduras often do not meet US medical standards. It warns that Medicare does not apply overseas and that most providers abroad accept only cash.

Its travel advisory rates Honduras at Level 3, “Reconsider Travel,” because of crime.

Carlos Hernández, who leads the Association for a More Just Society (ASJ), a Honduran anti-corruption group, called the situation of waiting patients “inhumane.” He asked the government to publish which doctors have already been paid, El Mundo reported on Monday.

For investors, the dispute sets the business lobby against a key profession in a close US trade partner. US goods trade with Honduras reached an estimated US$12.5 billion in 2025, the Office of the US Trade Representative says.

That trade runs under CAFTA-DR, the free-trade pact between the United States, five Central American countries and the Dominican Republic. It took effect for Honduras on 1 April 2006.

What Is Not Known

The Labor Secretariat has not said whether it will act on Urtecho’s request, or what penalties the Labor Code would allow.

It is also unclear when the remaining Honduras doctors will be paid in full, the condition the CMH has set for ending the assemblies.

More: Honduras news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Cohep?

Cohep, the Consejo Hondureño de la Empresa Privada, is the umbrella council of Honduras’ business chambers. Armando Urtecho is its executive director.

What is the CMH?

The Colegio Médico de Honduras is the professional college that represents the country’s doctors. Its president is Samuel Santos.

Why are doctors in Honduras protesting?

Honduras doctors want overdue salaries paid, dismissed colleagues reinstated, pay adjustments, contracts, more staff and a larger health budget.

How did the doctors respond to the cartel remark?

CMH president Samuel Santos called the remarks regrettable, La Tribuna reported. The college has kept its assemblies going and says talks have moved to the presidency.

Are public hospitals in Honduras open?

Emergency rooms remain open. Outpatient clinics are disrupted because Honduras doctors employed by the Health Secretariat are in assemblies. Social security clinics were due to reopen on 12 October.

CHILE · TRANSPORT

Key Facts — The country Chile, where the capital Santiago is crossed by privately run toll highways that charge drivers electronically.

— What happened On Monday, 12 October, President José Antonio Kast announced lower electronic (TAG) tolls on Autopista Central, Santiago’s main north-south highway.

— The discount 25% in peak and congested hours and 10% at off-peak times, Cooperativa, Meganoticias and Emol reported.

— From when 1 January 2027, Kast said, once the agreement clears an administrative review in the coming weeks.

— Who qualifies Drivers whose TAG account is paid up within the first 60 days after the cut takes effect.

— What the operator gets A concession about 20 months longer, according to minister Louis de Grange as quoted by Cooperativa, and to La Tercera and Emol.

— Who owns the road VíasChile, 80% owned by Spain’s Abertis and 20% by the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, per its 2024 annual report.

Chile plans to cut the Autopista Central toll by up to 25% from 1 January 2027, President José Antonio Kast said on Monday. The road carries the Pan-American Highway through Santiago, and its tolls are charged through TAG, a small windscreen device, including to foreigners in rental cars.

In return, operator VíasChile gets a concession about 20 months longer, said Louis de Grange, minister of Public Works and Transport, as quoted by Cooperativa. Only drivers with paid-up accounts will get the discount, Kast said, according to Cooperativa and Meganoticias.

How the Autopista Central Toll Cut Works

Kast said the Autopista Central toll discount will be 25% at peak and congested hours and 10% at off-peak times. Both Cooperativa and Meganoticias reported the same rates and the 1 January 2027 start.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Like Santiago’s other urban highways, Autopista Central charges more at rush hour, with a top rate for the most congested periods. The bigger cut therefore goes to commuters who drive at the busiest times.

There is one condition. Drivers must have their Autopista Central TAG account paid up within the first 60 days after the measure takes effect, Kast said.

“Whoever does things properly is rewarded,” he said, in remarks quoted by both outlets. The deal is not yet in force: it faces an administrative review in the coming weeks, Chilevisión and Emol reported.

A monthly bill of 100,000 pesos (about US$102), all from peak-hour trips, would fall to 75,000 pesos (about US$77), Chilevisión and La Tercera reported. Those conversions use about 977 pesos to the US dollar on 13 October 2026.

Who Owns Autopista Central

Autopista Central is run by VíasChile, the Chilean arm of Spanish toll operator Abertis. Cooperativa reported that VíasChile reached the agreement with Louis de Grange, the minister for both Public Works and Transport.

According to VíasChile’s 2024 annual report, Abertis owns 80% of the group and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, the emirate’s state wealth fund, owns 20%. Abertis itself is split equally between Spain’s ACS and Italy’s Mundys.

The same report says VíasChile bought the other half of Autopista Central from Canadian investor AIMCo, giving it control of the road.

Abertis has negotiated with Chilean governments over Santiago’s roads before, including a major investment deal agreed in 2021.

What VíasChile Gets in Return

De Grange said the Autopista Central toll cut comes “in exchange for an extension of the concession term of close to 20 months.” Cooperativa quoted him, and La Tercera and Emol also reported a 20-month extension.

The details will depend on when the Contraloría, Chile’s public-spending watchdog, approves the change, De Grange added. The Contraloría must sign off on every amended concession contract before it applies.

Opposition deputies said the deal mainly helps the company. They include Ignacio Achurra of the left-wing Frente Amplio, the party of former President Gabriel Boric, and Nelson Venegas of the centre-left Socialist Party.

Achurra argued that longer contracts mean families still pay in the long run and block a cheaper re-tender, Cooperativa and Emol reported. Venegas said the agreement “tends to favour mainly the concessionaires.”

Why Kast Wants Lower Tolls

Kast, a conservative who founded Chile’s Republican Party, took office in March. Louis de Grange runs both the Public Works and the Transport ministries, as our guide to Chile’s key players explains.

In September De Grange said the government was negotiating with four Santiago highways, T13 and Pauta reported. They were Autopista Central, Costanera Norte, Vespucio Sur and Vespucio Norte.

De Grange said any cut had to be “something users notice in their pockets.” He added that older concessions are easier to renegotiate, because the state can offer them longer contracts in return for lower tolls.

On Monday Kast said De Grange is talking to other urban highways about similar deals. De Grange said they will be announced as they close, because concession terms and toll levels differ from road to road.

What It Means for You

Rush-hour commuters with paid-up accounts should see their Autopista Central toll fall by a quarter from January, if the deal is approved. Off-peak trips will be 10% cheaper.

Visitors who rent a car in Santiago also pay the Autopista Central toll whenever they use the road. Whether rental firms will pass the discount on has not been announced.

For investors, the cut was agreed with the operator rather than imposed, and the operator gets extra contract time in exchange. De Grange is negotiating similar deals with other Santiago highways, which matters to foreign funds holding Chilean road concessions.

What Is Not Known

Neither Kast nor De Grange gave the concession’s new end date. Nor did they say how much Autopista Central toll revenue VíasChile gives up in exchange.

The exact peak and off-peak hours and the new per-kilometre rates in pesos were not given. No date was set for sending the amended contract to the Contraloría.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a TAG in Chile?

A TAG is a small electronic device on a car’s windscreen that pays tolls automatically. Santiago’s urban highways have no toll booths, so the TAG account is billed each time a car passes under a gantry.

When does the Autopista Central discount start?

Kast said it will apply from 1 January 2027. The agreement first faces an administrative review in the coming weeks and must be approved.

Who gets the discount?

Drivers whose Autopista Central toll account is paid up within the first 60 days after the cut takes effect. The rate is 25% at peak and congested hours and 10% off-peak.

What does the operator get in return?

A concession about 20 months longer, minister Louis de Grange said, as quoted by Cooperativa. La Tercera and Emol reported the same figure.

Who owns Autopista Central?

VíasChile controls the road. Its 2024 annual report shows the group is 80% held by Spain’s Abertis and 20% by the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority.

PERU · ENVIRONMENT

Key Facts — The country Peru, on South America’s Pacific coast, holds the Cordillera Blanca, which UNESCO calls the world’s highest tropical mountain range.

— What happened In a statement on Monday 12 October, Environment Minister Vladimiro Huaroc urged joint action on the flood risk at Laguna Parón, a glacial lake.

— The number State glacier scientists estimate a flood from the lake could affect more than 22,000 people in the town of Caraz.

— The place Laguna Parón sits at 4,185 metres (13,730 feet) in Huascarán National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985.

— Why now The ministry wants preventive steps in place before Peru’s Andean rainy season begins.

— Still open The ministry announced no evacuation, emergency decree or visitor closure on Monday.

Peru’s environment ministry warned on Monday 12 October that a glacial lake flood from Laguna Parón could affect over 22,000 people in Caraz. The lake is a visitor attraction in Huascarán National Park, a UNESCO-listed climbing and trekking area in the Áncash region.

The ministry announced no evacuation or closure. Environment Minister Vladimiro Huaroc asked officials at every level of government to act early, before the rainy season.

What the Minister Said in Áncash

Huaroc led a working meeting at the regional emergency operations centre in Áncash, the Ministry of the Environment (Minam) said on Monday. Peru’s civil defence agency, its water authority and its glacier institute were among those at the table.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He asked the agencies to decide who operates and maintains the lake’s water-control works. He also called for closer monitoring and better coordination between them, the ministry said.

Huaroc, a former governor of the Junín region, joined the cabinet of conservative President Keiko Fujimori in July, Actualidad Ambiental reported.

“The lessons of the past remind us of the importance of anticipating risks and acting in time to protect the population,” Huaroc said.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Laguna Parón Worries Scientists

INAIGEM, Peru’s state institute for research on glaciers and mountain ecosystems, assessed the danger. Its evaluations put more than 22,000 Caraz residents at risk from a possible glacial lake flood, Minam said.

In Spanish such a flood is called an aluvión, a fast surge of water, mud and rock. The ministry said a Parón flood could hit with an impact similar to the 1970 aluvión that buried the town of Yungay.

An INAIGEM study modelled an extreme case, the environmental news site Actualidad Ambiental reported in May 2021. In it, a 136,000-cubic-metre avalanche from the Hatunraju glacier hits the lake and sets off a surge of water and debris.

That would release more than 18 million cubic metres of water, roughly 7,200 Olympic swimming pools, toward Caraz. The study put possible losses above 300 million soles (about US$87 million at 3.43 soles to the US dollar on 13 October 2026).

A glacial lake flood is a growing worry across the Andes as glaciers shrink. In August, Peruvian authorities flagged 152 glacial lakes at high risk of bursting.

A Lake With a History of Alarms

Parón is the largest lake in the Cordillera Blanca and sits at 4,185 metres above sea level, the business daily Gestión reported.

In June 2019, Peru declared an emergency at the lake after its level passed safe limits, the state news agency Andina reported. The decree, signed by then-President Martín Vizcarra, also named risks to the Cañón del Pato hydroelectric plant.

In July 2023, an avalanche and falling rock hit the lake. Peru’s national emergency centre and INAIGEM then rated the glacial lake flood danger “very high”, Gestión reported.

Park authorities and INAIGEM restricted visitor access to the lake that month, according to Gestión and La República. An INAIGEM report found nearly 80% of homes in the lower Llullán-Parón valley highly vulnerable, La República reported.

What It Means for You

Minam announced no evacuation, travel ban or new closure for Laguna Parón on Monday. Visitors planning a trip should still watch for glacial lake flood warnings as the rainy season nears.

Huascarán National Park has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1985. Its namesake peak rises to 6,768 metres (22,205 feet), UNESCO says.

The US State Department rates Peru at Level 2, “Exercise Increased Caution,” and its advisory does not single out Áncash. Before a trip to the lake, check with Sernanp, Peru’s national parks service, because access was restricted at short notice in 2023.

Peru is also holding a nationwide disaster drill on the evening of Tuesday 13 October.

What Is Not Known

Minam did not say which agency will take charge of the lake’s water-control works, or when.

The ministry published no current lake level and did not say how likely a glacial lake flood is in a given year. Minam did not mention any change to visitor access.

Minam said agreements with local communities and water users are needed to manage the lake and avoid conflict. It did not name those groups or set a date for talks.

More: Peru news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Laguna Parón?

It is a glacial lake at 4,185 metres in Huascarán National Park, in Peru’s Áncash region. It is the largest lake in the Cordillera Blanca and a visitor attraction.

How many people could a glacial lake flood from Parón affect?

More than 22,000 people in Caraz, according to INAIGEM evaluations cited by Peru’s environment ministry on 12 October 2026. It is a risk scenario, not a forecast.

Is Laguna Parón closed to visitors?

The ministry announced no closure on 12 October 2026. Park authorities restricted access to the lake at short notice in July 2023, so check with Sernanp before you go.

What happened in Yungay in 1970?

In 1970 an earthquake and an aluvión, a flood of mud and rock, struck Áncash, and the flood buried the town of Yungay. Peru’s environment ministry said a Parón flood could have a similar impact.

EL SALVADOR · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country El Salvador, the smallest country in Central America, has used the US dollar since 2001 and relies on imported fuel.

— What happened The state fuel agency kept reference pump prices unchanged from Tuesday, 13 October, to Monday, 26 October.

— The prices Central zone: super (premium) US$5.13 a gallon, regular US$4.80, diesel US$4.86; gasoline is one cent more in the west and east.

— The streak It is the second two-week period without a change, after a US$0.17 rise on 15 September kept super above US$5.

— The US angle The agency cites Hurricane Isaías shutting US oil platforms and refineries, and lower US crude and diesel stocks.

— Against the US Salvadoran regular costs about 45 cents more than the US average of US$4.354 on 5 October, while diesel is about US$1.34 cheaper.

El Salvador fuel prices will not move from Tuesday, 13 October, to Monday, 26 October, with regular at US$4.80 a gallon in the central zone. The state fuel agency names closed US refineries and thin US fuel stocks among the risks it watches.

The Dirección General de Energía, Hidrocarburos y Minas (DGEHM), which publishes reference fuel prices every two weeks, announced them on Monday, 12 October. It is the second period in a row without a change, Diario El Mundo reported.

What Salvadoran Drivers Pay Until 26 October

In the central zone, a gallon of super, the premium grade, costs US$5.13, regular US$4.80 and diesel US$4.86. Diario El Mundo and El Diario de Hoy, two leading Salvadoran papers, both reported the DGEHM figures.

In the western and eastern zones, super and regular cost one cent more, at US$5.14 and US$4.81. Diesel stays at US$4.86 everywhere.

Both papers report a change of zero cents for all three fuels in every zone. The DGEHM posted the new list on X, the social network.

Super has stayed above US$5 since prices rose by US$0.17 on 15 September, Diario El Mundo reported. El Salvador fuel prices have risen repeatedly this year, as The Rio Times reported in August.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on El Salvador Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why US Refineries Matter to El Salvador

The DGEHM listed three outside risks for oil prices, both newspapers reported. The first is a new attack on Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline.

The other two are in the United States. One is Hurricane Isaías, which forced US oil platforms and refineries to close, the agency said.

The other is a fall in US crude and diesel stocks, which the DGEHM sourced to an early-October International Energy Agency (IEA) report. The IEA is a Paris-based body that tracks energy markets for member governments.

Because El Salvador has used the US dollar since 2001, no local exchange rate stands between world oil prices and the pump. El Salvador fuel prices are set in dollars.

Both outlets quote the DGEHM as crediting coordination between the government and oil companies for the stable prices. Neither mentions a subsidy or what the arrangement costs.

How Prices Compare With the United States

The Energy Information Administration (EIA), the statistics arm of the US Department of Energy, put US regular at US$4.354 a gallon on 5 October. Salvadoran regular is about 45 cents more expensive than that.

Diesel runs the other way. The EIA put US diesel at US$6.199 a gallon, about US$1.34 more than the US$4.86 Salvadoran drivers pay.

What It Means for You

For US visitors renting a car, El Salvador fuel prices are predictable for the next two weeks. A 12-gallon tank of regular costs about US$57.60 in the central zone.

For Salvadorans in the United States who send money home, one family cost will not rise for now. Diesel, used by buses and freight trucks, is also unchanged.

For firms trucking goods to Salvadoran ports, diesel at US$4.86 keeps a key cost flat until 26 October.

What Is Not Known

The DGEHM has not said what prices will apply from Tuesday, 27 October, when the next two-week period begins. It is also unclear how the coordination with oil companies works, or whether it uses public money.

Neither paper reports how long the government intends to keep El Salvador fuel prices steady. Neither says how much US refining capacity Hurricane Isaías shut, or for how long.

More: El Salvador news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are El Salvador fuel prices until 26 October?

In the central zone, a gallon of super costs US$5.13, regular US$4.80 and diesel US$4.86. In the western and eastern zones, super and regular cost one cent more, while diesel is the same.

Why did El Salvador keep fuel prices unchanged?

The DGEHM, the state fuel agency, points to risks abroad, including Hurricane Isaías closing US refineries and lower US fuel stocks. Local papers say coordination between the government and oil companies helped keep prices stable.

Is fuel cheaper in El Salvador than in the United States?

Regular gasoline is about 45 cents a gallon more expensive than the US average of US$4.354 reported for 5 October. Diesel is about US$1.34 a gallon cheaper than the US average of US$6.199.

COSTA RICA · LABOR

Key Facts — The country A Central American democracy of about five million people, where medical devices make up close to half of goods exports.

— What happened Sixteen opposition deputies filed a constitutional consultation on the 4×3 workweek bill (file 24.290) on Monday, 12 October.

— The effect The final vote, set for Tuesday, 13 October, is frozen until the constitutional court answers.

— The bill The 4×3 workweek allows voluntary schedules of four 12-hour day shifts and three days off, or three night shifts and four off.

— The US angle The Costa Rican-American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham), which speaks for US-linked business, has urged lawmakers to pass it.

— Still open The court has not said when it will rule. El Observador, a Costa Rican outlet, estimates about two months.

The Costa Rica 4×3 workweek reform stalled on Monday, 12 October, when 16 opposition deputies asked the country’s constitutional court to review it. Their request froze the final vote, which had been set for Tuesday, 13 October.

The bill would let some factories and service centres run four 12-hour shifts followed by three days off. It matters to US investors because it targets medical-device plants, and AmCham, the US-linked business chamber, has urged its approval.

What the Costa Rica 4X3 Workweek Bill Would Change

The 4×3 workweek bill is file 24.290 in the Legislative Assembly, Costa Rica’s single-chamber congress. It creates “exceptional” working hours for sectors that run around the clock.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 with 36.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (75); weakest: military means (0). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Day workers could work four 12-hour shifts and then rest for three days. Night workers would work three shifts and rest for four, according to CRHoy, a Costa Rican news site.

It covers advanced manufacturing, the making of medical implements, support services and corporate services operating across time zones. The current Congress, seated on 1 May, amended the text to exclude the public sector.

Workers would earn a 17% premium on day or mixed shifts and 25.5% at night. They would also get 90 minutes a day for meals and rest, counted as paid working time.

The switch must be voluntary and in writing, and employers may not punish staff who refuse. The Assembly passed the bill in a first vote of 31 to 19 on Thursday, 8 October.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Costa Rica Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Filed the Challenge and Why

The request went to the Sala IV, the constitutional chamber of Costa Rica’s Supreme Court. At least 10 deputies must sign such a consultation, and it pauses the 4×3 workweek bill until the judges answer.

Seven signers belong to the Broad Front (FA), the left-wing party led in Congress by José María Villalta. Eight come from National Liberation (PLN), the centrist former ruling party.

The 16th is Claudia Dobles of the Citizen Agenda Coalition (CAC), who holds her party’s only seat. El Observador reported that the Broad Front drafted the filing and lodged it at 12:40 p.m. on Monday.

The court told Assembly president Yara Jiménez that the request is at the admissibility stage, El Observador reported. Monumental, a San José radio station, said the court confirmed receiving it.

On procedure, the filing argues that a pause in the fast-track process, ordered by the previous Congress until 30 April, broke the Assembly’s rules. On substance, it says 12-hour days clash with an International Labour Organization (ILO) convention on maximum daily hours.

Opponents also object that the governing party removed a clause letting workers vote on whether their company adopts the scheme. Broad Front deputy floor leader María Eugenia Román has said her party “will not allow labour guarantees to be reduced”.

Who Backs the Reform

In line with President Laura Fernández’s administration, the governing party says the bill gives investors legal certainty, Teletica, a national TV network, reported. It argues the reform will bring investment and jobs.

Her Sovereign People’s Party (Pueblo Soberano, PPSO) holds a majority and supplied 30 of the 31 votes in the first round. The other came from Abril Gordienko of the centre-right Social Christian Unity Party (PUSC).

PPSO deputy floor leader Juan Manuel Quesada had already called a court filing an “obstructionist” tactic. AmCham’s president said the first vote “marks a decisive advance” toward modernising labour rules.

Uccaep, the umbrella group of Costa Rica’s private business chambers, also wants the bill passed. Its president, Maritza Hernández, said in September that the country “needs to close this process” with a balanced law.

What It Means for You

For US investors, the freeze delays a rule change long sought by export plants in Costa Rica’s free-trade zones. More than 600 companies there produced 67% of the country’s goods exports in the first half of 2026, La Nación reported.

Medical-device makers alone exported about US$5.4 billion in that half-year, with the United States as the main buyer. The US group Boston Scientific, the leading producer, employed about 10,000 people in three plants in July, La Nación said.

Until the court answers and the Assembly holds its final vote, the 4×3 workweek is not law in Costa Rica. Companies planning round-the-clock schedules must keep working under the current Labour Code.

For workers, the trade-off stays the same: longer weekends in exchange for much longer days. Any switch would still need each employee’s written consent.

What Is Not Known

As of Monday, the court said the request was at the admissibility stage, and it has not set a date for its answer. El Observador estimated about two months, which would make a final vote in 2026 unlikely.

La Nación, a leading daily, said the filing freezes the bill for at least a month. The Sala IV first decides whether to admit the request, then rules on form and substance.

It is not known whether the judges will find any of the defects the opposition alleges. The bill can return to the floor for its final vote only after the court has answered.

More: Costa Rica news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Costa Rica 4×3 workweek?

It is a bill that would let some export and service firms schedule four 12-hour day shifts followed by three days off. Night workers would do three shifts and rest four days, and each switch needs the worker’s written consent.

Why was the final vote frozen?

Sixteen opposition deputies filed a constitutional consultation with the Sala IV on 12 October. The 4×3 workweek bill cannot go to its final vote until the court answers.

When will the court decide?

The court has not said. El Observador estimated about two months, which could push the final vote into 2027.

Are 12-hour 4×3 shifts legal in Costa Rica now?

No. The bill passed only its first vote on 8 October and still needs a second and final vote, then the president’s signature.

PERU · MINING

Key Facts — The country Peru, on South America’s Pacific coast, is a major metals exporter with old mining towns high in the Andes.

— What happened On Monday 12 October, AMSAC, Peru’s state clean-up company for old mines, awarded the Quiulacocha mine waste site to Cerro de Pasco Resources.

— The US angle A US government lender agreed in March to fund up to US$5 million and is weighing a loan of up to US$300 million.

— Critical minerals The project targets silver and base metals plus gallium and indium; Washington lists silver, gallium and indium as critical minerals.

— The numbers AMSAC expects more than 500 million soles (about US$146 million) in contractual payments over an estimated 21 years of operation.

— Still open The final contracts with AMSAC are not signed yet; the company expects them in the coming days.

Peru has picked a US-backed miner to clean up and reprocess a decades-old pile of mine waste. On Monday 12 October, state company AMSAC awarded the Quiulacocha tailings in Pasco, high in the Andes, to Cerro de Pasco Resources.

The deal matters in Washington because the project also targets gallium and indium, metals used in chips and defence systems. A US government lender has already agreed to fund up to US$5 million and is weighing a loan of up to US$300 million.

What Peru Decided on 12 October

AMSAC, short for Activos Mineros, is the state company that cleans up mining sites left behind by former owners. Its sale committee awarded Public Auction No. 001-2026-AMSAC to Cerro de Pasco Resources del Perú, AMSAC announced and the company confirmed.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The award covers the Quiulacocha tailings, the finely ground rock left after metals are taken out of ore, plus the surface rights. The winner may reprocess this mine waste to recover the metals still inside it.

The company calls the site one of Peru’s largest legacy mining liabilities. The award still depends on definitive agreements with AMSAC, which the company expects to sign in the coming days.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Washington Is Watching

The parent, Cerro de Pasco Resources Inc., is a Canadian mining company listed in Canada and Lima. Americans can buy its shares on OTCQX, a US over-the-counter market, under the ticker CDPMF.

In March, the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC), Washington’s development lender, agreed to fund up to US$5 million of early work. That covers drilling and a feasibility study, with the company matching each dollar, its 2 March statement said.

The DFC is also weighing a construction loan of up to US$300 million. The company stressed that this loan is not assured.

The project targets silver and base metals together with gallium and indium. The company calls the last two essential to advanced semiconductors, energy systems and defence.

Silver, gallium and indium are all on the US government’s final 2025 list of 60 critical minerals, the US Geological Survey said. The survey is the Interior Department’s science agency.

A Polluted Legacy Older Than 60 Years

AMSAC says the Quiulacocha area has suffered more than six decades of pollution, in its 12 October statement. The Peruvian mining news sites ProActivo and Energiminas also reported the award and its figures.

A state-funded clean-up would cost about 550 million soles (about US$160 million, at 3.43 soles per US dollar on 13 October), AMSAC says. Under the new model, private investment helps pay for that work, and the investor carries the risks its contract assigns.

AMSAC expects more than 500 million soles (about US$146 million) in contractual payments over an estimated 21 years of operation, plus any taxes. A community trust fund of about 20 million soles (about US$5.8 million) is also planned.

AMSAC puts the combined projected benefits and public savings at more than 1 billion soles (about US$291 million). “Our main goal is for the benefits of this transformation to reach the people of Quiulacocha and Cerro de Pasco,” said AMSAC chief Dante Aguilar.

The company already owns El Metalurgista, a concession in central Peru with silver-rich tailings from more than a century of mining. With Quiulacocha, it expects to hold all the rights its reprocessing project needs.

What It Means for You

For US investors, the award is a step forward for a development-stage company whose shares trade in the United States. It is not yet a signed contract, and there is no official resource estimate for the site.

For Peru, it tests a new idea: private miners clean up state-held mine waste in exchange for the metals inside. For background, see how Peru’s copper mining works.

What Is Not Known

Neither the company nor AMSAC has published the tonnage of waste, the price paid or the number of rival bids.

The company has no mineral resource yet under NI 43-101, Canada’s rule for reporting mining resources. It warns that the final agreements may slip and that the award could be challenged.

The DFC loan has not been approved. The winner must also obtain permits, environmental plans and guarantees, AMSAC said when it launched the auction on 2 July.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Quiulacocha tailings site?

It is a deposit of mine waste in the Pasco region of Peru’s central Andes. AMSAC, the state clean-up company, says the area has suffered more than six decades of pollution.

Who won the Quiulacocha auction?

Cerro de Pasco Resources del Perú, the Peruvian unit of a Canadian-listed company. The parent trades in the US under the ticker CDPMF.

Is the US government involved?

Yes. The DFC, a US government lender, agreed in March to fund up to US$5 million. It is also weighing a loan of up to US$300 million.

World.title: United States condemns China’s sanctions against Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca
World.content:
United States condemns China’s sanctions against Belize Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The United States has condemned China’s decision to impose sanctions against Belize’s Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca and a senior Paraguayan official, accusing Beijing of attempting to intimidate countries for exercising their sovereign right to maintain diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

In a statement reported by Reuters on Monday evening, U.S. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the Trump administration strongly opposes China’s actions against countries in the Western Hemisphere.

“The Trump Administration opposes coercion and aggression by China against countries in our hemisphere for exercising their sovereign rights,” Pigott stated.

Pigott also referenced previous remarks by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who warned that Washington would not allow foreign adversaries to use the Western Hemisphere to threaten American security or undermine its international partnerships.

The State Department spokesperson reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to supporting its friends and partners, including Taiwan, in advancing shared prosperity, security and democratic values.

The American response follows China’s announcement on Monday of sanctions against Fonseca and Paraguay’s Minister of Information and Communication Technologies, Gustavo Villate. The measures include travel restrictions, the freezing of any assets they may hold in China and prohibitions against Chinese entities conducting business with them.

Beijing accused the two officials of undermining its sovereignty through their continued support for Taiwan, which China claims as part of its territory.

The Government of Belize has firmly rejected the sanctions, declaring that they will neither alter the country’s foreign policy nor weaken its longstanding diplomatic relationship with Taiwan. Taiwan has also condemned the measures as political intimidation and interference in the sovereignty of independent nations

Belize and Paraguay are among just 12 countries worldwide that maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

Washington’s intervention adds a new dimension to the dispute, placing the United States publicly alongside Belize, Paraguay and Taiwan in opposing Beijing’s sanctions. The U.S. statement did not announce any retaliatory measures against China.

World.title: At just 14, Dangriga student Quesneay Cayetano launches his own clothing brand, MOTION BZ
World.content:
At just 14, Dangriga student Quesneay Cayetano launches his own clothing brand, MOTION BZ

By Breaking Belize News Staff: At just 14 years old, Dangriga resident Quesneay Cayetano is already making moves in the business world, launching his own graphic T-shirt brand, MOTION BZ, with hopes of turning his creativity into a successful clothing business.

Cayetano, a second-form student at Ecumenical High School, started his venture just one month ago. Despite his young age, he is already earning recognition for his neat work, attention to detail, and determination to build a brand of his own.

His clothing line features colourful graphic T-shirts with palm tree designs, available in several colour combinations for BZ$30 each. The brand carries the motto “MOVE DIFFERENT,” reflecting the young entrepreneur’s ambition to stand out and pursue his dreams.

Balancing his schoolwork with his growing business, Cayetano hopes to establish MOTION BZ as a recognizable clothing brand, starting in his hometown of Dangriga.

Those interested in supporting the young entrepreneur or purchasing one of his shirts can contact 621-0715.

For Cayetano, the journey is only beginning, but he is already demonstrating that age does not have to be a barrier to entrepreneurship.

World.title: Murder case against Frederick Wagner delayed again as preliminary inquiry awaits; accused of setting 61-year-old girlfriend on fire
World.content:
Murder case against Frederick Wagner delayed again as preliminary inquiry awaits; accused of setting 61-year-old girlfriend on fire

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Nearly a year after 61-year-old school warden Dawn Bernard was allegedly set on fire by her common-law husband, Frederick Wagner, the murder case against him has suffered another delay.

Wagner appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, October 9, but proceedings were adjourned because the Chief Magistrate, who has carriage of the matter, was unavailable. Wagner, who remains unrepresented, is now scheduled to return to court on October 26, 2026, as the case awaits a preliminary inquiry.

The latest adjournment follows earlier delays, including a June court appearance when prosecutors acknowledged that the case file was still not ready despite Wagner having been charged with murder in December 2025.

The case stems from a disturbing incident on November 10, 2025, at Bernard’s Lakeview Street residence in Belize City. According to police, Bernard suffered extensive burns to her face, shoulders, chest, back and hands after allegedly being doused with rubbing alcohol and set ablaze.

Before her condition deteriorated, Bernard reportedly identified Wagner as her attacker, telling investigators, “Da meh man do meh this.” She later slipped into a coma and died on November 16.

Wagner was initially charged with attempted murder and use of deadly means of harm on November 14. Following Bernard’s death and a post-mortem examination, he was formally charged with murder on December 10, 2025.

Police previously confirmed that Bernard had made a domestic violence complaint against Wagner in 2018, although no additional complaints were recorded afterward. Her death sparked renewed concern over domestic violence and the dangers faced by women in abusive relationships.

Wagner remains on remand at the Belize Central Prison. The murder allegation against him has not been proven in court.

World.title: No case file ready for Dean Vaccaro, accused of murdering 15-year-old Rackeem Armstrong; case adjourned until December
World.content:
No case file ready for Dean Vaccaro, accused of murdering 15-year-old Rackeem Armstrong; case adjourned until December

By Breaking Belize News Staff: More than four months after being charged with the murder of 15-year-old Rackeem Armstrong and the attempted murder of his 18-year-old cousin, Justin Young, Dean Emerson Vaccaro, 34, remains without disclosure of the prosecution’s case against him.

Vaccaro, a labourer of Sandhill Village, appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Friday, October 9, where prosecutors informed the Senior Magistrate that the case file was still not ready and had been returned to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for further work.

The prosecution indicated that it remained within the required timeframe for disclosure, and the court granted another adjournment until December 18, 2026.

Vaccaro was arraigned on June 3 on four indictable charges: murder, attempted murder, use of deadly means of harm, and dangerous harm. He was remanded to the Belize Central Prison.

The charges stem from a deadly shooting in Gardenia Village on May 31, when a gunman approached a group of relatives gathered outside and opened fire, killing Armstrong and seriously injuring Young.

Armstrong, an honour-roll student at Ladyville Technical High School who reportedly dreamed of joining the Belize Coast Guard, was shot in the head and shoulder. Young suffered extensive injuries, including a gunshot wound near his spine, raising concerns about his ability to walk again.

Police previously indicated that the shooting may have stemmed from a dispute involving a motorcycle, although investigators had not established who the intended target was. Authorities were also seeking another suspect in connection with the incident.

Vaccaro remains on remand as the case awaits further proceedings.

World.title: No case file yet for duo accused of murdering friend Jamir Cambranes; court grants another adjournment
World.content:
No case file yet for duo accused of murdering friend Jamir Cambranes; court grants another adjournment

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Two Belize City men accused of murdering their 19-year-old friend, Jamir Rudel Cambranes, returned to court on Friday, October 9, but their case was adjourned after prosecutors revealed that the case file was still not ready for disclosure.

Kameron Kareem Heusner, 21, and Kenrick Lindbergh Robinson, 19, appeared before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2, where the prosecution informed the court that the disclosure materials remained unavailable. The matter was subsequently adjourned to October 19, 2026.

Both men are charged with the murder of Cambranes, a Belize City technician whose bullet-riddled body was discovered in bushes along the Burrell Boom/Hattieville Road on April 22, 2026.

According to police, Cambranes was last seen alive on April 21, when he reportedly met with individuals known to him before entering a silver Chevrolet Equinox. Investigators say surveillance footage captured the young man entering the vehicle outside Robinson’s residence on Laura Dunn Street before it headed toward Ladyville.

Cambranes reportedly sent his girlfriend a photograph of the vehicle’s license plate shortly before he stopped responding to her calls and messages. Concerned for his safety, she tracked his phone and alerted his relatives, who subsequently discovered his body.

Police later recovered surveillance footage, WhatsApp communications and forensic evidence from the vehicle, including blood samples, which helped investigators identify the suspects.

Robinson was arraigned on April 27, while Heusner was charged two days later and arraigned on April 30. Both were remanded to prison.

Police previously indicated that no clear motive had been established for the killing. Both accused men remain on remand as the case awaits disclosure of the prosecution’s evidence.

World.title: Second suspect charged in armed home invasion of Belize City tacos lady; Over $2,500 in jewelry stolen
World.content:
Second suspect charged in armed home invasion of Belize City tacos lady; Over $2,500 in jewelry stolen

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A second suspect has been charged and remanded to prison in connection with the armed home invasion of a Belize City taco vendor, during which more than $2,500 worth of jewelry was stolen.

Celestino Anwar Zetina, 24, appeared before Senior Magistrate Mannon Dennison on Friday, October 9, where he pleaded not guilty to a charge of aggravated burglary. Bail was denied because the alleged offence involved firearms, and he was remanded to the Belize Central Prison until November 2, 2026.

Zetina joins 18-year-old Shawn Garbutt, who was previously charged and remanded in connection with the same incident. Both men are scheduled to appear in court together on November 2.

The charges stem from an armed home invasion at the Castle Street residence of a taco vendor. According to police, the woman was leaving her home at approximately 5:50 a.m. when two masked men, allegedly armed with firearms, confronted her and forced her back inside while demanding money.

The intruders reportedly stole a jewelry box containing a gold chain, diamond rings and other jewelry valued at approximately $2,525 before escaping.

Garbutt was arraigned on September 28 and pleaded not guilty. During his initial court appearance, he reportedly claimed police had only found him in possession of an elephant pendant and that he had initially been told he would face a charge of handling stolen goods rather than aggravated burglary.

With Zetina’s arraignment, both accused men are now behind bars awaiting further court proceedings. The allegations against them have not been proven in court.

World.title: National Kriol Council condemns ‘degrading racial caricatures’ on cover of Assad Shoman’s new history book
World.content:
National Kriol Council condemns ‘degrading racial caricatures’ on cover of Assad Shoman’s new history book

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The National Kriol Council (NKC) has strongly condemned what it describes as exaggerated and degrading racial imagery on the cover of historian Assad Shoman’s newly released A History of Belize in Thirteen Chapters, calling on the author and publisher to explain the controversial artwork.

In a statement issued on October 9, during Kriol Heritage Month, the Council said the depiction of Black figures on the cover evokes racist caricatures historically used to ridicule and dehumanize people of African descent.

The controversy surrounds the book’s Sapphire Edition, launched on October 9 at Angelus Press. The publication is the third edition of Shoman’s influential historical work, first published in 1994 and widely used in Belizean educational institutions. The latest edition includes updated material addressing the environment, economy, Guatemala’s territorial claim, and human rights.

While acknowledging the historical significance of Belize’s Coat of Arms, which features two woodcutters, the NKC argues that historical symbolism does not excuse imagery it considers offensive.

“Our ancestors were not caricatures. They were people whose labour, resilience, resistance, knowledge, and cultural contributions helped shape Belize,” the Council declared.

The organization called on Shoman and the publisher to explain the selection of the cover and reconsider whether it appropriately reflects the dignity of the people depicted. It also urged cultural authorities to ensure greater recognition of Kriol identity and Maroon heritage in official historical documentation.

The controversy had already attracted public criticism following the book’s release, with members of the Kriol cultural heritage community questioning whether the artwork resembles blackface caricatures. Love FM

The Council maintained that preserving historical records should not mean perpetuating the indignities of the colonial past.

“Our ancestors deserve dignity. Our history deserves truth. Our heritage deserves protection. Our identity deserves respect,” the statement declared.

The NKC concluded with a forceful message: “WE WILL NOT ACCEPT ERASURE.”

World.title: Taiwan thanks Belize, praises Francis Fonseca and blasts China’s sanctions as political intimidation
World.content:
Taiwan thanks Belize, praises Francis Fonseca and blasts China’s sanctions as political intimidation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Taiwan has strongly condemned China’s decision to sanction Belize’s Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca, describing Beijing’s actions as political intimidation and an unacceptable interference in the sovereignty and foreign policies of independent nations.

In a statement issued Monday, October 12, Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the sanctions “preposterous” and accused China of attempting to coerce other countries into submitting to its political agenda through intimidation and transnational repression. The Ministry also described Beijing’s tactics as “despicable.”

The Taiwanese Embassy in Belize also publicly expressed appreciation for Belize’s continued support, posting a message thanking the government and people of Belize for standing firmly with Taiwan and fighting against what it described as oppression and intimidation from authoritarianism.

“We also wish to extend our utmost respect for Minister Hon. Francis Fonseca,” the Embassy stated in a message published on its official Facebook page.

Taiwan further maintained that it is a sovereign, independent country and that China has no right to interfere in its diplomatic relationships. It reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening cooperation with Belize and Paraguay, emphasizing that its partnerships are built on equality, mutual respect and shared democratic values.

China announced sanctions against Fonseca and Paraguay’s Communications Minister Gustavo Villate earlier Monday, imposing travel bans, restrictions on business dealings with Chinese entities and the freezing of any assets they may hold in China. Beijing accused both officials of undermining its sovereignty through their support for Taiwan.

The Government of Belize has also rejected the sanctions, declaring that the measures will not alter its foreign policy or deter it from maintaining diplomatic relations with Taiwan. Belize’s Foreign Ministry emphasized that Fonseca was carrying out his official duties in the national interest.

The diplomatic confrontation comes just weeks after Taiwan’s Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung visited Belize and signed new cooperation agreements with Fonseca. Belize and Taiwan established diplomatic relations in 1989 and marked their 37th anniversary on October 11, just one day before China announced the sanctions.

World.title: Waterhouse fine sparks questions over JC star Lyle’s eligibility in schoolboy football
World.content:
Jamaica College forward Jamone Lyle (third left) gets away from St Catherine High School’s Caiden Yen (on ground) while his teammates Jaquan Brown and Davill Jarrett (right) look on during their ISSA Manning Cup game at Ashenheim Stadium in St Andrew on Wednesday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

KINGSTON, Jamaica – A major controversy has erupted around Jamaica College’s (JC) 2026 Inter-Secondary Schools Sports Association (ISSA) schoolboy football campaign following revelations that star player Jamone Lyle has signed a professional contract, potentially rendering him ineligible for high school competition.

The issue came to a head following a disciplinary letter issued by Jamaica Premier League club Waterhouse Football Club, who Lyle represents in that competition.

The letter, dated October 9, 2026, details a disciplinary hearing where Waterhouse FC fined Lyle $60,000 for “unauthorised participation” in a Manning Cup match on October 7, 2026. According to the club, Lyle ignored explicit instructions from head coach Donovan Duckie and general secretary Richard McCallum, prohibiting him from taking the field for JC, thereby breaching his professional contract and club rules.

Under longstanding ISSA regulations, student-athletes who have signed professional contracts or actively participate in professional senior leagues are strictly prohibited from competing in schoolboy competitions like the Manning Cup and Walker Cup.

Lyle, who recently earned his senior Reggae Boyz debut against El Salvador in the Concacaf Nations League, played a pivotal role in JC’s 3–2 victory days later and again last Saturday in the Walker Cup semifinal win against Mona High, where he scored in normal time and during JC’s penalty shootout victory.

The implications of Lyle’s involvement extend well beyond an internal club fine. ISSA rules mandate severe penalties for schools fielding ineligible or professional players, although they softened the rule, allowing students – who have not signed professional contracts – to compete in both competitions five days after playing in either.

In 2019, ISSA denied Portmore United’s Lamar Walker of Clarendon College from participating in schoolboy football after he went on a tryout to Brazilian club Vaco da Gama. Similarly, he had just made his senior debut for Jamaica.

World.title: Absent witness, IT issues delay Ruel Reid and Co trial
World.content:
Former Education Minister Ruel Reid heading to court.

An absent witness meant no evidence was elicited in the trial of former Education Minister Ruel Reid, Former head of the Caribbean Maritime University (CMU) Fritz Pinnock, and their co-accused at the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court on Monday.

The trial also started late, as when parties arrived for 10:00 am, the technology used to facilitate virtual attendance and record the trial was not ready.

It meant the matter had to be stood down while the accused, defence attorneys, and the prosecution waited almost two hours for the requisite individual, with knowledge of how to operate the system, to arrive and set up.

When proceedings eventually got underway at almost 12:00 pm, Senior Deputy Director of Public Prosecutions Ashtelle Steele indicated to presiding Judge Sanchia Burrell that the witness scheduled to take the stand on Monday was unavoidably absent due to unforeseen circumstances.

Burrell noted, however, that the prosecution ought to have multiple witnesses on standby for situations such as this.

Steele, in response, shared that the order in which witnesses are being called had been reshuffled the week prior to facilitate defence attorneys and that had affected this week as well.

“So your ability to plan and organise your witnesses is still impacted by the attendance of the attorneys,” the judge said.

More than 90 witnesses are expected to be called in the fraud trial of the five accused, which also includes Reid’s wife and daughter Sharen and Sharelle Reid, and Jamaica Labour Party Councillor Kim Brown Lawrence.

While there are 35 counts in total in the trial, the accused are charged with different counts and different witnesses are expected to affect different and sometimes multiple accused.

While Burrell lauded the conciliatory approach taken by the prosecution in how the witnesses are being called and noted she was not interfering with it, she added that there comes a time when the Crown just has to proceed.

Steele emphasised strongly that, with the testimony of one witness expected to be called later this week, all accused persons need representation present.

She also noted that testimony expected this week would be document-heavy, adding that the arrangement in which some attorneys tune in via Zoom may not be suitable for that.

“We do not recommend that counsel be online,” she said.

Brown Lawrence’s attorney Oswest Senior Smith was represented in court by a junior while listening in via Zoom were Carolyn Chuck, who represents Sharelle Reid, and Linda Wright, who represents the former education minister.

Chuck held for Shannen Clarke, who represents Sharen Reid.

Several attorneys in the fraud trial, including Hugh Wildman, who represents Pinnock, and Wright, also sit in the ongoing murder trial of six policemen occurring simultaneously in the Supreme Court in downtown Kingston.

Burrell had previously warned Pinnock he could possibly have to cross-examine a witness himself during the Monday sitting if an attorney did not turn up to represent him.

In addressing him directly on Monday, she queried whether he wished to place anything on the record regarding representation.

He indicated that his attorney had shared an email but did not share the contents with the court.

In response, Burrell indicated that an email could not be placed on the record.

“There is a way that we practise in the court; it’s not ad hoc,” she said, highlighting procedure that had shortly before taken place with other attorneys indicating absences or holding.

“There is a way that things are done and I will not, under my stewardship, be deviating from the proper way that we were all taught to do things,” she maintained.

The judge added that she had never seen it done, where emails are sent regarding matters that must be on the record.

She added that there have also been some inappropriate actions, citing emails sent to the judge, with accused persons attached to the correspondence.

Pinnock requested he be allowed to take notes on his laptop to which Burrell agreed, but noted that certain safeguards would have to be put in place.

However, without a witness, the trial adjourned until Tuesday at 2:00 pm.

Prosecutors allege that between March 2016 and October 2019 the five accused participated in a scheme with others unknown, which siphoned off more than $25 million from both the Ministry of Education and CMU.

It is alleged that this money was funnelled through transfers to various accounts either owned or controlled by the accused, or handed over in cash.

The accused have all pleaded not guilty to the charges.

– Dana Malcolm

World.title: The 20-round loophole in the Firearms Act
World.content:
Four entries were made to the Licence Management System of a firearms dealer of three individuals purchasing a total of 6,000 12-gauge bird-hunting ammunition, without the request or consent of the dealer.

Even as defence lawyers protest the rigidity of the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022, calling for a review by legislators, proponents have pointed to a section that allows offenders with up to 19 rounds of illegal ammunition to evade the mandatory minimum sentences being balked at by the legal fraternity.

If convicted under Section 45 of the Act for unauthorised possession of ammunition, the Sixth Schedule outlines the penalty for an unlicensed person as ‘on summary conviction before a parish court, a fine, not exceeding five million dollars, or imprisonment, for a term not exceeding five years’.

To the chagrin of proponents of the disputed Act, attorney-at-law Ruel Gibson of Stubbs, Gibson and Associates explained that the difference lies in the number of rounds as evidenced by Sections 5 and 10.

“It appears that Section 45 allows the parish court to deal with matters of illegal possession of ammunition by an unlicensed person, providing that the amount is under 20 rounds. Being in possession of 20 rounds, or more, as per Section 10, makes the offence tantamount to that of dealing in prohibited weapons, which becomes a Gun Court matter, carrying a minimum penalty of 20 years upon conviction,” Gibson remarked.

Explaining how an increased number of illegal rounds possessed by an unlicensed person further triggers mandatory minimum sentencing, Gibson pointed to Section 6 (1) (b).

“Section 6 deems the possession of 50 rounds or more to be stockpiling of prohibited weapons, which would result in a minimum penalty of 20 years. Therefore, evidently, under 20 rounds allows sentencing flexibility in the parish court,” Gibson added.

However, proponents of the Act have lashed out at illegal possession of ammunition being tried in the parish court, pointing to the capacity of most handguns, the murder weapons of choice for criminals, carrying a maximum of 18 rounds.

Criminologist Dr Jason McKay, an active serving police officer, agreed that aspects of the Act are in need of review, suggesting there should be a separate Act, distinguishing licensed firearm holders, who could easily be in possession of an extra round for many reasons including sport-shooting but was adamant that no leeway should be afforded unlicensed persons found in possession of illegal ammunition.

“It does not take more than one round to take a life,” McKay pointed out. “Homemade firearms with one round, ‘one-pop’ guns, will kill you as instantly as the most expensive pistol on the market.

“Gunmen do not walk around with extra magazines to put themselves in the 20-or-more category. Therefore, if a premises, or person, is searched and ammunition recovered, it will rarely ever exceed 17 rounds. Does that make any of those bullets less deadlier than 20 rounds?” McKay asked.

However, he shared concerns with the legal fraternity about the treatment of imitation firearms under the Act.

“Possession of imitation firearms should come down to a matter of circumstances and intent, particularly if used in the commission of a crime,” he said.

World.title: 7 Jamaicans feature on Rolling Stone’s ‘Best Albums of 1976’ list

World.title: Seiveright apologises to Barita over social media post, acknowledges ‘unfair impression’
World.content:
Delano Seiveright

Government Minister Delano Seiveright has expressed regret over a social media post concerning the pilot rollout of a product by the Barita Financial Group, acknowledging that his comments may have created an “unfair impression” of the initiative. The minister has also issued an apology to the board and management of Barita, and has withdrawn the post.

“Having received further clarification, I regret any unfair impression my earlier posts may have created about Barita,” Seiveright said in a subsequent post on social media. “I apologise to its Board and staff, Chairman Mark Myers, CD, & Deputy Chairman Paul Simpson, CD, and have withdrawn the posts.

“I welcome Barita’s initiative, wish it continued success and remain committed to these broader principles,” he said.

Barita Financial Group has announced the controlled pilot rollout of BPay by Barita, a digital wallet offered by Barita Merchant Bank Limited, a deposit-taking institution licensed by the Bank of Jamaica (BOJ).

In a statement Sunday, the company noted that the initiative is “focused on bringing digital financial services directly to communities, campuses and workplaces.”
