World.title: Estonia's defense ministry allocates €250,000 for war movies
World.content:
The MoD has announced a funding competition worth €250,000 to support the production of films and other audiovisual works aimed at strengthening the Estonian public's willingness to defend the country.

"I would like to impress upon everyone on the committee selecting these films at the Ministry of Defense that any film that is overly propagandistic or too polished and carefully packaged is actually less credible. When we talk about defending Estonia, my view, my belief, is that the truth ultimately works best," film director Ilmar Raag commented.

The Ministry of Defense is inviting submissions for feature films, documentaries, animated films, television series and narrative video games. The ministry has supported the production of Estonian war films for more than 20 years, including "Names in Marble," "1944" and "O2."

According to ministry representative Thomas Mell, different audiovisual formats make it possible to reach different generations.

"The willingness to defend the country is an important part of Estonia's national defense and strengthening it is one of our core responsibilities. Supporting films and other audiovisual works is one way to contribute to this. Film is a medium that reaches a wide audience, as do video games nowadays, for example, and they help communicate national defense issues in ways that resonate with different generations," Mell said.

Raag, who previously received funding through a Ministry of Defense competition to produce a documentary, believes that funding decisions must also take into account the potential for a backlash.

"O2". Source: Karl Anders Vaikla

"Those who allocate funding at the ministry need to recognize that if a filmmaker takes an overly simplistic, propagandistic approach, it could actually backfire," Raag noted.

To qualify for Ministry of Defense funding, projects must align with national defense objectives. This raises the question of how much influence the state, as a funder, can exert over a film's content.

"As the Ministry of Defense, we do not interfere in any way with filmmakers' creative freedom. We do not dictate scripts, themes or how characters should be portrayed. Instead, filmmakers themselves are free to submit their proposals to us," Mell explained.

The Ministry of Defense is accepting applications until November 18. The funding can be used next year.

World.title: Gallery: See what the Pirita River estuary will look like in the future
World.content:
The winning design for developing the area near the mouth of the Pirita River envisions residential buildings, commercial spaces, a hotel and a promenade.

The aim of the competition announced this summer was to find a cohesive architectural design for the area that would be practical, technically feasible and economically viable. A total of 15 entries were submitted.

"While the quality of the entries varied and not all the proposals met the client's expectations, the competition nevertheless achieved its goal: We found a very strong design that clearly stood out from the rest and the jury's decision was unanimous," said jury chairman Aivar Tuulberg, chairman of the supervisory board of the Tallinn Olympic Sailing Center (TOP).

The winning entry was designed by Maarja Kask, Ralf Lõoke and Martin McLean of architecture firm Salto. Their design draws on the site's location between the sea and the river. The proposal's defining architectural feature is its stepped buildings.

In addition to apartments, the development will include a hotel, spa, swimming pool, curling facility, sports and fitness facilities and a health center. Plans also call for a restaurant and cafe, retail, service and office space, a childcare facility and an event and conference hall.

The winning design for the Pirita TOP area. Source: Maarja Kask, Ralf Lõoke and Martin McLean from Salto architects.

The development's largest public square is planned for the waterfront, overlooking the Tallinn skyline and will connect to the seaside promenade. A separate plaza will be created in front of the hotel entrance.

An underground parking garage will be built, with its entrance located on Topi tänav.

The developer's next step is to proceed with the detailed spatial plan and work with the winning architects to further develop the design.

"It is still too early to give specific dates, but our goal is to move forward as smoothly and quickly as possible in cooperation with the City of Tallinn," Tuulberg added.

The architectural competition jury comprised chairman Aivar Tuulberg, TOP representative Margus Hütt, Tallinn Urban Planning Department architect Kalle Rannula and architects Mari Hunt and Emil Urbel, representing the Estonian Association of Architects.

World.title: Ukraine strikes on Yandex data centers cut traffic to Estonian sites nearly 100%
World.content:
Traffic from Russia's Yandex network to Estonian websites has fallen nearly 100 percent following Ukrainian strikes on the internet company's data centers.

The Information System Authority (RIA) says average requests from Yandex fell roughly 420 times by October 13 compared with September's average, following strikes last week. RIA puts the overall drop in Yandex traffic to Estonian sites at 99.8 percent.

Ukraine struck three Yandex data centers last week — one near Moscow on Sunday, one in Sasovo on Thursday and one in Kaluga on Friday.

"The average number of queries coming from the Yandex network has decreased by 99.8 percent, or roughly 420 times, compared with the September average, as of October 13," said Simon Berner, an analyst at RIA's analysis and prevention department.

Yandex was forced to suspend operations at the data center near Moscow on Sunday after the facility was damaged in a Ukrainian drone strike.

Foreign media has reported that the strikes on Yandex also dealt a blow to the Kremlin's online influence operations, including via bot activity in English, which often takes a far-right perspective.

RIA says, however, that it is too early to assess possible changes in the activity of cyberattacks carried out by Russia.

"At the same time, there is no reason to assume that disruptions to Yandex data centers would have a significant effect on the frequency of cyberattacks directed against Estonia. Various infrastructures are used to carry out attacks, and these do not depend on the functioning of Yandex services," Berner said.

Monitoring Russia's influence activities, including the activity of social media bots and troll accounts, does not fall within RIA's competence, so the authority cannot confirm or refute claims that their activity has decreased.

Yandex also operates food delivery and taxi apps used by tens of millions of people; it has previously said its data centers are essential to the normal functioning of its services.

Yandex taxi services in Estonia were banned shortly after the start of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Estonia to sound nationwide sirens in emergency alert test Wednesday
World.content:
A nationwide EE-ALARM public warning test is to take place Wednesday, with sirens sounding between 3 p.m. and 3:10 p.m.

An SMS reminder will go out around midday. No action is needed during the test; in a real emergency residents should seek shelter.

The test, on Wednesday, October 14, will sound public sirens across the country and send notifications through the Eesti app and the "Ole valmis!" mobile application, as well as a ticker message on ERR's channels.

On 14 October, Estonia will conduct its third nationwide EE-ALARM public warning test of the year. An SMS reminder will be sent around midday. Between 15:00–15:10, sirens will sound, with alerts via the Eesti and Ole Valmis! apps and ERR channels. ⚠️ No action is needed during the test. In a real emergency, seek shelter! — Estonian Defence Forces | Kaitsevägi (@Kaitsevagi) October 12, 2026

No notification will be sent sent when the test ends. The aim is to check the system's reliability, verify repairs and updates, and identify any shortfalls.

The Rescue Board asks residents to think in advance about where they would shelter at home, at work or at school. A recent survey found over two-thirds of Estonian residents would look for the safest place in their home, usually the basement, if told to shelter, but only about a quarter believe they already have such a feature in their home.

The test follows an accidental siren activation in Muuga on October 6 during routine maintenance work, ERR's Russian-language portal reported.

Wednesday's event the last of three nationwide tests in 2026. The others took place in March and June. Next year's tests are scheduled for February, June and October 2027.

More detailed information is here, and is also available from the kriis.ee site here and the Rescue Board here, while the Ole Valmis/Be Prepared app can be downloded here or from Google Play and Apple app stores.

World.title: Outgoing presidential culture adviser: Staying creative is important
World.content:
After five years serving as President Alar Karis' culture adviser, Estonian composer Rasmus Puur says the job shouldn't come at the expense of staying active creatively.

Puur joined Karis' team while studying at the Sibelius Academy in Helsinki. He initially had no plans to take the job but was eventually persuaded to try it.

Working quarter-time allowed him to continue composing and other creative work, though the workload sometimes resembled a full-time job.

"Anyone who's ever worked part time knows it can vary a lot — sometimes you end up working full time, sometimes you could do a little less," he said, adding that those times you could squeeze in an orchestra rehearsal or do something else.

Puur had to fit composing around the president's schedule, sometimes turning down commissions and racing to finish pieces during quieter interludes.

"I'd know the president was on a visit to somewhere in the U.S. that week and think, 'OK, things are a little quieter for now, so I need to get this piece written,'" he recalled.

Still, he stressed the importance of not losing touch creatively.

"With this kind of job, I think it's very important to stay connected to your creative self and the wider [creative] scene, so you don't end up isolated from it," the composer said.

Showing up, new traditions

A key part of Puur's role was helping the Estonian president engage with cultural events and recognize creatives' work. Even simply showing up, paying attention or presenting an award can mean a great deal to people in the field, he said.

During Karis' five-year term, the head of state attended major cultural anniversaries, song festivals and other events, and even served as official patron of the Year of the Estonian Book.

New traditions included annual reading marathons on the presidential palace's front steps in Kadriorg each March and the establishment of Estonian Literature Day, observed January 30, when the president announces the Literature Teacher of the Year.

Puur also highlighted Karis' visits to communities across the country for Mother's Day and Father's Day celebrations, which helped bring people together and put local events and efforts in the national spotlight.

Native Language Day 12-hour reading outside Kadriorg, Friday, March 14, 2025. Source: Raigo Pajula/Office of the President of the Republic

"Showing Kilingi-Nõmme, Haljala or the Jõgeva Cultural Center live on public broadcasting, with the president speaking there, is hugely important to that local community," he stressed.

Karis also took cultural figures with him on foreign visits to build international ties and open new doors for Estonian artists.

"He genuinely believed that art and culture can sometimes reach people more effectively than traditional diplomacy," Puur said.

One example was a proposed exhibition of Estonian painter Konrad Mägi at Paris' Musée d'Orsay, an idea discussed during the Estonian delegation's visit during the 2024 Summer Olympics and now potentially back under consideration.

What comes next

Puur said his time at the Office of the President (VPK) taught him the importance of a close-knit team, particularly in a fast-paced environment where decisions carry significant responsibility. Running important questions by each other helped, he said, as did being able to joke around while under pressure.

As Karis leaves office, replaced by the newly sworn-in President Ülle Madise, Puur will hand over the title of presidential culture adviser to Jaak Prints.

He said there are no fixed job instructions for the role, which each president and adviser shapes according to their own personalities and priorities.

Under Karis, he believes, cultural figures felt their work received attention and recognition, even as arts organizations faced funding shortages and cuts.

Puur, meanwhile, has no firm plans for what comes next. For now, the composer wants to adjust to life outside the VPK again, and see where music and other opportunities might take him.

"One day at a time," he said. "I have some ideas, but first let's see what civilian life is like; it's been a while since I've experienced it."

Conductor Rasmus Puur and singer Mari Kalkun at the 2025 Song and Dance Festival in Tallinn. Source: Ken Mürk /ERR

World.title: IMF projects Iraq’s economy to contract by 16% in 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts a 16 percent contraction in Iraq’s real GDP in 2026, followed by a 19 percent growth in 2027, according to statistics from the October 2026 World Economic Outlook report.

Estimates indicate rising inflation and a widening current account deficit in 2026.

Iraq’s economy fell by 0.4 percent in 2025. Meanwhile, the IMF forecasts a 3.5 percent inflation rate in 2026, compared to 0.3 percent in 2025, before falling to three percent in 2027.

The IMF predicts Iraq will have a deficit of 10.8 percent of GDP in 2026, up from 3.8 percent in 2025, before moving to a 2.2 percent surplus in 2027.

According to these predictions, Iraq is one of the region’s oil-exporting economies that will decline in 2026; the numbers show a 3.8 percent contraction for these oil exporters, followed by 7.4 percent growth in 2027.

According to the analysis, Saudi Arabia’s real GDP would fall by 3.3 percent, the UAE’s by 3.9 percent, Qatar’s by 15.6 percent, and Kuwait’s by 16.7 percent in 2026, before rising again in 2027.

Figures for Iraq show a sharp contrast between the 2026 and 2027 predictions, with the economy transitioning from severe decline to solid growth—according to the IMF.

The projected growth in 2027 does not imply an increase in living standards or household financial situations, as these metrics are still dependent on other factors such as employment possibilities, income levels, inflation, and public finance performance.

World.title: Iraq and Saudi’s Acwa discuss doubling Najaf solar project to 2,000 MW
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is considering doubling the capacity of a planned solar power plant in Najaf from 1,000 to 2,000 megawatts following discussions between Iraq’s Minister of Electricity Ali Saadi Waheeb and Saudi energy company Acwa in Riyadh.

Waheeb met with Acwa Chairman Mohammed Abunayyan on the sidelines of the 25th WPC Energy Congress, where the two parties evaluated the planned solar project’s development and discussed the next stages in its execution.

According to the Iraqi Minister, the talks centered on accelerating the preparation and finalization of Acwa’s commercial proposal for the Najaf development.

The two parties also discussed the idea of increasing the plant’s projected generating capacity to 2,000 MW and integrating battery energy storage systems (BESS) at a recommended 30% ratio.

The prospective extension would greatly expand the project’s size, although the parties have not yet announced a final decision on increased capacity or amended investment conditions.

Iraq’s departing Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Safia Taleb Ali al-Suhail, attended the meeting.

Aside from the Najaf solar expansion, Waheeb and Abunayyan addressed potential collaboration in managing and maintaining existing Iraqi power plants.

The Iraqi minister indicated an interest in using Acwa’s technical and operational knowledge to increase plant efficiency and conduct a pilot project at an existing functioning power-producing facility in Iraq.

The Najaf solar project goes back to 2023, when Acwa agreed to build a 1,000 MW solar plant in the governorate, around 160 kilometers south of Baghdad.

The facility was suggested as part of Iraq’s aim to increase large-scale renewable energy production and decrease reliance on conventional power facilities.

Iraq has been working to diversify its power mix and attract foreign investment as growing demand, aging infrastructure, and fuel supply problems continue to pressure the national system.

The Riyadh meetings indicate fresh attempts to develop the Najaf project, with the commercial concept and prospective capacity growth still under consideration.

World.title: Tom Barrack meets Iraqi PM in Baghdad as bilateral ties enter new phase
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US Envoy to Iraq and Syria Tom Barrack met with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi in Baghdad, emphasizing Washington’s sustained involvement with Iraq as the two nations prepare to enter a new chapter of ties after the departure of US-led coalition troops.

Barrack regarded the discussion as positive and lauded the Iraqi prime minister’s leadership, linking Iraq’s stability and prosperity to regional security.

“Stability is not inherited; it is built by leaders who choose the hard road,” Barrack wrote on X after the meeting.

“Iraq’s security and prosperity are the region’s,” he said, praising al-Zaidi for his leadership and collaboration.

The meeting comes after the US-led coalition completed its military operation in Iraq on September 30, marking a dramatic shift in ties between Baghdad and Washington.

At the time, Barrack praised the pullout, claiming that US President Donald Trump had brought Baghdad, Erbil, regional allies, and Washington’s interests together in a common strategic framework.

Barrack also portrayed the transition as a chance for Iraq to place its armed forces under unified state leadership, with the US retaining a connection with Baghdad via diplomacy and collaboration rather than a permanent military presence.

“With that alignment, a door long closed has opened,” Barrack wrote on September 30, alluding to Iraq’s ability to consolidate state control over its security institutions.

He described the growing relationship as one in which “America is a friend rather than a garrison.”

The current Baghdad conference takes place as Iraq and the United States strive to widen their alliance beyond the military war against ISIS, with a focus on economic cooperation, investment, diplomacy, and common regional interests.

Barrack has also met with top Iraqi officials recently, including Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein in Turkey and Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zaidan in Baghdad, as Washington continues high-level engagement with Iraq’s political and judicial institutions.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia discuss energy cooperation as electricity and oil ministers meet in Riyadh
World.content:
Riyadh (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Oil Minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, and Iraq’s Electricity Minister, Ali Saadi Waheeb, met with Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman in Riyadh to discuss extending bilateral energy cooperation and boosting coordination between the two nations.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the 25th WPC Energy Congress, sponsored by Saudi Arabia and attended by energy ministers, industry executives, and representatives from major international energy firms.

According to Waheeb, the talks focused on ways to increase energy cooperation and create tighter coordination in accordance with Iraq and Saudi Arabia’s interests.

The Iraqi electrical minister emphasized Baghdad’s desire to continue discussions with Riyadh and expand areas of collaboration, particularly in ways that could help improve the stability of Iraq’s power system.

The meetings brought together Iraq’s two senior energy ministers and their Saudi counterparts at a time when regional energy security, infrastructure investment, and dependable power supply are still top considerations.

Iraq has been attempting to modernize its electrical infrastructure, diversify energy suppliers, and establish regional alliances in response to local power constraints and rising demand.

The Riyadh meeting was part of a larger series of engagements by Iraqi energy officials at the congress, which included talks with neighboring countries about electrical interconnections, technical cooperation, and investment prospects.

Additionally, the high-level meeting came after a separate high-level energy meeting in Baghdad on Saturday, when Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi welcomed TotalEnergies CEO Patrick Pouyanné and ConocoPhillips CEO Andy O’Brien, along with their teams.

The talks in Baghdad centered on investment in oil production and related gas at Basra’s Bin Umar oilfield, including deadlines for raising output and chances to extend production in adjacent locations.

World.title: Tom Barrack meets Iraq’s top judge Faiq Zaidan in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US Envoy Tom Barrack met with Iraq’s top judicial leadership in Baghdad on Monday, as Washington and Baghdad strive to rebuild their bilateral relationship in the face of regional tensions and a shifting security situation.

Barrack met with Judge Faiq Zaidan, President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, to explore ways to strengthen bilateral legal and judicial collaboration.

The meeting comes at a difficult time for the region, after fatal assaults on Riyadh’s international airport over the weekend, which Saudi officials blamed on Yemen’s Houthi movement.

In a statement issued after the negotiations, Barrack praised his meeting with Zaidan as positive and emphasized the necessity of an independent judiciary for Iraq’s future.

“A strong, independent judiciary is the bedrock of sovereignty, the rule of law, and the stability that lets Iraq turn its potential into prosperity,” Barrack wrote, thanking Zaidan for his partnership.

Barrack also met with Steve Fagin, the United States’ chargé d’affaires in Baghdad, and praised his diplomatic skills while emphasizing Washington’s aspirations to broaden its relationship with Iraq beyond security cooperation.

He regarded the present time as a watershed point in bilateral ties, stating that the United States was moving toward a more comprehensive relationship based on economic cooperation and common interests.

The Baghdad talks follow Barrack’s weekend conversations with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein in Turkey, during which the two sides discussed bilateral ties and regional events.

The diplomatic contacts follow the completion of the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, signaling a move toward a bilateral partnership based on political, economic, and security cooperation.

World.title: British airbase plot ‘almost certainly directed’ by Iran Guards: UK PM
World.content:
London – Britain’s government Monday accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of being behind a major scare at a UK airbase used by the United States, as allies including Washington warned Tehran against hostile acts.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the British parliament that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) “almost certainly directed” an incident at Royal Air Force Fairford in southwest England last month.

The US, which had been using the base for its war in Iran, abruptly withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the site last week after the mysterious episode on September 27.

Burnham said Britain’s assessment of the incident was that it “is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard”.

“We will not tolerate these threats on our soil. We will crack down on Iran’s use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams,” he told MPs.

Shortly afterwards, 29 countries, including the US, Britain, Australia, Canada, France and Germany, released a joint statement denouncing “in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks”.

The statement said such attacks included “acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners”.

“Any attempt by Iran to threaten, silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce people on our territories through proxies or any other means is unacceptable,” it read.

The Foreign Office confirmed in its own statement Monday that Iran’s ambassador to the UK had been summoned for talks.

“We are also announcing the designation of two Iranian nationals for their role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime, with the clear intent of threatening, planning or conducting attacks overseas,” foreign minister Ed Miliband said.

The foreign ministry said the individuals included Ruhollah Bazghandi, the IRGC’s head of counterespionage operations, who is “now subject to an immediate asset freeze, travel ban and director disqualification”.

Speculation has swirled about the incident since police were called to the base after a local farmer reported a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.

– ‘Major’ incident –

Despite a major counter-terrorism probe, seven suspects arrested in the days following, including a British-Iranian national, have all since been released on bail. None has been charged.

The incident was declared “major” by British authorities and triggered the evacuation of a nearby village.

But the source and nature of the threat have remained shrouded in mystery.

Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but did recover some petrol, according to officials.

Burnham has previously said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, which Tehran has rejected.

Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran,” and US bombers and other planes had been seen taking off and landing at the base.

US President Donald Trump has said Washington withdrew its bombers because of “threats” he believed were linked to Tehran.

In the foreign ministry statement, Miliband noted that the UK had already “designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) under our new state threats powers, and imposed major sanctions on those responsible for Iran’s malign activity”.

World.title: Iraq’s Minister of Electricity visits Riyadh to attend WPC Energy Congress
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Minister of Electricity, Ali Saadi Waheeb, attended the 25th WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh on Monday, where he met with key international energy authorities and discussed ways to develop Iraq’s electrical industry and promote regional collaboration.

Waheeb attended the event with Iraq’s Minister of Oil, Basim Mohammed Khudair, as Saudi Arabia welcomed ministers, industry executives, and officials from international energy corporations to discuss energy security, investment, and technological innovation.

The visit comes amid heightened security concerns after the weekend’s fatal strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport by Yemen’s Houthis.

According to Saudi police, an assault on Saturday killed at least 12 people and injured over 300, while another on Sunday killed one person and injured 11 others.

The attacks hampered airport operations as the monarchy continued its international energy meetings.

Waheeb accompanied Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman for the opening of the congress exhibition, which displayed advances in energy technology, infrastructure, and investments.

On the sidelines of the conference, the Iraqi minister met with Turkey’s Minister of Energy and Natural Resources, Alparslan Bayraktar, to discuss extending collaboration on power infrastructure.

According to Bayraktar, the two nations have agreed to speed power interconnection lines and transmission projects, as well as increase bilateral investment to boost regional energy security.

In a statement on X, the Turkish Minister said that Ankara and Baghdad planned to expand their energy relationship beyond oil and gas to include the electricity sector.

Waheeb also spoke with Algeria’s Energy Minister, Mohamed Arkab, on technological cooperation, renewable energy, and potential for developing power generation, transmission, and distribution projects.

Waheeb met separately with Jordan’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources, Saleh Ali Hamid Al-Kharabsha, to explore ways to increase bilateral energy cooperation, exchange technical skills, and improve power infrastructure.

The young Iraqi Minister also attended the 16th meeting of the Arab Council of Ministers for power in Riyadh, where officials addressed regional power integration, renewable energy, energy efficiency, and increased collaboration among Arab nations.

Waheeb stated that Iraq was looking to use foreign experience and attract investment to upgrade its energy infrastructure, extend regional power connections, and enhance electricity supply.

World.title: Federal agents search home of Trump critic Ilhan Omar: government
World.content:
Washington – US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of a criminal investigation, officials said, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump’s confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.

The search was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement, according to Fox News, citing sources familiar with the matter.

The operation, just three weeks before Omar seeks re-election in the November 3 midterms, raised concerns about longstanding Justice Department practices intended to prevent law enforcement actions from influencing elections.

The cable network reported that the operation was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.

Trump’s border enforcement chief Tom Homan told Fox News he was unwilling to give details ahead of any official announcement but confirmed that an “investigation was ongoing for a while” and that “there was a warrant executed this morning.”

US media quoted the Justice Department confirming that agents had carried out a court-authorized search in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the investigation.

The search reportedly began around 6:00 am. Video footage apparently taken by a member of the public and posted to X showed several agents wearing HSI jackets outside Omar’s Washington residence.

Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration’s sweeping crackdown on immigration.

The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.

– Rare offense –

In September, Homan said that Omar was the subject of an ongoing criminal investigation, but again declined to provide details.

Omar said at the time that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.

There was no immediate public response from Omar to Monday’s search. AFP has sought comment from her office and the Trump administration.

But Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department, criticized the timing of the search.

“There’s a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don’t take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there’s a candidate on the ballot,” she wrote on X.

Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, wrote on X that the “precedent set by this action is chilling,” warning that raids targeting political candidates shortly before elections could become more common.

Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.

She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as “The Squad,” who have been among Trump’s most vocal opponents in Congress.

No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday’s search.

Trump and his Republican allies have for years argued that non-citizens vote in significant numbers in US elections, a criminal offense punishable by imprisonment and deportation.

But studies consistently find non-citizen voting to be too rare an offense to have affected the outcome of any federal election.

An election fraud database kept by the conservative Heritage Foundation, dating back decades, contains just 1,619 cases of election-related offenses — of which non-citizen voting makes up a tiny 5.5 percent.

World.title: 'Time for PM to pack his bags and go': Congress targets Centre as food inflation hits 7.74%

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh on Tuesday launched an attack on the Narendra Modi-led government over rising prices, alleging that people are struggling to cope with the increasing cost of food and other household essentials.Ramesh pointed to the September inflation figures, arguing that the rise in food prices deserved greater attention than the headline retail inflation rate of 5.54 per cent. Food inflation stood at 7.74 per cent during the month, while retail inflation rose from 3.40 per cent in March to 5.54 per cent in September, reaching its highest level in 23 months, according to the government data cited by him.In a post on X, Ramesh wrote, âVote Theft is the Truth. Onions recorded a 108 per cent increase, while garlic prices rose 55 per cent, ginger became 63 per cent more expensive and lemons saw a 36 per cent rise.Describing the price increases as having âcrossed all limitsâ, Ramesh accused the government of overlooking the difficulties faced by households.He said the pressure was not restricted to grocery bills, with transportation, education, clothing, shoes and household goods also becoming more expensive.âThe impact of inflation isnât confined to just the dinner plate. Essentials like transportation, education, clothing, shoes, and household goods are all getting more expensive,â he said.Ramesh argued that the burden of rising prices was being felt differently across income groups, with poorer households struggling to afford food and middle-class families facing pressure on their savings. He also flagged the growing burden of debt.âThe poor are losing their daily bread from their plates, the middle class is seeing their savings vanish from their pockets, and the burden of debt keeps growing, but the Prime Minister is drowned in arrogance, paying no attention to the peopleâs troubles,â the Congress leader added.He also invoked the government's promise of âachhe dinâ to question its handling of the situation, alleging that the erosion of savings had accompanied the rise in prices.âThe government that came to power promising âgood daysâ is not only stealing votes but also robbing savings.âRamesh's criticism extended to the government's response to public anger over inflation and his allegations of vote theft. He claimed that the government had little incentive to address people's concerns if it did not fear losing their support.âWhen a vote-stealing government has no fear of the peopleâs anger or losing votes, why would it care about the public? Thatâs exactly whatâs happening now. Inflation keeps rising, public outrage over vote theft keeps growing, but the Prime Minister sits there like a silent sage. Now itâs time for him to pack his bags and go,â he said.The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has projected India's economy to expand by 7 per cent in both FY26 and FY28. Its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, however, cautioned that the global economy's resilience was becoming increasingly fragile and uneven amid rising energy and food prices and geopolitical uncertainty."The global economy remains resilient, but that resilience is becoming more fragile and more uneven," the IMF said.The Fund expects the global economy to grow by 3.1 per cent in 2026 before growth improves to 3.4 per cent in 2027.Global inflation is projected to climb to 4.7 per cent in 2026, largely on account of higher energy and food prices, before easing to 4.1 per cent in 2027.

World.title: 'Whoever thinks hoisting tricolour is violation is traitor': Abhijeet Dipke on CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's detention
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday slammed the government after

detained Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya Shinde near Jantar Mantar, questioning whether hoisting the national flag at the protest site had become a violation of the law.

Dipke's remarks came after the the CJP leaders and other protesters allegedly climbed over barricades and entered Jantar Mantar, which Delhi Police recently removed from its list of designated protest venues.

Speaking to reporters, Dipke said, "Has hoisting the national flag become a violation of the law?"

"Our team went to Jantar Mantar this morning and hoisted the tricolor. When did hoisting the tricolor become a violation? Whoever thinks that hoisting the tricolor at Jantar Mantar is a violation is a traitor.

And if Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde, and the others who were arrested for hoisting the tricolor are charged, then there should be strict action taken against it. How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolor? What kind of country is this? What kind of rule is this?" Dipke questioned.

The CJP founder said the protest would continue and urged Delhi Police to ensure that those detained could consult their lawyers.





"The whole country will become Jantar Mantar. Jantar Mantar is not just a location; it is a spirit of resistance," Dipke said.

"We hope that the Delhi Police will let them talk to their lawyers. It shouldn't happen that, as it happened to me, they are kept for 24 hours without being allowed to speak to a lawyer. As a legal procedure, they should be allowed to speak to a lawyer because you cannot just pick someone up like this," he added.

Calling the police action a "greatest example of a dictatorial mentality," Dipke accused the government of treating public spaces as its private property.

"The dictatorship doesn't want anyone to go to Jantar Mantar and hoist the tricolor. They think the whole country is their personal property. It is not like that; Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of this country, the 140 crore Indians," he said.

"We will hoist the tricolor there, and we will keep hoisting it until Jyanesh Kumar resigns," he added.

Earlier in the day, Delhi Police detained Ranka, Das and Shinde after they allegedly crossed barricades and entered Jantar Mantar. In a post on X, Dipke said the activists had been detained after entering the site with the national flag.

"Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning before they were picked up by Delhi Police. Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Ajinkya along with other team members have been detained.

You cannot denotify the resistance, @narendramodi," he wrote.

Ranka also posted a message on X saying, "Hands Off Jantar Mantar." A video shared by Ranka showed protesters climbing over barricades and entering the Jantar Mantar premises. Security personnel arrived shortly afterwards and took the protesters into custody, according to reports.

World.title: Supreme Court stays defamation case proceedings against Rahul Gandhi over 2018 remarks against PM
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) stayed criminal defamation proceedings against Congress MP Rahul Gandhi over his alleged 2019 remarks calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi “commander-in-thief” over the Rafale fighter jet deal.

A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the interim order on a petition filed by Mr. Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, challenging the Bombay High Court’s September 8 decision refusing to quash the proceedings.

“In the meantime, further proceedings before the trial court shall remain stayed,” the court ordered.

Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for Mr. Gandhi, sought a stay on the ground that the proceedings were not maintainable.

The Bench also issued notice to the Maharashtra government and the complainant, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) member Mahesh Shrishrimal, and posted the matter for hearing after four weeks.

The complaint arose from two sets of remarks allegedly made by Mr. Gandhi in September 2018. Mr. Shrishrimal objected to his use of the phrase “Hindustan ka chowkidar chor hai” at a rally in Rajasthan on September 20 and to a subsequent social media post in which he allegedly described the Prime Minister as “Commander in Thief”.

Mr. Shrishrimal alleged that the remarks imputed theft not only to Mr. Modi but also to members of the BJP and others associated with him, and sought Mr. Gandhi’s prosecution for criminal defamation under Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code.

Proceedings were initiated by a Mumbai magistrate court in 2019. Mr. Gandhi subsequently moved the Bombay High Court in November 2021, denying the allegations and seeking quashing of the proceedings.

Justice N.R. Borkar of the High Court rejected Mr. Gandhi’s contention that the BJP was not an identifiable body for the purpose of the defamation complaint.

“On a prima facie reading of the defamatory statement, inter alia describes the Prime Minister, who is also the prominent face of the said political party, as having engaged in the acts of theft, while being the Commander of Thieves. Therefore, at this threshold stage, it cannot be said that the alleged defamatory imputation is incapable of extending to those clearly identified with the party and its leadership, including its office bearers,” the High Court had held.

The High Court had also said that whether the alleged remarks affected only the Prime Minister or extended to other BJP members was a matter of evidence to be determined by the trial court.

“For the aforesaid reasons, and in the absence of any manifest illegality or perversity in the impugned order, it is not a fit case for interference in exercise of inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC. This court finds no infirmity in the impugned order,” it had said.
